the-st-james.tn: A brand stamp bearing the name "The St James."

the-virginian.tn: A brand stamp bearing the name "The Virginian."

super-bruyere.not: The number following the "England" wording is a date code: a pipe coded 13 dates to 1936, one coded 23 to 1948, and one coded 4 to 1954. More recent examples of the Parker Super Bruyere carry no date code.

rows: Made in London, England 13, PAT. No. 116989/17
Made in London, England 23, PAT. No. 116989/17
Made in London, England 4, PAT. No. 116989/17

big-ben.tn: No stamp casting or logo depiction is recorded.

laser-markings.tn: The words "Wallen / stein" in two lines on the underside, with a seashell emblem below.
laser-markings.not: These stamps are laser-engraved; records show them on examples dated 2011.

made-in-france.tn: A single dot on the stem and a letter-within-circle logo.
made-in-france.not: Records indicate the pipe was made at the FBC workshops in St Claude, which also produced Longchamp pipes; a leather-covered oval bowl and a spiral metal pin are distinctive features of this production. The bowls were leather-covered at a Paris workshop, then sent to London to be fitted with a Parker stem. The stamp is one of the examples showing the link between French pipe manufacture and London brands.

ingo-garbe.tn: A rune-shaped letter G on the underside together with the maker's name.
ingo-garbe.not: Ingo Garbe carved his first pipes in Germany in 1967, later settling in Denmark. His pipes carry only his name and a rune-shaped letter G; no grade, shape number, or date code appears. On early pipes the stamp reads "Ingo G."

heberling.not: Maker Eric Heberling began carving and selling pipes in 2011. As of 2012, the pipes are not graded.

j-ropp.tn: The name "J. Ropp" and the phrase "Maitre Pipier" on the left face.
j-ropp.not: The "J" in the stamp is the initial of Jean Ropp, of the family firm's third generation.

londonaire.tn: An anchor-shaped logo on the stem.
londonaire.not: The pipe carries no stamp other than "Londonaire." Records indicate this name belongs to a production line of Calabresi.

silver-star.tn: Logo featuring a star motif; the stamp carries the words "Silver Star" and "Brebbia."
silver-star.not: The presence of both Brebbia and Corsellini stamps on the same pipe leaves the relationship between the two makers an open question.

rows: M.P.B.s Silver Star, Brebbia Scelta Extra

sillem-s.tn: The left face carries the text "Sillem's" in a script style.
sillem-s.not: A private brand of Seiffert & Sohn GmbH. The pipes are mostly made by Savinelli. The brand name is also used on various accessories combining silver with wood, leather, or glass.

rows: On the lower left side of the ferrule

cool-sweet.tn: Logo consisting of several letters on the stem.

rows: Real Briar, Cool & Sweet, Empire Made

ogden-s.tn: Details of the logo are not recorded.
ogden-s.not: The brand was founded in 1870 by Liverpool tobacconist Thomas Ogden. It passed into Imperial Tobacco's ownership in 1902. The pipe in question is a product of the Royal Dutch Pipe Factory, part of Elbert Gubbels & Sons.

posella.tn: Stamp made up of two letters; "Posella" on the shank.
posella.not: Vitaliano Posella is the son of briar-block cutter Salvatore Posella; he began making pipes with his brother-in-law Tonino Jacono, then set up his own workshop when Jacono moved to Jesi. The workshop is in San Vito sullo Ionio, Calabria. Grades run in ascending order R (rustic), RN, SR (part-rustic), L, star(s) (smooth), F (straight grain), and Fancy; the top F and Fancy pipes also carry a "ViP" stamp.

modern-guinea-grain.tn: A text stamp bearing the name "B. Barling & Sons" together with the model name, model number, and a Danish production notice.

rows: B. Barling & Sons, Guinea Grain, 4085, Made in Denmark

masta.tn: The text "Masta" and the wording "Made in London, England" on the shank.
masta.not: Records indicate the brand was founded around 1900 and joined Parker-Hardcastle Ltd in 1967.

walat.tn: A single letter stamped within a circle on the stem.
walat.not: The brand's maker was Ludwik Walat, who died in 1980. Ryszard Filar and Ryszard Kulpiński apprenticed under him.

dunhill.tn: Single dot on the stem; stamps include a diamond, a ring, and a number enclosed in a circle.
dunhill.not: Hardcastle, Parker, and Vernon are recorded as Dunhill's secondary brands. The brand also uses its own "DR" stamp. Records indicate examples bearing the "Dunhill Paris" stamp were produced during the Second World War.

rows: Made in England 16 [1 within a circle] R/B

erica.tn: Letter E within a shield-shaped crest.

root-bruyere.tn: The text "Parker Root" set within a rhombus-shaped frame.
root-bruyere.not: The group code "4" seen within a circle on this pipe matches the group coding Dunhill used after 1952.

rows: Made in London, England, 4 (within a circle)

esterd.tn: "Aged Briar" and "Two Stars" wording alongside the "Esterd" name on the left side.
esterd.not: The same logo also appears on the Azuma brand.

harrington-park.tn: A fleur-de-lis logo; the text "Harrington Park" on the left face.
harrington-park.not: Records indicate the brand was sold by Hudson Universal Pipes. For similar logos, see Duke of Kent, Omega, Thomas; for other fleur-de-lis logos, see Ajustomatic, Cellini, Fleur de Lis, Vincenzo Lombardi.

westchester.tn: A multi-letter logo; the brand name appears on the body.

wimbledon-2.tn: A stamp consisting of the words "Wimbledon" and "Made in England" on the body.
wimbledon-2.not: Records indicate the brand was made by Comoy's or GBD.

heighstone.tn: Logo depicting a mountain; the underside carries the brand name.
heighstone.not: For other mountain-motif logos, see KB&B The Swiss.

thorpe.tn: No logo; "T. Thorpe" appears on the underside.
thorpe.not: The maker of these pipes is Timothy W. Thorpe, who made his first pipes in 2006. Grading, in ascending order, runs I and II (rustic), III and IV (sandblasted), and V (smooth).

bier.tn: No logo; the underside carries an emblem along with the letters 'I R'.

ultra-fine.tn: The letters "LHS" within a diamond and the words "Ultra Fine" on the left face.
ultra-fine.not: "Ultra Fine" was the top grade in LHS's grading scale.

club.tn: A star motif inside a shield-shaped logo.
club.not: See also the different forms of the Savinelli crests.

peterson-sterling-silver.tn: "Peterson" and "Sterling Silver" in quotation marks on the left side; Dublin hallmarks on the silver band.
peterson-sterling-silver.not: The hallmarks on the band belong to the Assay Office Dublin.

rows: Made In The Republic of Ireland, 106

trademark.tn: The words "Castello" and "Trademark" on the body, and the signature "Carlo Scotti" within an oval on the underside.

cortina.tn: Logo combining star and crown elements.
cortina.not: The same star logo also appears on Danish-made Georg Jensen and Stern pipes.

silveren-dansk.tn: The stamp carries the text "Silveren Dansk" and a shape number.

schwartz.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries "Roland" set between rhombus shapes.
schwartz.not: The maker is Roland Schwarz (b. 1953). Grading runs in ascending order 1 (rustic), 2 (sandblasted), 3, 4 ... 9, 0, and 00.

jcg.tn: The letters "JCG" inside a diamond shape.

astley-s.tn: A stamp consisting of a single letter 'A', seen in vertical, axial, and horned variants.
astley-s.not: One of London's Astley's product lines is named "Rock Briar."

rows: Astley's 109 Jermin St, London, Made in England

hercules.tn: A logo depicting a human figure.
hercules.not: The same shape 320 also appears in the "KS" size; it comes in a plain polished finish (Siena line or Erica Fiamma) and in a black sandblasted finish.

kola.tn: "Kola de Luxe, Made in France" on the left side, along with a letter logo enclosed in a circle.
kola.not: Records indicate Kola is a brand of the firm Simon Vuillard & Strauss of Saint-Claude, and it appears in a manufacturers' list dated 1910. The same maker's other brands are Captain Comfy, Vuillard, and Windsor.

rows: Kola de Luxe, Made in France

edil.tn: "Ropp" lettering in an oval on the right side of the shank, the name Edil on the left side.
edil.not: A similar logo appears on the Colossals brand.

eder-mathias.tn: A hatted man figure on the underside along with the letters M H and the wording "Mr. Hyde".
eder-mathias.not: The pipes are made by Eder Nicoletti Mathias, born in Brazil in 1977; his workshop is in Antibes, France. Besides the hatted-man mark, the pipes carry the signature "M H", "Mr Hyde", or "e m".

barok-2.tn: A single-letter logo; the underside bears the stamp 'Barok' and a country-of-origin mark.
barok-2.not: For another brand from the same workshop, see Baroque.

cosmopolitan.not: The Claridge brand's logo resembles this one.

saga.tn: The underside carries the lettered text "Saga Pipes."

northern-briar.tn: A logo formed of a ring motif.
northern-briar.not: The brand was founded in 1958. Its maker and current owner is Ian Walker, who keeps his workshop on a roughly 27-meter river boat that he relocates within England. Grading runs from bottom to top as REGAL and PREMIER.

pipes-sold-in-england.tn: An arched "Barling" wording on the left side, with "Make, Ye Olde Wood" and the model number below it.
pipes-sold-in-england.not: According to records, this stamp has been seen on a set of seven pipes that came together with their box.

rows: Barling (arched, at the top) Make, Ye Olde Wood, 1128

fairchild.tn: "Ron Fairchild" signature and year of manufacture; mark consists of one or three dots.
fairchild.not: The maker is Ron Fairchild; records indicate he produces roughly 100 pipes a year.

ryzhenko.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo data is on record.

greg-clemons.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.
greg-clemons.not: The maker is Gregory S. Clemons. The numbering gives the year and serial number together; the stamp "05-61" denotes the 61st pipe made in 2005.

kronborg.tn: A letter logo enclosed in a circle and the words "Kronborg, Castle Elsinore".
kronborg.not: Kronborg Castle is the fortification guarding the Øresund strait between Sweden and Denmark; it is referred to as Elsinore in Shakespeare's play Hamlet.

gulden-dansk.tn: A logo of two letters on the stem.

chester.not: Records indicate it is one of Reiss-Premier Co's brands.

ferrari.not: Records indicate the brand is based in Milan.

collection.tn: A logo formed from a diamond (rhombus) motif.
collection.not: The Collection line comprises the brand's upper-tier pipes; production was led by Alain Albuisson. Grading rises in the order 2, 3, and 4 stars.

rows: Hand carved real briar (within a circle) [Hand]
Hand Carved Real Briar (within a circle) [Hand]

meliora-cogito.tn: A plain round inlay on the stem.
meliora-cogito.not: The pipes were made by Massimo Angelo; records indicate they were produced for Dante pipes.

rows: by Massimo Angelo for Ser Jacopo

savinelli-giubileo-d-oro.tn: Three dots on the stem; the dots appear dark due to oxidation of the brass.
savinelli-giubileo-d-oro.not: All pipes in the Giubileo d'Oro line carry the article "LA" before the "SAVINELLI" stamp. The four-digit shape number (6003) and the star stamp are the line's distinguishing marks; the number of stars, from one to three, indicates the grade. Records indicate pipes bearing this stamp predate the 1970s.

john-aylesbury.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem.
john-aylesbury.not: The own-brand of a German wholesaler that also distributes brands such as Bentley, Peterson, and Brebbia.

sussex.tn: "Sussex" on the left side; "Made in England" within a circle on the right side.

kaywoodie-gale.tn: "Kaywoodie" on the left side together with "Gale".
kaywoodie-gale.not: The stamp dates to 1938-1942. Features identifying the period are the cap, the clover leaf above the stem, and the four-hole pin marked "Drinkless".

le-nuvole.tn: The words "Le nuvole" on the underside, with a cloud emblem beside the grade number.

rows: Le nuvole, Lavorate a Mano, In Italia

ascorti.tn: A stamp of a single letter set within a circle.
ascorti.not: The brand was founded in 1980 by Roberto Ascorti (b. 1958), son of Giuseppe (Peppino) Ascorti. As of 2007 annual production was about 1,500–2,000 pipes. See also Caminetto.

rows: Ascorti Collect T.B.I. Ascorti Hand Made Italy
Ascorti, Special Edition, Christmas 2005, For Tinder Box.

schoenleber.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.

tabago.not: The maker of the brand is Bård (Baard) Hansen, who works in Bergen, Norway; he does not put a logo on the stems of his own Tabago pipes. Pipes stamped "Tabago Handmade in Denmark" instead belong to a former Stanwell employee who produced briefly in the 1970s.

peterson-captain-pete.tn: A stamp made up of a text and two-letter forms enclosed in a circle; the name "Captain Pete" appears on the shank.
peterson-captain-pete.not: The "Made in Ireland" stamp points to the pre-Republic period; the form "Made in the Rep. of Ireland" and the abbreviated "REP." form belong to the Republic period. Captain Pete pipes were also made in Dublin.

rows: "A Peterson Product", Made in the Rep. of Ireland

the-pipe.tn: The "The pipe" stamp, made up of a single letter and a pipe symbol.

coronado.not: The same stem logo also appears on the Robert's and Union brands.

sir-scott.tn: A plant-motif logo; the brand wording appears on the left side.

arcadian.tn: Two dots and a crown-shaped logo on the stem.

rows: Arcadian, B [within a diamond], Genuine Briar 76

gigliucci.tn: A stamp on the underside reading "Gigliucci" together with letters from the early Etruscan alphabet.
gigliucci.not: The pipes are stamped with letters from the early Etruscan alphabet: R for rustic, S for sandblasted, O for smooth with a bird's-eye pattern, and F for smooth with a flame pattern. The grade is indicated by the letter repeated once, twice, or three times, rising in that order. The two-digit number gives the year of production (12 = 2012).

sir-sheldon.tn: A star-motif logo; "Sir Sheldon" on the shank.

city-gold-star.tn: Solid, gold-colored star on the stem.
city-gold-star.not: Unlike City de Luxe's hollow silver star, this brand's logo is a solid gold-colored star. One of GBD's second-line brands, produced at the brand's facilities in France.

savinelli-fat-boy.tn: Stamp bearing the lettering "Denby's Fat Boy" on the left side.

hiro.tn: No separate logo; the text "HiRo" on the underside.
hiro.not: The pipes are made by a maker named Hiroyuki, born in 1958, working on the island of Hokkaido. Not to be confused with Hiroyuki Tokutomi.

camelia.tn: The word Camelia within an oval on the left face; a diamond-shaped element in the stamp.

kaywoodie-filtronic.not: The Filtronic series was produced from 1971 to 1975.

sir-oward.tn: Logo in the form of a plain round dot.

kaywoodie-mandarin.tn: The text "Kaywoodie Mandarin" on the shank.
kaywoodie-mandarin.not: The Mandarin line was produced from 1958 to 1967.

peterson-captain-peterson.tn: A stamp made up of a single letter enclosed in a circle; the name "Captain Peterson" is written on the shank.
peterson-captain-peterson.not: The brand of Peterson's English branch. This English-made example is dated before 1960.

rows: "Captain Peterson" C, A Peterson Product, Made in England, 21

dorset.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle; the stamp carries the name "Dorset".
dorset.not: A yellow version of the same logo also appears on the Hamilton brand.

super-russet.not: The 4 within the circle matches the group code Dunhill used to indicate bowl size.

rows: Made in London, England 4 (within a circle)

clairmont.tn: Single blue dot on the stem.
clairmont.not: The brand was founded in the 1970s by Alberto Paronelli; the pipes were generally made by Tom Spanu. "Clairmont" is the Frenchified form of Chiaramonti, Spanu's birthplace. See also Casteldoria and Castelsardo.

jopp.tn: The word "JOPP" enclosed in an oval, with four diamond shapes below.

le-roi.tn: A single letter-L inlay on the stem.
le-roi.not: The grading format (**A) and the letter L on the stem are largely identical to those seen on A. Lacroix pipes.

mastro-de-paja.tn: A plain or ornate round inlay on the stem; the text "Mastro de Paja" on the shank.
mastro-de-paja.not: The brand was founded in 1972 by Giancarlo Guidi, who left in 1982 to join Ser Jacopo; in 1995 the brand passed to Alberto Montini. A sun emblem is used for grading; second-quality names are Calibano and Montini. Mario Lubinski handled the brand's distribution from 1972 to 1980.

rows: Mastro de Paja, For. W. Lubinski, Fatta a mano, brev. 331218172, 1 [within a circle]
Mastro De Paja, Fatta a mano, [Grade: single sun], 1978, 1 [within a circle], C [within a circle]

stem-logo.tn: "Missouri Meerschaum" within a circle on the underside, with a clover-motif stamp on the stem.
stem-logo.not: The stamp on the stem combines the clover motif with an "&" symbol.

simmons.tn: Logo featuring a single letter and a human figure; the stamp carries the text "H. Simmons."

peterson.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo description is recorded.

sara-eltang.tn: The underside carries a footprint figure alongside the text "Sara Eltang."
sara-eltang.not: A sub-brand tied to Tom Eltang, named after Tom and Pia Eltang's daughter. It is said that Sara always helped her father in the workshop barefoot.

heatherby.tn: The letters "KB & B" set inside a large clover outline.
heatherby.not: Records date this stamp to 1919-1924. These pipes used an inner tube similar to that of Dunhills of the period; examples with the blue clover logo are contemporary with early Kaywoodie pipes.

rows: KB & B [within a large clover outline]

keyer-s.tn: A single-letter stamp; the word "Keyer's" appears on the shank.
keyer-s.not: Records suggest Keyer's may be a private label used for Savinelli-made pipes. Savinelli's shape codes beginning with 5xx denote a square shank; the 505 code here falls within that series.

comoy-s-london-pride.tn: On the right side, the "England" text within a circle.

stern.tn: A star-motif stamp; "Stern" on the underside.
stern.not: The same star logo also appears on Danish pipes bearing the Georg Jensen and Cortina brands.

p-mercier.tn: A two-letter initial stamp of the brand name.

blackwood.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem; the word 'Blackwood' on the top face.

ronaldo.tn: A round stone inlaid on the stem.

cavicchi.tn: A round wooden inlaid mark on the stem.
cavicchi.not: Maker Claudio Cavicchi; as of 2006, output was roughly 1000 pipes a year. Grading rises in the order 1© through 5©, with the smooth-grain "Diamante" at the top.

james-t-cooke.tn: A round logo with a yin-yang pattern on the stem.
james-t-cooke.not: In the brand's early period a musical-note-shaped logo was used. The serial number consists of the year plus a sequence number; the stamp 87-39 denotes the 39th pipe made in 1987.

rows: Hand Made by, J.T. & D., Cooke, USA, Vermont

macarthur.tn: On the underside of a corncob shank, a maker's text within a circle.
macarthur.not: Known as the "Mac" shape, this form was produced based on the pipe model General Douglas MacArthur (1880-1964) commissioned from the Missouri Meerschaum company.

rows: Missouri Meerschaum Washington. Mo. (within a circle)

missouri-meerschaum-2.tn: On the underside, within a circle, the wording "Missouri Meerschaum Washington M° U.S.A." together with registration and trademark notices.
missouri-meerschaum-2.not: On early examples, the shank was made from corn cob rather than cedar. The bowl was not stained; instead, a soft piece of wood was pressed against the spinning bowl, producing a dark burnished finish through friction. This method was no longer in use as of 2012.

rows: Missouri Meerschaum Washington M° U.S.A. [within a circle]

mortensen.not: The emblem represents Mjölnir, the hammer of Thor, the Norse god of thunder.

sir-charles.tn: Logo consisting of two letters; the left face carries the text "Sir Charles of London."

royal-falcon.tn: Logo featuring a bird figure in the shape of a falcon.
royal-falcon.not: Related to the Falcon brand under Comoy's; see Falcon (Comoy).

comoy-s-royal.tn: A three-piece inlaid letter "C" on the stem (two black, one white).
comoy-s-royal.not: Stamping the series name above the word "Comoy" is an uncommon practice for this brand. The three-piece inlay method was discontinued in the early 1980s.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England

the-mansion-house.tn: "The Mansion House" alongside a three-bar motif.
the-mansion-house.not: The same three-bar logo also appears on the Everyman, Guildhall, and The Lumberman stamps.

baudis.tn: No logo depiction or stamp casting is recorded.

bent-bob-s.tn: A logo consisting of several bars in a motif.
bent-bob-s.not: The same logo also appears on Savinelli's Royal Oak brand.

tilt.tn: A single-letter logo; the word "Tilt" on the body.

savinelli-dry-system.tn: Single letter and the words "Dry System" within a shield-shaped field.
savinelli-dry-system.not: The Dry System line departs from Savinelli's usual three-digit shape code and may be stamped with a three- or four-digit code. For this reason, a Dry System pipe carrying a four-digit code is not on its own considered an early example. For the same logo, see Savinelli Siena.

castelsardo.not: Pipes carved by Tom Spanu. The brand name follows the naming sequence drawn from places in Spanu's life.

corrado.tn: Two dots side by side on the stem.
corrado.not: Records indicate roughly 50 freehand pipes were produced per year.

man-about-town.not: For other brands using a hat-shaped logo, see Lobbia, London Royal, Churchill, and Sabatini.

zhan.tn: No emblem on the stem; the inscription "P. ZHAN" set between lines on the underside.
zhan.not: The maker is Ping Zhan, born in 1979. A photographer and software engineer, Zhan began making pipes in 2011.

albuisson.tn: No mark on the stem; the stamp consists of the wording on the shank faces.

bb-s.tn: A multi-letter 'BB&S' stamp used together with a crown emblem.
bb-s.not: The abbreviation BB&S stands for Benjamin Barling and Sons. See also the Londoner, Cragmoor, and Portland records for related stamps.

rows: PORTLAND PIPE CO., B.B.& S London Made England, Dearborn

curt-rollar.not: The four-digit number in the stamp gives the month and year; 0183 means January 1983, and the letters CR are Curt Rollar's initials. Mark Tinsky and Curt Rollar founded The American Smoking Pipe Co. in 1978; Rollar left the company in 1990.

prototype.tn: Double logo on the stem combining a jeweled logo with a white bar logo.
prototype.not: The example pipe was carved in 1999.

rows: 00.24 Castello, Made in Cantu, Italy, Reg N° ...

andrew-marks.tn: A round wooden inlay on the stem.
andrew-marks.not: The maker is Andrew Marks, who has been carving pipes since 1969.

lorenz-2.tn: A single dot on the stem.
lorenz-2.not: Master Ludwig Lorenz (b. 1963) is the son of Karl Lorenz, himself a pipe maker; annual output is around 300 pipes. Grades run from low to high: D, C, B, A, and AA. The example pipe has a diamond set into the 18-karat gold band.

ranger.tn: Letter emblem inside a circle on the stem; cursive "Big-Ben" and "Ranger" on the shank.
ranger.not: This emblem was mostly used on short-shanked (nosewarmer) models and is the same as the one used on the "Straight Grain" series.

calich.tn: A single dot or three dots on the stem.

rattray-s.tn: Shield-shaped logo; "Rattray's" on the left side.
rattray-s.not: Named after the Scottish tobacconist, this brand is used on pipes imported by Otto & Kopp GmbH. The pipes were first made by Jørn Larsen, and since at least 2004 by Butz Choquin. The Rattray's tobacco shop is in Perth, Scotland.

bontemps.tn: A stamp made up of chevron and arrow motifs; the words "Bontemps Saint-Claude" on the underside.
bontemps.not: One of the brands of the Berrod-Regad group, based in Saint-Claude. Records also mention a Bontemps adaptation of Peterson's P-Lip stem.

enrico-bocci.tn: Monogram-style logo made of two letters.
enrico-bocci.not: The pipes were made by craftsman Enrico Bocci; records indicate production ceased in the 1980s.

scotland-yard.tn: Brand mark consisting of a single letter.

rows: Scotland yard, Made in London (within a circle) England

grand-master.tn: A two-letter logo together with "Grand Master" and "Twin Bore" on the shank.
grand-master.not: Other brands using the twin-bore stem arrangement include Beau Nash, Leonard's, Kaywoodie Allbriar, Durobit, Radice, Siam, and Twin Bore. This information is based on Wilczak and Colwell's study.

frasorteret.tn: No separate logo; "Frasorteret" lettering stamped on the underside instead.

sven-lar.tn: "SVEN LAR" on the underside along with the handwritten signature "M. Kabik."
sven-lar.not: The brand belongs to Michael Kabik, who left the trade in the late 1980s. These pipes were made after the maker ended his CHP-X production.

v-beast.tn: The words "V. Beast" on the underside.
v-beast.not: The brand's maker is Valera Rijenko (also spelled Valery Ryzhenko), born in 1964. A self-taught maker, he started with pear-wood pipes in 2002 and moved entirely to briar in 2003.

sasieni-blue-bar.tn: A blue bar-shaped stamp on the stem.
sasieni-blue-bar.not: Records indicate this rarely seen Sasieni stamp is hard to date; it is placed between the mid- and late 1920s, a transitional mark between the single-dot and four-dot stamps.

tom-spanu.tn: A single dot on the stem (green in the earlier logo, blue in the later one) and a solid-ring mark.
tom-spanu.not: The names Clairmont, Casteldoria, and Castelsardo derive from places in Tom Spanu's life and are used in the brand's naming.

rows: Tom Spanu, Clairmont [old logo, green dot]

late-2000s-pipe.tn: The words "Wallenstein" and "German Handmade" on the left side, with a scallop-shell emblem on the shank.
late-2000s-pipe.not: The stamp belongs to a pipe dated 2006; the scallop-shell emblem is the brand's grade indicator.

hand-made.tn: A crowned-snake figure and a diamond-shaped motif on the stem.
hand-made.not: The crowned-snake logo on the stem shows small variations in detail from example to example; a similar one also appears on the Rock Grain model.

willmer.tn: A single-letter logo; "Willmer" and "Made in England" stamps on the body.
willmer.not: The name Bentley in the stamp denotes Willmer's own product line. It should not be confused with the Danish Bentley brand or with the US-based Bentley thought to be Kaywoodie's secondary brand.

rows: Willmer, Made in England, Hand Made
Willmer, Straight Grain, A A A A, PRESENTATION

danish-sovereign.tn: Multi-letter script-style logo; underside stamp reading "danish sovereign, Made in Denmark".
danish-sovereign.not: One of Stanwell's second-line brands, offered only to the US and Canadian markets. Production took place at Stanwell's workshops in Borup.

bartlett-bickley.tn: A single red dot on the stem.
bartlett-bickley.not: The stamp carries the mark 'BARBIC', the number 459, and the firm's Piccadilly, London address.

hasso.tn: No separate logo; the underside bears the text "Hasso" and the letter "H" is stamped.
hasso.not: Maker Hasso Baudis was born in 1955 and made pipes from 1978 to 1983. Records indicate he made about 1000-1100 pipes in that period, afterward working as an architect.

reichert.tn: No separate logo; "Handmade, A. Reichert, Germany" inside an oval on the underside.
reichert.not: Maker Axel Reichert has made pipes since 1998. Pipes are not graded or dated.

rows: Handmade, A. Reichert, Germany (within an oval)

pimpernel.tn: A single blue or red dot on the stem.

axmacher.tn: The wording "F. Axmacher, Germany" within a circle.
axmacher.not: The maker Frank Axmacher was born in 1963. On stamps up to 2008 the letters "AX" are set between the two horizontal strokes of an "F", with the grade and date stamped below the strokes; in that period's two-letter grading, the first letter denoted rising quality from F to A, and the second the maker's own assessment. On the current circular stamp the date appears within the circle (11 = 2011), and the grade rises in the order C, B, A, and AA for exceptional pipes.

savinelli-molinella.tn: On the left side, "Molinella" above and "Savinelli" below; on the right side, a shield emblem together with the model number and country information.
savinelli-molinella.not: Model number 623 is also used in the Gold and Sherwood series. A similar logo appears on the Oldenkott brand.

joao-reis.tn: The words "João Reis" on the underside.
joao-reis.not: Maker João Reis, born in Portugal in 1978, has lived and worked in Denmark since 2004. According to 2009 records, his annual output is about 150 pipes. The brand has no dating or grading system.

peter-heinrichs.tn: Logo combining a human figure with a pipe motif and a single letter; "Peter Heinrichs" on the shank.

pipe-de-roi.not: Records attribute the brand to the André Bourgeois workshop in Saint Claude.

lobnik.tn: On the underside, the text 'Lobnik' together with three stars and a lightning-bolt mark; there is no separate logo stamp.

taylor-made.tn: A round wood-colored inlay on the stem.
taylor-made.not: The mark Bill Ashton-Taylor (1945-2009) used after leaving Dunhill and before founding the Ashton brand.

kaywoodie-filter-pipe.tn: A stamp on the underside reading "Kaywoodie" and "Filter Pipe".
kaywoodie-filter-pipe.not: This stamp was used from 1961 to 1968. To separate the bowl from the shank, the stem is turned half a turn to release the retaining pin, then pulled from the shank.

titanus.tn: No recorded stamp breakdown or logo description available.

tomy.tn: The brand name within a diamond-shaped frame, along with a single-dot mark.

ed-sheffield.tn: Round, wood-colored mark on the stem.

chelsea.tn: "Chelsea" and "Natural" on the left face; on the right face, an emblem between "1933" and "Chicago".

radice.tn: Two dots side by side or a decorated round emblem on the stem; "Radice" on the shank.
radice.not: On twin-bore models, two airways are drilled through the stem, marked by two dots set crosswise on it; similar twin-bore examples are Grand Master, Kaywoodie Durobit, and Leonard's. Filter-compatible models were made for the German market. Records indicate some pipes carry a rare moon-and-sun emblem on the stem.

rows: Radice, Dark, Hand made in Italy

helio-ferretti.tn: Two-letter logo; the shank carries the "Helio Ferretti" name.
helio-ferretti.not: The brand belongs to the gift shop Febac S.A., recorded at an address near Hospitalet de Llobregat, close to Barcelona. The pipes were manufactured by Ibérica de Pipas.

lowell.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

savinelli-sila.tn: Logo on the stem featuring a star motif; the left face carries the text "Sila."
savinelli-sila.not: The same stem logo is also used on Savinelli's Antique Shell, Garda, and Oscar lines.

royalton.tn: Logo made up of a single letter.
royalton.not: The example in the records is the Royalton Crown model.

artigiana.tn: A script stamp with the brand name and country on the left face and the series name on the right face.

reviagin.tn: Two dots on the stem; "M. REVIAGIN." on the underside.
reviagin.not: Records indicate the two dots on the stem were discontinued after 2006. The maker's faceted "Bee"-shaped pipes have a second cooling chamber set into the shank.

mac-baren.tn: A shield-shaped coat-of-arms logo on the stem.
mac-baren.not: Mac Baren is a Danish tobacco brand; the logo on the stem is the same coat of arms used on its tobacco tins and pouches. In the source, tobacco-brand-derived pipes are mentioned alongside Clan, Borkum Riff, and Prince Albert (see).

hynick.tn: No separate logo stamp; the maker's name appears on the right face.
hynick.not: A handmade brand. Tim Hynick has been carving pipes since 2003; his pipes carry no grade or date stamp, only a signature.

bmf.tn: The letters BMF enclosed in an oval.
bmf.not: The stamps mention Saint-Claude, France's pipemaking center. Leather-covered examples are also on record.

rows: Bruyère Garantie, BMF (within an oval), Saint Claude
Super, BMF (within an oval) Bruyere Extra

universale.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

underboar.tn: The word "UNDERBOAR" and a registration number on the left face.
underboar.not: The Underboar line was produced from the 1920s until the Second World War. Charatan marketed this line with the slogan "the self-cleaning pipe," referring to the mechanism built into the pipes.

manz.tn: No separate logo is used; the underside is stamped with the maker's name plus a grade and date code.
manz.not: Born in 1968, Cornelius Mänz was a textile designer before he began carving pipes in 2001, producing 60-70 pipes a year by 2004. Until June 2003 the stamp read "C. Mänz handgemacht" in a straight line; from July 2003 it took the form of a rugby ball reading "C. Mänz Germany." The number in the stamp gives the month and year of production (403 = April 2003). Grades run in ascending order CD, C, BC, B, AB, A, and the very rare "best."

dr-geo.tn: "Dr Geo" brand-name lettering on the shank.
dr-geo.not: The brand of the Gichard & Cie firm, active in Saint-Claude; production has ended.

rows: Pipe Dr Geo Déposée, Algerian Briar Made in France

wings.tn: A diamond-shaped logo; the letters "NBP" within a crest.

ma-colombe.tn: A bird motif in the shape of a dove.
ma-colombe.not: The pipes were made by Jean Masson, born in 1934, whose workshop is in Villard-Saint-Sauveur near Saint-Claude. Output reached roughly 250 carved and 1,000 classic pipes a year, slowing after 2009. Masson is the inventor of the patented "Anti-jus" (anti-buildup) system.

a-lacroix.tn: Single-letter stamp used together with star motifs.
a-lacroix.not: Grading is done by number of stars, rising from two stars to five stars. Records indicate the letter following the stars denotes a further sub-ranking within the same star grade. The brand's second line is named Le Roi.

jrgen-larsen.not: Annual output is about 100 pipes. See also Peter Stokkebye and Jesper of Denmark.

todorov.tn: No recorded stamp breakdown or logo description available.

brandt.tn: No stamp data is on record.

dobi-s.tn: Logo based on a single-letter element.
dobi-s.not: Dobi's pipes were marketed by the retailer Cremonesi in Vaprio d'Adda, in the province of Milan. Records indicate the pipes were manufactured by Rossi.

altadis.tn: A logo spelling out the brand name 'Altadis.'
altadis.not: Altadis is a multinational group active in the tobacco industry; records note it was considered the sector's largest multinational group in 2004.

marcee.tn: The letters M R C within a shield; beside them, the words 'Marcee' and 'De Luxe.'
marcee.not: The stamp is linked to the Maréchal Ruchon & Co factory; records indicate an English-French manufacturing connection behind the brand.

rows: Marcee, M R C (within a shield), De Luxe

ilsted.tn: A text-only stamp with no separate logo, bearing the maker's name on the underside along with "Handcut" and "Made in Denmark".
ilsted.not: Grading combines one letter with one number (for example, F 3). Letters rise from A to J, numbers from 1 to 4. Whether a stamp in the form "2 B" carries the same meaning as "B 2" is unknown.

rows: Poul, Ilsted, Handcut, Made in Denmark, (grading?)

brughiera.tn: A single silver-colored dot on the stem.

todd-johnson.tn: A plain round single dot on the stem; the maker's name in the stamp alongside the Greek inscription ΣΤΩΑ.
todd-johnson.not: The early grading scale consists of the Spartan, Athenian, and Alexandrian grades. The hoplite helmet mark in the stamp denotes pipes of exceptional quality.

rows: Todd Johnson [curved within an oval] ΣΤΩΑ (STOA)
Todd M Johnson [curved within an oval] ΣΤΩΑ (STOA)

henley-club.tn: Two-letter logo; the shank carries the "Henley Club" name.
henley-club.not: Records indicate the pipes were produced around 1940.

rows: Henley Club, London Made, Made in England, 911

thuner.tn: No logo; the letters "R T" appear on the underside.
thuner.not: The stamps carry no grading or dating information.

phitu.tn: "Hardcastle's" and "PHITU" on the left side, registered design number on the right side.
phitu.not: Hardcastle's design corresponding to Yello-Bole's "Chinrester" model.

kaywoodie-durobit.tn: "Kaywoodie" and "Durobit ©" stamp on the left side.
kaywoodie-durobit.not: The Durobit stamp was used between 1966 and 1972. The double-holed stem is more durable for smokers who have a habit of biting the mouthpiece. The model is a variant of the 1955 Stembiter without the notch on top of the stem.

town-hall.tn: A single-bar inlay on the stem; the words "Town Hall" on the body.
town-hall.not: This is one of Comoy's second brands bearing the single-bar stem logo. Other names in the same group are Carlyle, Charles Cross, St James, The Golden Arrow, and Trident.

max-brandt.tn: A logo formed of a ring-shaped motif.
max-brandt.not: Max Brandt, known as "Olive," is the son of Oliver Brandt and stamps his pipes with the letters "MB." The "Brandy" series is a joint production. Grading on MB and Olive pipes runs, smallest to largest, AA, EX1 through EX12, Artline, and the rare Rune; Brandy pipes are numbered 1 through 12.

collection-2.tn: A Castello Collection record with no separate stamp casting on file.
collection-2.not: The pipe in this record is stamped as number 12 of a series of 250.

purex-superfine.tn: A single-line decoration on the stem; letters "LHS" inside a diamond and "PUREX Superfine" on the left side.

rows: LHS (within a diamond) PUREX, Superfine, Imported Briar, 12

kaywoodie-flame-grain-meerschaum.tn: A stamp on the left side reading "Kaywoodie" and "Flame Grain Meerschaum", with the shape number on the right side.
kaywoodie-flame-grain-meerschaum.not: A briar pipe with a removable meerschaum bowl liner; its period is 1947-1955. Pipes of the Flame Grain grade with a meerschaum-inlaid bowl appear in Kaywoodie's 1947 catalog. The inlay was originally made of solid Turkish meerschaum.

peterson-peterson-1899.tn: "Peterson" on the shank with the word "Patent" and a grade number.
peterson-peterson-1899.not: The silver hallmarks indicate the year 1899 and belong to the Dublin Assay Office. The number 2 following the word "Patent" indicates the second-highest of the grades offered; this pipe, from the patent era, has no fills.

bewlay.tn: A single-letter logo; the stamps read 'Bewlay.'
bewlay.not: The brand was distributed by the Bewlay & Co pipe shop chain until the 1950s, after which it was taken over by Imperial Tobacco & Co.

golden-sunset.tn: A stamp on the shank reading "Golden Sunset" along with wood type and country of origin.

sethile.tn: The underside carries the text "SEThile" along with date, production-sequence, and grade codes.
sethile.not: The maker, Scott E. Thile, is a piano tuner and musician who began carving pipes in 2006. Until August 2012 he used an ascending grade scale of D, C, B, and A, after which grading was discontinued. The two-digit number in the stamp gives the year of production (07 = 2007), and the number following it gives the production sequence; in 2013 the Etude (ET), Opus (OP), and Freehand (FH) lines were introduced.

vauen.tn: A plain single white dot on the stem; the words "Vauen Luxus" on the left face.
vauen.not: Records indicate this model's design belongs to Barontini. Vauen's Dr. Perl variant follows the same arrangement as Peterson's P-Lip stem.

ena.tn: Letter enclosed in a circle within a diamond-shaped field.
ena.not: The ENA stamp belongs to the Emilio Navarro SL factory.

camy.tn: The Camy stamp rendered in the brand's own script on the shank.

harlekin.tn: A logo combining a mammal and a pipe figure; the text "Harlekin" on the top face.
harlekin.not: One of the brands of Skandinaviska Pipfabriken. For the same maker's other brands, see Bromma and Dollar.

fischer-2.tn: A stamp formed of a single letter.
fischer-2.not: The maker is Peter Fischer, born 1949. Records indicate an annual output of about 150 pipes.

peterson-circle-briar-inlay-logo.tn: Circular briar inlay on the stem.
peterson-circle-briar-inlay-logo.not: The marks on the silver ferrule date the pipe to 1985.

rows: Made in the Republic of Ireland

armellini.tn: A plain round dot on the stem, plus a stamp with a single letter and ring motif.
armellini.not: Records indicate the "m" letter on the stem is a precursor to the round dot used later, and it also appears on the Mauro sub-brand. After the death of Mauro Armellini (1936–2004), the brand was carried on by his daughter Vilma Armellini. Its second-grade brands are Mauro and Converti.

legion-of-honor.tn: The words "Legion of Honor" on the left side.
legion-of-honor.not: A sub-brand used by Mastercraft for pipes it imported from France.

magnet.not: On this line's pipes the stem is attached to the bowl by a magnetic connection.

ermanno.tn: Single letter within a shield-shaped crest.
ermanno.not: The same logo is also used on the Erica brand.

classic.tn: Target-like motif of concentric rings on the stem; "Ropp" written inside an oval on the stamp.

sterling-hall.tn: A letter B within a diamond shape, flanked by diamond marks on either side.
sterling-hall.not: Records link it to the Calvalcade, Smokemaster, L.L. Bean, and Hallmark brands.

rows: ◊ [B within a diamond] Sterlin Hall By Briarcraft ◊

wild-honey.tn: A two-letter logo; the stamps read "Wild Honey" and "Made in England."
wild-honey.not: The brand belongs to the Wild Honey Tobacco Co.

ken-erickson.tn: A round wood inlay on the stem.

suez.tn: The letters KB & B set within a clover shape.
suez.not: This pipe is recorded as dating to the 1930s.

rows: Suez, KB & B (within a clover), Italian Briar

savinelli-autograph.tn: The maker's handwritten signature on the right face, with the stamp "Savinelli Autograph" on the left face.
savinelli-autograph.not: Autograph pipes are handmade and each one is unique. Grading rises in the order 3, 4, … 8, 0, 00, 000.

almanac.tn: A logo consisting of a pipe depiction.
almanac.not: For a similar logo, see H.T.L.

red-star.tn: Star-shaped logo; "Red Star" on the shank.

marwyn.tn: The letters LHS within a diamond-shaped frame; on the left side, the text 'Marwyn.'

purex.tn: Letters "LHS" inside a diamond, with "Purex" and "All Briar" beside them.
purex.not: This model's stem is also made of briar. Similar examples with briar stems are Barnaby, Il Ceppo, and Kaywoodie Allbriar; Salvatella uses a different wood.

rows: LHS (within a diamond), Purex, All Briar

royal-ascot.tn: Stamp featuring a crown motif; some examples use a horseshoe-shaped logo instead.
royal-ascot.not: The same crown logo also appears on Corsican Briar. Records indicate pipes under this brand were made in France for Duncan and sold in the US market through Mastercraft; the horseshoe-logo examples are thought to be of English rather than French origin.

peterson-mark-twain.tn: On the left side, the text 'Peterson's' and 'Mark Twain.'
peterson-mark-twain.not: The series was issued for the writer's 150th birthday; the numbered second edition is limited to 1,000 pipes. Peterson produced unnumbered Mark Twain pipes between 1983 and 1989; since the band stamp on this example reads 1981, a dating contradiction arises.

rows: Made in The Republic, of Ireland

luigi.tn: The brand stamp "Luigi" spelled out in letters on the left side of the shank.

paul-olsen.tn: "Paul Olsen" wording used together with a crown emblem.
paul-olsen.not: Paul Olsen is the name of a Danish tobacconist chain that was first owned by the Olsen family and later passed to the Orlik Tobacco Company. Most pipes sold under this name were made by Poul Winsløw.

empire-state.tn: Letter enclosed in a circle within a triangular field.
empire-state.not: The same logo also appears on the Regis brand; see Regis.

lion-s-head.tn: The "Made in England" text within a circle beside the "Lions Head" stamp.

rows: Lions Head, Made in England (within a circle), 220

dorchester.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle.

perla-nera.tn: "Perla Nera" and "Castello" on the underside, with the name Carlo Scotti inside an oval, in signature style.
perla-nera.not: The series name given to Castello's plain black polished pipes. The stamp indicates a place of manufacture of Cantù, Italy.

rows: Perla Nera Made in Cantu Italy
Carlo Scotti (within an oval), Carlo Scotti (signature)

wolf.tn: A logo consisting of a ring motif; the stamp "Wolf London HHW" on the left face.
wolf.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, although the shank carries an English-origin stamp, the brand belongs to the US-based Wolf Pipe Co.

florov.tn: A stamp on the underside with the maker's name and, at the top grade, an elephant figure.
florov.not: Maker Alex Florov was born in Moscow and emigrated to the U.S. in 1992. Grading rises from C, to B, to A; the top grade, marked with an elephant figure, is Slonim.

thayne.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.

shekita.tn: No logo on the stem; the underside carries the "Shekita" stamp and a production number.
shekita.not: The maker, Konstantin Shekita, was born in 1967; he made his first pipe at the "Golden Gate" factory in Kiev. Starting in 2007 he began attending international pipe shows, and records from 2011 indicate he produced roughly 200 pipes a year. The first two digits of the number give the production year (10 = 2010), with the remaining digits giving that year's production sequence.

dunbar.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; "Dunbar" lettering on the left face.

rows: Made in London [within a circle] England

svendborg.tn: "Svendborg" on the shank and a single-letter "C" stamp.
svendborg.not: The name Jan Hansen that appears in the stamps is a pseudonym used by Henrik Jørgensen. Records indicate the maker chose this name because he felt his own initials (HJ) could be misread.

kings-cross.tn: A single-letter stamp used together with an inverted-V (chevron) motif and parallel bars.
kings-cross.not: See also the Kings Cross brand and Marxman's Kings Cross series.

geiger-carlson.tn: No logo on the stem; the underside reads "Geiger & Carlson".
geiger-carlson.not: The brand arose from the collaboration of Love Geiger and Bengt Carlson.

amiel.tn: A two-letter logo; the stamp reads 'Amiel.'
amiel.not: The brand was founded in 1923 by Raoul Amiel in Philippeville (present-day Skikda), Algeria. The factory employed about thirty people when it closed in the early 1960s. Raoul's son Bernard Amiel (d. 2008) ran GBA Synergie, which bought Ropp in 1988 and held the brand until 1991.

filar.tn: A round wooden inlay on the stem; a letter enclosed in a circle in the stamp.
filar.not: The pipes' maker is Ryszard Filar. Ryszard Filar and Ryszard Kulpinski worked together from 1981 to 1983, and Bartolomjiej Antoniewski joined the same workshop in 1985-1986.

jean-claude.not: Records suggest the brand may be a sub-brand of Molina.

shelton-square.tn: Logo consisting of an arrow motif; the stamp carries the text "Shelton Square" set within a rhombus.
shelton-square.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell, this is a French brand whose maker is unknown. The same logo also appears on The Mayflower and Rustique brands.

captain-warren.tn: A single-letter stamp; the text "Captain Warren" appears on the left face.
captain-warren.not: Captain Warren pipes are made either by Ser Jacopo or Savinelli; it is not always possible to distinguish which workshop a given example came from. See also Savinelli's Capt Warren series.

savenko.tn: The underside carries "SAVA" set between two lines.
savenko.not: Maker Andrey Savenko began carving pipes in 2009. His pipes carry no stamp other than "SAVA."

kaywoodie-calabash.tn: A Kaywoodie calabash model carrying no stamp.
kaywoodie-calabash.not: This Kaywoodie calabash production dates to 1938-1968.

dr-plumb.tn: Single red dot and "Dr Plumb" brand-name lettering.
dr-plumb.not: The brand was founded in Saint-Claude in 1925. Production was carried out at the Ruchon & Verguet and Ropp factories, also in Saint-Claude. The brand now belongs to the British Cadogan group.

ser-jacopo.tn: A single gray, red, or coral-colored dot on the stem; on higher-tier lines, a precious-stone inlay set in a gold bezel.
ser-jacopo.not: The gray dot is the brand's first mark, used on the stems of its entry-level pipes. The coral dot (Corallium rubrum) is an older logo discontinued in the 1980s; a variant set within a silver ring also exists. The "Dalla Gemma" line uses five stones set in 18-karat gold bezels: emerald, spinel, sapphire, ruby, and diamond.

rows: Ser Jacopo, Fatta a Mano, PICTA, Per Aspera ad Astra
Ser Jacopo, Fatta a Mano, in Italia
◊ Ser Jacopo, dalla Gemma, Fatta a Mano, Giancarlo Guidi, … Per Aspera ad Astra … Fiammata ZAFFIRO ◊
Ser Jacopo, dalla Gemma, Fatta a Mano
Ser Jacopo, dalla Gemma, Fatta a Mano In Italia

patent.tn: A single-letter stamp; the shank reads "Frank", "Medico", and "Real Briar".

double-dri.tn: Logo based on a two-letter element; the stamp carries the lettering "Medico Double-Dri".

kai-nielsen.tn: A single-dot mark on the stem.

rows: V V V V Old Briar Straight Grain (pipe made for the US market)
A , Kai Nielsen, Hand Made in Denmark, Old Briar (pipe made for the European market)

wessex.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter and a solid ring.

cliper.tn: A plain, single-color round inlay on the stem.
cliper.not: The brand was made by Ibérica de Pipas.

amphora.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle; the stamp reads 'Amphora.'
amphora.not: A brand of Elbert Gubbels & Sons - Royal Dutch Pipe Factory, which went bankrupt in March 2012. Some examples have an air-adjustment mechanism at the shank-stem joint. For the same maker's other brands, see Big-Ben, Humbry, IRC, Roermond, Royal Dutch, Thompson, and Porsche Design.

thompson.tn: A single-letter logo; "Thompson" on the shank.
thompson.not: See also the Barbados line of the Big Ben brand.

s-g.tn: The letters "S & G" set within an oval.
s-g.not: The number 9436 on the right face matches GBD's shape number for a straight billiard. Taken together with the "London England" inscription above the number, records indicate the pipe was made by GBD and sold by Salmon & Gluckstein Ltd.

micoli.tn: On the underside, the text 'Micoli' set between two dashes.
micoli.not: Records indicate the brand's pipes show rustic and carved surface finishes; the carved motif is also carried onto the double-bend stem.

alfred.tn: A mark on the stem consisting of a letter surmounted by a crown.

bosi.tn: A single blue dot on the stem; plain and ornamented round inlay forms are also used.
bosi.not: The brand of the American master Kirk D. Bosi, who has carved pipes since 1999.

peterson-pre-republic-era.tn: Period stamp with "Peterson's" and "Dublin" on the left side, and a "K&P" mark on the ferrule.
peterson-pre-republic-era.not: No stamp appears on the stem in this period's examples. None of "Ireland", "Eire", or "Irish Free State" appears on the shank; dating relies on this absence.

don-carlos.tn: "Don Carlos" lettering used together with a bar motif.
don-carlos.not: The brand belongs to craftsman Bruto Sordini; today's logo has been used since 2000. Pipes are divided into three grades — rustic, smooth, and straight grain — and rated within each grade with one to three musical notes; the very top examples carry the "Chorale" stamp. Dating has used a numeric stamp since 2002: in 2002, "50/2" gave the craftsman's age together with his years in pipemaking; from 2004 onward, a single number increasing each year was used; no stamp was used in 2003.

rows: Don Carlos, Fatta a mano, in Italia [two musical notes]

nino-rossi.tn: A stamp in the form of an oval metal disc set into the shank.
nino-rossi.not: After the First World War, Leonida Rossi was made head of the company, with his brothers also joining the management. The firm's name became Fratelli Rossi Barasso, from which the FRB abbreviation on the stamps derives.

o13.tn: A logo consisting of the wording "1er".

fireside.tn: A stamp combining a windmill depiction with the "Fireside" name.
fireside.not: The leather-covered pipes were made at the Hilson factory. The brand's pipes were manufactured in various countries, mainly Belgium, Denmark, and France.

rows: Genuine Leather, Imported Briar, Made in Belgium

gilli.tn: A "Gilli Mauro" stamp struck on the lower right side along with the maker's handwritten signature.

cherepanov.tn: No logo stamp on the stem; the underside carries "Cherepanov, Russia" lettering set between two lines.
cherepanov.not: Maker Sergey Cherepanov made his first pipes in 2008. No grading system is used for the pipes. According to 2010 data, annual production is around 100 pipes.

cesari.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.

ken-system-pipes.tn: A stem mark bearing the brand name; the text "Ken" on the shank.
ken-system-pipes.not: These pipes were made with a patented internal mechanism; the stamps show patent number 2242803 or the phrase "PAT. APLD".

cavalier.tn: A mark on the stem consisting of a single letter and a ring (band).
cavalier.not: This Cavalier pipe carries the shape of a well-known Dunhill model and has been downgraded to this brand bearing the Hardcastle stamp. Pipes with fewer flaws are downgraded the same way from Dunhill to Parker.

optimal.tn: A bar motif together with the hand-written "Optimal, Butz Choquin" on the front of the bowl.
optimal.not: These pipes, dated to the 1960s, were designed by Joe Colombo.

rows: 122, Saint Claude France, Modele depose, N°154 217
On the front of the bowl
On the front of the bowl
122, Saint Claude France, Modele depose, N°154 221

salmon-gluckstein.tn: No logo; the band carries the text "S & G. LD" along with anchor, walking-lion, and date-letter hallmarks.
salmon-gluckstein.not: The [a] date letter on the band is the mark of the Birmingham Assay Office and indicates the year 1900. The stem is made of amber, fitted with a threaded horn tenon.

suhr.tn: A decorated round dot on the stem.

hans-christian-andersen.tn: The text "Hans Christian Andersen" in the stamp.
hans-christian-andersen.not: This stamp belongs to a limited series issued in 2005 for the 200th anniversary of the writer Hans Christian Andersen's birth.

prince-albert.not: Named after the tobacco brand of the same name. The "Prince Albert" brand was acquired by John Middleton in 1987.

dunhill-2.tn: Briar pipe with a Vercingetorix figure, its winged-helmet top made as a screw-on bowl cap.
dunhill-2.not: The pipe's winged-helmet-shaped top piece is a screw-on bowl cap, and the pipe is presented with its patented case. The ventilated case design was patented in 1920 under number 141486/19. Records date the example to between 1920 and 1930.

rows: The top (winged helmet) is a screw-in bowl. The pipe is displayed in a patented case.
The patent 141486/19 has been granted in 1920 for the design of the ventilated case. The vents on the case and the removable bowl may be observed on the enlarged views.

savinelli-erica-fiamma.tn: Sun motif on the stem; country stamp within a shield on the right side.
savinelli-erica-fiamma.not: The same sun logo is also used on Savinelli's Fiammata and Molinella lines. Shape number 320 also appears in the brand's Sandblasted 320KS, 320EX Hercules, and 320KS Siena lines; for a similar logo see Oldenkott.

e-andrew.tn: Single gold dot on the stem; "E. Andrew" lettering on the shank.
e-andrew.not: The pipes are made by craftsman Edward Andrew Jurkiewicz, who works in Milwaukee.

mac-cranie.tn: One or two dots on the stem.
mac-cranie.not: Records indicate this example was made in 1990 by Ashton pipe maker William Ashton Taylor for the McCranie's shop in Charlotte, North Carolina, the sole retailer permitted to sell Ashton pipes under its own name. Another example is said to have come from Tonino Jacono.

perry-white.tn: "Perry White" and "Hand Made" wording plus a grade code on the underside.
perry-white.not: The pipes are made by Bob Swanson; the brand name comes from Swanson's grandfather. The letters MM in the stamp indicate Italian-sourced briar. Smooth pipes are graded A, sandblasted or rustic pipes B, from 1 to 3; larger sizes are marked with codes from XL to XXXL and M (magnum); per records, 2010 production was 50-75 pipes a year.

rows: America, Perry White, Hand Made, MM5B2

klein.tn: No separate logo; the words "Peter Klein Denmark" appear on the underside.

iffy-tvf.tn: No separate logo stamp; the abbreviation "T.V.F" is stamped on the right face.
iffy-tvf.not: The "T.V.F" stamp is struck so as to straddle the join between the shank and the stem.

countryman.tn: Elephant figure on one face of the stem, the country name on the other; used on meerschaum pipes.
countryman.not: The brand of the Tanganyika Meerschaum Corporation, under Amboseli Pipes. See also the related manufacturer's GBD, Kiko, Kikob, Kilimanjaro, Kudu, Twiga, Merlin, and Sportsman records.

rows: The other side of the stem

yorkshire-2.tn: A double-diamond motif and a pipe emblem on the stem; the word "Yorkshire" on the left face.
yorkshire-2.not: Because of the double-diamond logo on the stem, this stamp is associated with pipe retailer Barnaby Briars. The briar stem seen in this example is also a feature found on most Barnaby pipes. Other brands using briar stems include Barnaby, Il Cepo, Kaywoodie Allbriar, and LHS (Purex Allbriar).

david-jones.tn: Large round mother-of-pearl dot on the stem.
david-jones.not: The brand's maker, David Jones, has been making pipes since 1986. Grades run from lowest to highest: sandblasted pipes (ungraded), S (standard), E, P, PP, and PPP.

selected-briar.tn: No separate logo; the shank carries the "Stanwell" and "Selected Briar" stamps.
selected-briar.not: Use of the "Regd. No." stamp was discontinued between the late 1960s and the very early 1970s.

rows: Stanwell, Regd.N°.969-48, Hand Made, In Denmark

de-luxe.tn: Shield figure on the right face; "Savinelli de luxe Milano" lettering on the left face.
de-luxe.not: Records note another example bearing number 506 known as Samanda, in which the Savinelli lettering sits on the clear stem.

old-bruyere.tn: A stamp consisting of the words "Hardcastle's" and "Old Bruyere".

rows: Hardcastle's, British Made, Old Bruyere, Giant

aux-mines-d-ecume.tn: An address inscription within an oval frame, with star and ornamented-circle motifs.

rows: Aux mines d'écume, PARIS, 35 Bould St Martin [within an oval]

weller.tn: A single letter "W" stamped on the underside.
weller.not: The brand has no grading system. Records indicate a maximum of 15 pipes were produced per year as of 2007.

hodula.tn: A mark of one, two, or three round dots.
hodula.not: The pipes are made by Pavel Hodula.

camphausen.tn: No separate logo; the maker's name and a grade letter are stamped on the underside.
camphausen.not: Oliver Camphausen (b. 1968) carved his first pipe in 2000 and began working as an independent pipemaker in 2006. Bulldog and volcano shapes are prominent. Grading rises in the order 5, 6 ... 9, followed by A, B, C.

europa.tn: A mark consisting of a single dot.

berezhnoy.tn: No logo; the underside reads 'A. Berezhnoy' and 'Hand Made Ukraine.'
berezhnoy.not: The maker is Alexandr Berezhnoy, born in 1965; he made his first pipes in 2010. In 2011 his output was about 60 pipes a year.

free-hand.tn: Star-motif logo; "Butz-Choquin" and "Free Hand" stamp on the left side.

hors-classe.tn: A brass logo consisting of the brand name in script.
hors-classe.not: The brass logo was reserved for Ropp's top-grade pipes.

rows: Ropp [within an oval], Hors Classe [Curved], D3

golf.tn: Single-letter logo enclosed in a circle on the stem; the shank reads "Golf Real Briar".

irwin-s.tn: Two letters set inside a circle on the stem.

al-pascia.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem.
al-pascia.not: The private brand of a Milan tobacconist. On early stamps the name is struck in plain block letters as "Al Pascia"; in some series of the brand there are no initials on the stem.

martin.tn: A logo formed from a mammal figure.
martin.not: Rafa Martin is both a tobacconist and a pipe maker; he paused his own production between July 2010 and early 2012.

regis.tn: Letter set inside a circle as the logo; "Regis" on the shank.

emil-chonowitsch.tn: No logo stamp on the stem; "CHONOWITSCH" lettering on the underside.

london-select.tn: On the left side, the text "Select" within a diamond shape.

sasieni-specially-selected.tn: A single dot on top of the stem; curved "Specially Selected" wording on the left side and a fishtail "Sasieni" signature.
sasieni-specially-selected.not: Dated to the pre-transition period, 1919-1924. The "Specially Selected By" stamp indicates the pipe was personally selected by Joel Sasieni. The same stamp is also seen on a two-dot example and on a limited edition dated 1979.

rows: (curved) Specially Selected by Sasieni (fishtail script) London Made

vuitton.tn: A single letter stamped within a circle on the stem.
vuitton.not: Other luxury brands that have had pipes made include Gucci, Hermès, and Pierre Cardin.

mackenzie.not: Records indicate it is a second brand of BBB, with some production carried out in the Republic of Ireland.

smoke-snuff.tn: A logo made up of a letter within a circle.
smoke-snuff.not: The house brand of a tobacco-products wholesaler operating mainly in Florida. The chain had stores in cities such as Orlando, Ocala, and St. Petersburg.

davidoff.not: The pipes were carved in workshops belonging to the Cuty-Fort group (Chacom, Jeantet, Vuillard, Jean Lacroix, Ropp).

antiquari.tn: A white rod inlay in the stem; "Castello Antiquari" on the underside.
antiquari.not: This example, which carries a patent number, dates from the first years after World War II; the white rod is ivory. The Antiquari line was discontinued in later years.

alpina.tn: A logo consisting of a pipe depiction; the left face reads 'Alpina Vieille Bruyere.'

jpl.tn: A stamp consisting of the letters "JPL".
jpl.not: The letters JPL come from the initials of the name Jean-Pierre Lacroix.

johan-kock.tn: A stamp depicting the outline of the island of Ærø in Denmark.
johan-kock.not: Maker Johan Kock's annual output is about 220 pipes. For another brand using an island silhouette, see Bonet.

jceberg.not: The name Brebbia appears in the stamp; see also Brebbia Iceberg.

prestige.tn: Stamp bearing "Chacom" and "Prestige" on the left side.
prestige.not: Records suggest that stamps written with a thick, tailed "C" were used on Chacom pipes made for export; this is unconfirmed.

aladdin.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

rm-davison.tn: No logo on the stem; a five-digit number and "RM Davison" on the underside.
rm-davison.not: Maker Bob Davison began making pipes in 2009. The last two digits of the number in the stamp give the production year (11 = 2011), and the first three give the pipe's sequence number for that year.

crawford.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries brand, country, and construction-method stamps.
crawford.not: Jerry Crawford began making pipes full-time in January 2012.

becker-musico.tn: A motif of bars arranged side by side.

mina.tn: A pipe drawing within a circle, flanked by diamond marks, with the text 'Da Mina, Cortina.'
mina.not: Da Mina is a pipe shop located at Via Roma 5 in Cortina d'Ampezzo (Veneto).

rows: ◊ [pipe within a circle] Da Mina, Cortina ◊

jelling.tn: A logo depicting a human figure.

king-s-imperial.tn: A stamp in the form of a crown figure.
king-s-imperial.not: For similar logos, see Corsican Briar and Royal Ascot.

grechukhin.tn: A record without a distinctive logo, the stamp struck on the underside of the shank.
grechukhin.not: Maker Vladimir Kazimirovitch Grechukhin began as a student of Alexei Borisovitch Fyodorov. The brand is associated with PS Studio.

sasieni-mc-donald.tn: There is no separate logo; on the left side reads the text 'Sasiεni, Mc Donald.'

coronet-2.tn: Logo consisting of a crown-shaped emblem.

grenci.tn: A stamp without a distinctive logo, reading "Grenci, Calabria - Italy" on the shank.

francis-a-rose.tn: "Francis A Rose" stamp accompanied by a bar motif.

encircled-b-logo.tn: A single letter B within a circle.

erik-nielsen.tn: Carries no separate logo; identified by the "Erik Nielsen" stamp on the right side.
erik-nielsen.not: Craftsman Erik Nielsen worked with Kurt Balleby for over a year before selling his first pipes in Chicago in 2003. As of 2011 he makes pipes under his own name in his own workshop.

aalbrg.tn: Word stamp on the underside consisting of the lines "Aalbørg", "Hand crafted", and "Made in Denmark".

kaywoodie-saxon.tn: The left face carries the "Saxon" brand mark and the line name "Consort."
kaywoodie-saxon.not: The pipes were made in a small workshop in Wickford, Essex, by Boettger's son, and sold by his father in the 1970s. Known line names include Club, Essex, Kent, Prince, King, Virginia, Consort, and Exclusive.

knudsen.tn: The words "Holmer Knudsen" within an oval frame on the underside, and "H. Knudsen Handarbeit" in script.

caribic.tn: A single-letter stamp; no detailed stamp casting is on record.

fiammata.tn: The stamp reads "Great Line Fiammata" together with the Castello logo.
fiammata.not: Fiammata is a rare stamp, used on only a handful of select pipes each year. Dating relies on the number inside the castle emblem; the number 50 corresponds to the year 1997.

bayle.tn: A two-letter logo; the stamp carries the name 'Bayle' and the model name 'Aera' in quotation marks.
bayle.not: The brand was founded in 1968 by the distributor Jean Etienne Gustave Bayle, based at 194 rue Charcot, Courbevoie. The pipes were made in other workshops such as M. Waille (EWA) and Genod. The brand ended in 1980.

byford.tn: A single letter on the stem.
byford.not: The brand carries the name of maker Colin Byford. Records indicate it is now owned by Orlik.

jip.tn: A stem mark bearing the brand name; the stamp "JiP" on the left face.

vanderbilt.tn: The word "Vanderbilt" together with a ring motif, with "Imported Briar" beneath it.

hampton-court.tn: A plain, single-color round inlay on the stem.

rows: Hampton Court, Made in England, 35 c

senatorov.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries "S. Senatorov" between two lines.
senatorov.not: The maker is Sergey Senatorov (b. 1982). He carved his first pipe at age ten and has made pipes professionally since 2006.

savinelli-goliath.tn: A stamp reading "Savinelli Goliath" on the underside, together with a shield mark.

select.tn: Text on the left face reading "Butz-Choquin, Maitre-Pipier, Select."

sasieni-4-dot.tn: Four dots on the stem; "Sasieni 4DOT" on the shank.
sasieni-4-dot.not: A post-transition stamp, dating from 1986 onward. "Ruff Root" is the name of the sandblasted finish. Starting in 1986 the "FOUR DOT" stamp was replaced by the "4DOT" text.

rows: Sasieni 4DOT Ruff Root Dark Made in London (within a circle) F, 5

s-bang.tn: No logo; the underside carries the curved words "S. Bang" and "København" along with the maker's signature.
s-bang.not: The workshop's annual output is roughly 500 pipes; pipes are not always stamped with a production year or with Ulf's or Per's signature. Grading for the European market runs in ascending order Black blast, Tan blast, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, A, B, C, and the very rare D; pipes bound for the US market are not graded, instead carrying a code giving the production year and sequence (e.g., 9736: the 36th pipe made in 1997). In 1984 the "Copenhagen" stamp was discontinued and replaced by the word "København."

thuringia.tn: No stamp description available in the records.

aristocrat.tn: A stamp of a single letter within a circle together with a rhombus motif.
aristocrat.not: Aristocrat is an export brand of John Redman Ltd., which had a factory in London. Records note that some examples with notably different stamps and logos may not be products of the Redman workshop.

rows: Aristocrat London Made Superman Made in England

teipen.tn: No emblem on the stem; "Teipen" set between lines on the underside.
teipen.not: The maker is Wayne Teipen. As of 2012 records, annual production was about 30-40 pipes.

croci.tn: Dot-and-bar marks on the stem; an emblem within an oval on the right face.
croci.not: This stamp arrangement differs from the brand's usual stamp. Records indicate it was used in the earliest production, in 1982-1983, before the "Pipa Croci" brand was registered.

rows: Pipa Croci, Fatta a mano, Mantova Italia, dal 1983
dal 1988, Pipa Croci, Fatta a mano, Mantova, Italia
Pipa Croci, Fatta a mano, Mantova, Italia [emblem within an oval]

radio.tn: A corncob pipe; a maker's stamp inside a circle on the underside, with the name "Radio" between diamond shapes.

rows: Missouri Meerschaum Washington M° U.S.A. (within a circle)

johs.tn: No stem mark; the word "Johs" and a handmade notice on the underside.
johs.not: Mogens Johansen carved pipes for Bjarne for fifteen years. Following the death of Bjarne Nielsen, he founded his own workshop under the name "Johs" in 2008.

di-monte.tn: Logo made up of a ring motif.
di-monte.not: The brand belongs to Supreme Imports Corporation.

skovgaard.tn: A lion figure together with the wording "Skovgaard" on the underside.
skovgaard.not: Maker Lasse Skovgaard Jørgensen (b. 1983) is the son of Bennie Jørgensen. As of 2006 records, about 400 pipes were produced per year. Grading, in ascending order, runs 1, 2, 3, and the lion stamp.

kaywoodie-allbriar.tn: 'Kaywoodie' and 'Allbriar' on the left face, with 'All Imported Briar' and a model number on the right face.
kaywoodie-allbriar.not: Pipes in this line use a double-hole stem; the vertical hole near the bit is original to production, not drilled later. This briar-wood stem was used between 1952 and 1955; for a similar feature see the Stembiter model. Other brands with the same type of wooden stem are Barnaby, Il Ceppo, and LHS (Purex Allbriar); for a different kind of wooden shank see Salvatella.

kirsten.tn: No separate logo; stamped instead with text, with the name "Kirsten" on the left side.
kirsten.not: Letters added to the stamp denote the model: L for Lancer, M for Medium, C for Cavalier, and X meaning a brass body. First-generation Kirsten pipes bearing the "Pats. Appl. For" stamp were made between 1936 and 1938.

savinelli-pisa.tn: A stamp with an architectural motif; the shank reads "Pisa".

kent-pipes.tn: A butterfly figure on the underside together with the text "KENT".
kent-pipes.not: The pipes are made by Kent Rasmussen, born in 1961, who began production in 1998. Grading rises from no star through one, two, and three stars; the top grade is marked with the butterfly symbol.

thurmann.tn: A mark consisting of a single dot and an ornamented roundel.

chippendale.not: The initials on the stem read "CD".

dot.tn: A single dot beside a crowned letter "S".
dot.not: The dot beside the crowned "S" indicates the stem is acrylic. Stanwell began using acrylic for its stems in 1995. The dot addition was later discontinued.

dal-fiume.tn: "D G" letters within an oval, alongside a ladybird emblem.
dal-fiume.not: Records indicate that, starting from 2008-2009, Gabriele Dal Fiume's (DG) pipes have used animal marks to indicate shape and finish: a tortoise marks sandblasted, a whale marks smooth and straight-grained, a nautilus marks pipes of a harmonious shape, and a ladybird marks the maker's finest work. Before 2009, a butterfly mark was used together with every grade other than "Dal Fiume" to indicate the best quality attainable within that grade. According to the maker's 2012 statement, these marks do not constitute a strict grading system. The example pipe carries no production-year or serial-number stamp.

kaywoodie-samuel-pepys.tn: The underside carries the text "Samuel Pepys" and "Made in France."
kaywoodie-samuel-pepys.not: This pipe is a French-made GBD, distributed by Kaywoodie; the maker is not identified on the box. Samuel Pepys is also registered as a standalone brand.

karl-kristian-olsen.tn: The text "K. Kr. Olsen" on the shank along with a single-letter mark.
karl-kristian-olsen.not: The pipes are made by Karl Kristian Olsen, working in the town of Outrup, Denmark. Under the name Outrup Pibeservice, the maker also undertakes pipe repair alongside his own handmade production.

brigham-klondike.tn: A logo consisting of a letter enclosed in a circle; the stamps read "Brigham" and "Klondike".

winslw.tn: A logo with a crown and two-dot motif; the stamp bears the name "Winslow" and country of origin, Denmark.
winslw.not: Poul Winsløw worked at the Preben Holm workshop starting in the 1970s and set up his own workshop in 1985. Annual production is roughly 3,000 pipes. The machine-assisted Crown series also falls under this brand; see also Crown.

rows: Winslow, Hand made in Denmark, E

calabresi.tn: An anchor emblem and a single letter forming the stamp.
calabresi.not: Londonaire is recorded as a sub-brand or series of Calabresi.

krska.tn: The words "Krška Czech Republic" on the underside, a logo formed from the letter K, and a crown mark.
krska.not: The crown stamp denotes the "Maestro" grade. Maker Karel Krška has offered his pipes for sale since 1992.

origine.tn: A star motif together with "Butz-Choquin" and "Origine" wordings on the left side.
origine.not: This is the current version of the historic model that contributed to the brand's fame. The white extension piece was made of albatross bone (radius) in the 19th century; on new pipes this piece is made of acrylic.

castello.tn: A rhinestone inlay on the stem together with a white-bar mark.
castello.not: The rhinestone mark was originally used on pipes shipped to the US market and is now seen only rarely. Some stems carry both the stone and the white bar together; one such example is a prototype carved in 1999.

rows: Castello, Sea Rock Briar, Made in Cantu
00.24 Castello, Made in Cantu, Italy, Reg N° ...

ercole-bogni.tn: Motif of bars arranged side by side.
ercole-bogni.not: Craftsman Ercole Bogni has been making his own pipes since 1963; he has also produced pipes for other makers in the Gavirate area.

valby.tn: The word "Valby" on a single line, with "Made in Denmark" beneath it.
valby.not: Valby is the name of a locality in Denmark near Copenhagen.

sasieni-5-dot.tn: Five dots on the stem; "Sasieni 5DOT" on the shank.
sasieni-5-dot.not: A post-transition stamp; records indicate it has been in use since 2001.

david-s.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; "David's, Exclusive" stamp on the shank.
david-s.not: Records suggest it is likely a private brand belonging to a tobacconist.

willard.tn: A logo with a dot and a star motif; the stamp "Willard Imported Briar" on the body.

kaywoodie-oversize-kaywoodie.tn: "Hand Made, Kaywoodie" on the left side and "Imported Briar" on the right side.
kaywoodie-oversize-kaywoodie.not: The 1947 catalog lists seven Oversize finishes; only two of these had a band: the Virgin-finished "Goliath" and the Walnut-finished "Hercules". The only meerschaum-lined model in the line is named "Samson". All Oversize models carry the "Hand Made" stamp.

seita.tn: Mark formed from the letters of the brand name; the shank carries the text "Seita."
seita.not: The pipes were carved for the French state tobacco company at an unidentified factory in Saint-Claude.

foundation.tn: Motif made of several bars; "FOUNDATION" stamp on the underside.
foundation.not: Craftsmen working for Foundation are distinguished by their marks: Peter Hemmer (PH), Gian Maria Gamboni (G), Andrea Gigliucci (AG), Fabio Marchesi (FM), Flavio Benucci (FB), Massimo Musicò (MM), and Giorgio Musicò (GM). The PH mark denotes export-oriented models to which Hemmer contributed.

peterson-standard-401.tn: Stamp in the form of a block-letter P; the shank carries the text "Peterson of Dublin."
peterson-standard-401.not: Records note that the block-letter P logo seen here is an uncommon form among Peterson stamps.

fiamma-di-re.tn: A logo using a crown emblem.
fiamma-di-re.not: The brand was founded by pipe maker Giannino Spadoni, working in Pesaro. Spadoni produced Fiamma di Re pipes until closing his workshop in 1990.

rows: Fiamma di re, fiammata due corone, pesaro maxima

dadson.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the name "Dadson" and a patent number stamp.
dadson.not: Dadson was a brand of H.H. Dadson & Co. (Shaw, Son and Co.), which distributed a patented system pipe close to Dunhill's Dry Way system, with the patent number stamped on the shank. Of the four surface finish options, the rustic one is carved using the same method as Sasieni's rustic finish; for comparison, see the Sasieni Retford and Four Dot Rustic entries.

bartlett-bickley-2.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

balister.not: Records indicate it is a brand of the firm Moss & Lowenhaup.

sir-del-nobile.tn: Logo in the shape of a rhombus (diamond).

mattner.tn: A letter within a circle; the text "Mattner" and "Johannesburg" on the shank.
mattner.not: The brand bears the name of German-born maker William Mattner. Mattner is deceased.

black-diamond.tn: A single dot on the stem.
black-diamond.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, the brand is likely Duncan's second-grade line.

rows: Black Diamond, Imported Shelled Briar, 3165 / TD

derby.tn: Ring motif and mammal figure within the "Derby" stamp.
derby.not: Linked to the same-named Derby recorded as a sub-brand of Oldenkott.

midnight.not: The Midnight series appears on Canadian-shaped pipes sold as boxed sets of three; its logo is metal.

huhn.tn: No separate logo stamp; the underside bears a symbol along with the maker's name and production details.

maya.tn: The text 'Jeantet Maya' in the stamp.
maya.not: The series takes its name from the cartoon character Maya the Bee.

kaywoodie-early-drinkless.tn: Letters KBB set within a clover on the shank, gold-foil clover inlay on the stem.
kaywoodie-early-drinkless.not: The 05 in the stamp is the shape code (short-shank billiard), while 27 indicates, per records, the year of manufacture (1927). The pipe has the push-tenon stem design that predates the synchrostem. Since the KBB stamp within the clover was discontinued in 1933, this mark places the pipe as having been made before 1933 at the old KB&B factory in Union City, New Jersey; the synchrostem patent was granted in 1932.

danbark.tn: Single-letter emblem; "Danbark" lettering on the shank.
danbark.not: The maker of these pipes is Søren Refbjerg Rasmussen.

kaywoodie-traveller.tn: "Kaywoodie" and "Traveller" on the shank, along with the wording "London England."
kaywoodie-traveller.not: One of the English-made Kaywoodie pipes produced by Oppenheimer Pipes.

jima.tn: A stem mark bearing the brand name; on the underside of the stem, a notice of French and foreign patents.
jima.not: The brand was taken over first by Chapel Frères & Cie (Chap), then by the Berrod-Regad group.

emperor.tn: Logo made of several letters; "Emperor, Imported Briar" lettering on the left side.
emperor.not: Emperor is a brand of the Empire Pipe Co. The same stamps are recorded appearing on the stem together with the wording "Custom Finish" or "Hand Finished".

savinelli-roma.tn: The text "Roma" used together with the shield-shaped Savinelli crest.
savinelli-roma.not: The placement of the shield logo on the stem varies from example to example; different Savinelli shield forms are compared to distinguish them.

rows: On the side of the stem

ancestor.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle.
ancestor.not: Records indicate it is one of the secondary brands used under the Comoy's umbrella. Shape number 363 corresponds to the square-panel shape in Comoy's catalog.

hurricane.tn: A logo of a single letter.
hurricane.not: Hurricane-type pipes were also produced or distributed by other brands under their own stamps, including Fribourg & Treyer (Shipmate), Dr Plumb, Butz Choquin (Auto-Sport), Cyclone, Mastercraft (Sparkproof), and Fortnum's (Windward).

rows: Roy Tallent Ltd, Made in England

ermuri.tn: Logo formed of a human figure.
