ermuri.not: Records indicate Ermuri is the brand of a buying group formed by independent retailers.

comoy-s-grand-slam.tn: A bar logo on the stem in white, turquoise, and white stripes.
comoy-s-grand-slam.not: Grand Slam pipes with the bar logo date to 1933-1945; after the Second World War this logo was replaced by a three-piece inlaid "C". Marks such as "*4" and "*5" in the stamp denote the size of the leather washer at the tip of the metal pin, and are struck on the underside of the shank. An example based on the same patent is also found on the Newhaven brand.

rows: Made in England (within a circle) U.S.PAT. 2001612, 219
Made in London (within a circle) England, 203 (shape code)

dr-mills.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle.

rows: Dr Mills Anti-Nicotine, Algerian Briar, Made in France

canadian.tn: An S letter set on the axis of the stem.
canadian.not: Stamp records indicate this name is a Sasieni product, made in England.

rows: "Canadian", by Sasieni, London Made, Made in England (rugby-ball shaped stamp)

mont-blanc.tn: A single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.

schimmenti.tn: A silver mark on the stem in the shape of a bent pipe merging with the letter "K."
schimmenti.not: The tops of the letters in the word "Kalabash" are styled in an Arabic manner, a reference to the architecture of Palermo. Sicilian culture was strongly shaped by the Moorish presence there from the 9th to the 11th century.

drury-lane.tn: Lettered stamp made up of the letters of the brand name.

rows: Made in London [within a circle], England, 551

jolly-roger.tn: A logo depicting a human figure with a pipe; the words "Jolly Roger" on the shank.

brigham-maple-leaf-logo.tn: A maple-leaf-shaped logo; the text "Brigham" on the shank.

golden.tn: A stamp reading "Golden Parker" struck on the left side.

bussang.tn: The words "Ropp Bussang" on the underside.
bussang.not: Bussang is the name of the village in the Vosges mountains of northeastern France where Eugène-Léon Ropp (1830-1907) set up his first workshop. The Bussang stamp, a horn stem, and a rounded rim are the criteria used to date a pipe to the early period of 1870-1893.

rows: S G D G (Sans Garantie Du Gouvernement)

di-capo.tn: Logo made up of a ring motif.
di-capo.not: The brand's maker is Pablo Minetti, of Italian origin, living in Buenos Aires; he began selling his pipes in 2003.

medici.tn: No logo; the underside carries the text 'Medici' and a decorative frieze.

baronet.tn: A logo composed of a crown, star, and diamond elements.
baronet.not: Records indicate this particular Baronet is not a Savinelli product. Since LHS has a series called Baronet, the pipe may belong to that series instead.

le-baron.tn: A target-shaped inlay of concentric rings; the "Le Baron" stamp on the underside.

crown-achievement.tn: "Charatan's" together with "CROWN ACHIEVEMENT" lettering on the left face.
crown-achievement.not: The hallmarked gold ferrule bears a leopard's-head mark, 325 indicating 9-carat gold, and "FC" for Frederick Charatan's initials. The example pipe is dated 1969.

sportsman.tn: A letter within a circle and "SPORTSMAN" in capital letters.
sportsman.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, pipes stamped SPORTSMAN may be the work of A. Frankau, Alex. Royan, H B Saunders, John Hudson Moore Inc., Lorraine, or Sasieni.

provenzano.tn: A single dot on the stem; "Mimmo Provenzano" name and production year on the shank.
provenzano.not: The dot on the stem is an old symbol; it was discontinued in 2012.

barclay-rex.tn: A multi-letter name logo together with a pipe depiction.
barclay-rex.not: The brand was founded in 1910; the shop was on Maiden Lane. As of 2010 records it operates from three addresses in New York: 75 Broad Street, 70 East 42nd Street, and 570 Lexington Avenue. See also André.

mummert.tn: No separate logo is used; the stamp shows the maker's name and a handwritten signature.
mummert.not: Werner Mummert has been making pipes since 1987, and multiple stamp forms are known. The "Bruyère" and "Otterbach" stamps point to an early period; Otterbach is the village in Rheinland-Pfalz where the maker lived. In his early years he graded his pipes from A to E.

prammer.tn: Decorative round dot with a letter inside a circle on the stem.
prammer.not: Maker Joseph Prammer (b. 1953) began carving pipes in 1993 and specializes in bog oak (morta). Per 2007 figures, annual production is about 200 pipes. Grades run in ascending order C, D, E, and EE; morta pipes are not graded.

pinehurst.not: All known Pinhurst pipes have a cigar-shaped bowl. The same logo also appears on the Echt Bruyere brand.

gold-spot.tn: A logo formed by a star-shaped motif.

aaa.tn: Three letters A set within a curved cartouche.
aaa.not: The AAA stamp belongs to the early production of Adriano Anselmi of Ancona; the brand name comes from the initials of the maker's first name, surname, and city. See Anselmi, Raganella.

maurizio.tn: The text "Calabash by Maurizio" on the shank.
maurizio.not: This brand has no connection to Maurizio Tombari's Le Nuvole brand.

manduela.tn: On the underside, the text "Manduela" set between short dashes.
manduela.not: Danish maker Manduela Riger-Kusk (b. 1967) learned the craft from Poul Ilsted between 1990 and 1992, later setting up her own workshop. She is known for the variety of materials and colors used in stems, extensions, and decorative parts; some pipes are stamped with the year of manufacture.

benson-hedges.tn: A multi-letter logo; the stamp shows the initials 'B&H.'

fe-ro.tn: Stamp consisting of the lettering "Fe-Ro" on the left side.
fe-ro.not: The example on record is a pipe fitted with a 9 mm filter.

skippy.tn: A logo made up of a human figure with a pipe.
skippy.not: Records indicate the pipes were made in France for an unnamed third party.

demuth.not: The stamp is a tobacconist's label and should not be confused with the William Demuth Pipe Company (WDC). Lancaster, USA, is the area where the first large Amish community settled around 1720-1730.

mac-donald-s.tn: A letter stamp within a circle; the text 'Mac Donald's Virgin' on the shank.
mac-donald-s.not: The stamp indicates the pipe was made in France and distributed to the United States market.

harcourt.tn: A logo depicting a mammal figure; the text "Harcourt" on the left face.
harcourt.not: A joint English-Danish brand. In the 1960s its pipes were made for the US distributor Lane Ltd. at the Nording and Preben Holm workshops, and in the 1970s at Preben Holm's workshop for Dunhill.

capitello.tn: An architectural capital motif together with the brand name.
capitello.not: Enzo Galluzzo, who had carved for Caminetto, founded Capitello around 1982-83 after parting ways with Luigi Radice and Giuseppe Ascorti. He ran the workshop with his partner Corrado Ripamonti until it closed in 1991. Records indicate Capitello was the only Italian pipe brand to oil-cure its pipes in the 1980s.

comoy-s-extraordinaire.tn: "Comoy's" and "Extraordinaire" lettering together with an oval-framed "Made in London" stamp.
comoy-s-extraordinaire.not: From 1950 onward the "Made in London" stamp was generally enclosed in a circle; the oval form seen here is considered distinctive for dating purposes. The name "Extraordinaire" was used for pipes larger or more unusual than normal.

rows: Made in London [within an oval] England, 804

bold-rebel.tn: The words 'Medico, Bold Rebel' on the left face.

lorenzo.tn: A single letter L in a shield-shaped crest.
lorenzo.not: In the source it is linked to the Spitfire, Lloyds, Edison, Erica, Old-Vic, T.V., Uncle Paul, and Tagliabue brands (see).

crown.not: Grades run from lowest to highest: Viking, 200, 300, and Collector.

rows: Crown, 300, 9 m/m, Hand Made in Denmark
Crown Viking, Hand made, in, Denmark

martin-r.tn: A single-letter logo; on the top, the text 'R. Martin' and 'Richborough.'
martin-r.not: Maker Richard Martin (1920-2003) was the son of Thomas Martin, founder of Blakemar Briars. In 1961 he moved the factory to Litchborough (Towcester) and modernized production. In 1986 ownership of the company passed to his nephew Michael Billington.

dun-king.tn: Crown motif and a letter enclosed within a circle; "Dun-King" lettering on the stem.

charles-cross.tn: Single bar (line)-shaped logo on the stem.
charles-cross.not: Other Comoy's second-line brands sharing a single-bar stem logo are Carlyle, St James, The Golden Arrow, Town Hall, and Trident.

sumerler.tn: A logo made up of a single plain round dot.
sumerler.not: Records indicate some pipes bearing this brand were carved by Armellini.

kingsland.tn: A plain round blue dot on the stem.
kingsland.not: Records indicate Kingsland pipes were made in England by Friedland & Jackson. Kingsland is also the name of a street in North London where pipe makers were concentrated.

rows: Kingsland, Real Briar, Foreign Blue spot

perri.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo description is recorded.

westminster.tn: An architectural logo depicting Tower Bridge.
westminster.not: The same logo also appears on the Empire brand. It has not been established whether the Tower Bridge logo pipe and the sun logo pipe come from the same maker. Records indicate the brand belongs either to Comoy or to John Redman Ltd.

paragon.tn: The letters "KBB" enclosed in a clover, with "Paragon" next to it.

rows: KBB [within a clover], Paragon, Italian Briar

the-swiss.tn: A mountain-motif logo along with the letters "KBB" set within a clover and the wording "The Swiss."
the-swiss.not: For another mountain-motif logo, see Heighstone.

rows: KBB (within a clover) The Swiss, Italian bruyere 4506

trident.tn: A single-bar inlay on the stem; "Trident" on the shank.
trident.not: One of Comoy's second-line brands bearing the single-bar logo on the stem. Other names in the same group are Carlyle, Charles Cross, St James, The Golden Arrow, and Town Hall.

peterson-green.tn: A stamp presented with a green painted finish, the shank reading "Peterson" and "Spigot".
peterson-green.not: Green Spigot is one of Peterson's lines finished with a green painted surface. The brand's other green lines are Racing Green, Green Spray, and the blue-green Irish Sea. Green-finished pipes are also seen in the Rainbow, Rattray's, and Savinelli brands.

newhaven.tn: A single dot on the stem.
newhaven.not: The "Pat. Applied for" wording on the stamp is, according to records, related to the patent known as "Grand Slam".

cesare.tn: A single round mother-of-pearl dot on the stem.

rows: Cesare Ultra Splendida, Hand Made in Italy

karin.tn: A logo consisting of a single "K" set inside a circle.
karin.not: The maker behind the brand, Karin, is the wife of pipe maker Romeo Domenico (Mimmo).

gepetto.tn: A Pinocchio figure worked in silver inlay.

il-ponte.tn: A single letter set inside a circle on the stem.

abspot.tn: Single letter enclosed in a circle.

mistrel.tn: The lettered "Mistrel" stamp on the shank.

rubin.tn: Logo made up of a chevron and solid-ring motifs.

ivarsson.tn: The text ". An Ivarsson . Product" set inside a circle on the underside, with the handwritten initials L I.
ivarsson.not: Lars Ivarsson (b. 1944) is the son of Sixten Ivarsson and father of Nana Ivarsson. According to 2009 records he produced 50-100 pipes a year.

edison.tn: Single-letter mark on the stem; "Edison handmade" lettering on the shank.
edison.not: The series was produced in collaboration with Danish craftsmen.

robin-hood.tn: Logo made up of a letter inside a circle and an arrow motif.
robin-hood.not: The same logo also appears on the Empire State and Regis brands.

azuma.tn: A stamp consisting of the wording "AZUMA Hand Made in Japan."
azuma.not: One of Tsuge's second-grade lines, aimed mainly at export in the 1980s. It is linked to the Esterd record, which uses the same logo.

john-redman.tn: A single-letter mark on the stem; on some examples the letter is enclosed in a frame, and an anchor figure is also seen among the stamp variants.
john-redman.not: The brand belongs to John Redman Ltd. Richmond is one of Sasieni's second-quality brands. See also Aristocrat, Buckingham, Buckingham Palace, Canberra, Captain Fortune, Dr John, Golden Square, Redonian, Richmond, Smokewell, and Twin Bore.

rows: Redman's Royal, London Made, Made in England

comoy-s-moorgate.tn: "Moorgate" wording on the left side; on some examples the logo is red.
comoy-s-moorgate.not: This is the stamp for Comoy's "Moorgate" series. The name Moorgate also appears elsewhere as one of Comoy's second brands.

gravina.tn: "GRAVINA" on the shank along with "First Quality Briar".
gravina.not: The brand was manufactured by Ibérica de Pipas.

knets.tn: The words "MKNETS" and "USA" below three stars on the top face.

bradberry.tn: A single dot and an arrow motif on the stem; the shank bears the name "Bradberry" and a series name.
bradberry.not: The brand of the New York-based Bradberry Briar Pipe Corp. The same firm's brands also include Town and Country and Wilkinson.

mr-brog.tn: No separate logo is used; the underside carries the brand name, city, and year stamp.
mr-brog.not: The pipes are made by Zbigniew Bednarczyk, born in 1965, who began carving pipes with Kazimierz Róg in 1991. The two craftsmen worked together under the name "Mr Brog"; after Róg's death in 2005, Bednarczyk continued under the brand name.

plymouth.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle, with "Plymouth" on the shank.
plymouth.not: Of two separate stamp castings, one points to Italian and the other to English production. This indicates that, as noted in the sources, the brand was not exclusively a Peterson product.

antidote.tn: "Antidote" and "Catalytic Pipe" on the left side, patent registration on the right side.

sasieni-transition-four-dot.tn: Four dots on the stem; "Sasieni" and "Four Dot" on the shank.
sasieni-transition-four-dot.not: A transition-period production with a Lucite stem, dated to 1979-1986.

rows: Sasiεni, Four Dot, London Made, Made in England

duke-of-kent.not: The fleur-de-lis stamp points to the same production source as the Bayard, Chadhall, Omega, and Thomas pipes. Records indicate this source is the Jeantet factory in Saint-Claude.

rows: Duke of Kent Meerschaum, Algerian Briar, Made in France

baldo-baldi.tn: A crowned pipe emblem alongside the wording "B. Baldi."
baldo-baldi.not: The maker is Baldo Baldi. The "B. Baldi" wording and the crowned pipe emblem may be stamped on either the left or right face of the shank. As of 2008 annual production did not exceed 200 pipes.

vintage.tn: The words "Vintage 1812" on the left face, with "By Barling" beneath it.

t-c-g.tn: The letters "T.C.G" within an oval on the left side.
t-c-g.not: The stamp is recorded as a Birmingham Assay Office mark.

jet-stream.tn: A multi-letter brand mark on the stem; the shank bears the stamp "MEDICO Jet Stream Imported Briar".

fleur-de-lis.tn: A stamp formed from a fleur-de-lis motif.
fleur-de-lis.not: Other brands using the fleur-de-lis motif include Ajustomatic, Cellini, Duke of Kent, Harrington Park, Omega, Thomas, and Vincenzo Lombardi.

rows: Fleur de Lis, Meerschaum lined, France 9465

sorn.tn: A logo built around a single letter and "Sorn" on the shank.
sorn.not: Stanwell's export brand for the US market.

peterson-kapet.tn: A stamp consisting of "Peterson's" on the left side with "Kapet" below it.

rows: Made in the Republic of Ireland, 65

fcsc.tn: Logo formed of the letters FCSC.
fcsc.not: The abbreviation FCSC refers to Football Club Saint Claude, the football club of Saint Claude.

west.tn: There is no separate logo; a maker's-name stamp appears on the underside.
west.not: Tim West moved into full-time pipe making in 1975. The digit stamped on the shank gives the last digit of the year of manufacture. The series names under this brand are "Best of the West" and "Old West."

lorenz.tn: A single dot on the stem.

bonaquisti.tn: The word 'Bonaquisti' on the shank together with a number giving the year of manufacture.

rows: Bonaquisti 02 (carved in 2002) Rustica, Made by Hand, XXL (within an oval)
Bonaquisti 0 (carved in 2000) Sabbia, Made by Hand

rolando-pipes.tn: The underside carries the text "Atelier Rolando" and a two-digit year code.
rolando-pipes.not: Maker: Rolando Negoita, of Romanian origin, who also works as a jeweler and industrial designer. The two-digit number in the stamp gives the year the pipe was completed (07 = 2007). The brand has no grading system.

prevost.tn: No logo on the stem; a curved "Prevost" on the underside.
prevost.not: The pipes were made by Pete Prevost. The brand has no grading system; see also Medici.

driftwood-finish.tn: No distinctive logo; identified only by the "Driftwood" finish name.
driftwood-finish.not: "Driftwood"-finish pipes do not use the grading scale based on seafood names; grades range from X to XXX. On these pipes the signature is reduced to the maker's nickname, "Walle".

smokers-emporium.tn: A single-letter logo; "Smokers Emporium" on the left side.

comoy-s-silver-cloud.tn: The underside carries the words "Comoy's" and "Silver Cloud" along with the inscription "Made in London, England."

rows: Comoy's, Silver Cloud, Made in London, England, 66

kaywoodie-heirloom.tn: "Kaywoodie" stamped on the left side, "Imported Briar" on the right.
kaywoodie-heirloom.not: The Heirloom line consists of hand-carved figural briar bowls and is a revival of Kaywoodie's carved-bowl pipes from the 1930s. The line was produced from the late 1950s to 1963, offered in three carving types: nobleman, satan, and prophet. Records indicate the carvings were done at the Kaywoodie factory by Charlie Ware (d. 1963).

sasieni-trafalgar.tn: A single red dot on the stem; the words "Sasieni" and "Trafalgar" on the underside.
sasieni-trafalgar.not: Wilczak and Colwell's study suggests this name may be a Charatan or Butz-Choquin sub-brand, though this is not certain. Records also note a Sasieni second brand of the same name.

pura-diagonale.tn: Decoration made up of several lines on the stem; "Brebbia" on the left side, "Pura Diagonale" on the right side.

kaywoodie-early-kaywoodie-1919-1924.tn: Letters KB&B set within a clover on the shank, with "Kaywoodie" lettering arched above it.
kaywoodie-early-kaywoodie-1919-1924.not: The letters KB&B are stamped within a clover on the shank.

rows: Kaywoodie (arch-shaped at the top) KB&B (within a clover)

bruce-peters.tn: A solid ring motif on the stem.
bruce-peters.not: The brand of the Penn Tobacco Company, founded in Wilkes-Barre in 1901 by Russell Uhl (d. 1914) and Henry Weigand (d. 1942); the brand's namesake, Bruce Peters, was the company's treasurer. Of the firm's four pipe series, Bruce Peters was the top tier; the others were Silver Mac Duff, Vox Pop, and Broadcaster. The pipes were made for Penn by Henry Leonard & Thomas and were obtainable only with the firm's tobacco coupons.

kikob.tn: The word "KIKOB" on the underside; there is no separate logo.
kikob.not: One of the brands of the Tanganyika Meerschaum Corporation, under Amboseli Pipes. For the same organization's other brands, see Countryman, Kiko, Kilimanjaro, Kudu, Merlin, Twiga, Sportsman.

rows: KIKOB, Genuine Imported Briar, Made in Tanganyika

torben-dansk.tn: No separate logo mark; the inscription "Torben, Made in Denmark, Dansk" on the left face.
torben-dansk.not: The pipes were made for Dan Pipe in Germany.

kb-b.tn: The letters "KBB" set inside a clover leaf, with a pipe motif.
kb-b.not: Facing a briar shortage during World War II, Kaufman Brothers & Bondy produced pipes under the name "Mission Briar" from manzanita wood gathered in California; this production declined after 1943, once Algerian briar shipments resumed. Monterey is also a sub-brand of KB&B. The shape number 55 in the stamp and the Carburetor patent numbered 2082106 coincide with Kaywoodie's system; since Kaywoodie made Carburetor pipes after 1948, manzanita production must have continued after the war as well.

rows: KBB (within a clover), Monterey, Specimen Briar

golden-bark.tn: A three-line "Golden Parker Bark" stamp struck on the underside.
golden-bark.not: The pipe carries the circled 4-group code also used by Dunhill.

rows: ◊ Made in London, England, 4 [within a circle], 272 ◊

ascot.tn: A stamp of a single letter set within a circle.

bucko.tn: A plant figure on the stem.

breeden-s.tn: A single-letter stamp; the left face reads "Breeden's Royale."
breeden-s.not: Records identify it as a brand of an American tobacconist.

lloyds.tn: The text 'LLOYDS' on the shank along with a target-like motif of concentric rings.
lloyds.not: Records indicate Lloyds is an export brand. Pipes stamped "Century Old" were generally made by Lorenzo for the U.S. market. For the same "Century Old" stamp, see Jet Pipe, T.V., and Century Old.

julius-vesz.tn: A grade number enclosed in a circle.
julius-vesz.not: Hungarian-born maker Julius Vesz produced two series: Hand Cut, entirely handworked and using very old briar, and Hand Made, smaller and plainer. Grades run in ascending order from 3-9 then A-D for Hand Cut, and 2-4 for Hand Made. The abbreviation GKCPC in the stamp denotes the Greater Kansas City Pipe Club; for the maker's early stamp, see Craft.

rows: Julius Vesz, Hand Made, 2 [within a circle], Canada 45
Julius Vesz, Hand Cut, 9 [within a circle], Canada, 2002

rogue.tn: Logo based on a single letter; the underside carries the text "Medico Rogue."

rows: Prince Amled, Made in Denmark, Hand Made

collection-kkkk.tn: The "KKKK" grade stamp inside an oval; a white bar logo on the wooden extension.

rows: [Castello logo] Castello, Collection, KKKK (within an oval), Carlo Scotti

loewe.tn: The letters 'L&C°' within an oval frame.
loewe.not: The brand was founded in 1856 by Emil Loewe. It later passed to Civic, joining the Cadogan group (BBB, Civic, Comoy, GBD, Loewe, Orlik) around 1979. The date letter 'D' on the band corresponds to 1978 in the London assay office system. See Haymarket.

6-super.tn: Number 6 enclosed in a diamond on the shank, with "Parker" and "Super" text.
6-super.not: The same shape number (45) is also used in the "Rugby" model.

capitol.tn: A single-letter stamp; the name "Capitol" is written on the left face.
capitol.not: According to records, the brand belongs either to the British firm R M Littaur & Co or the American firm KB&B; sources do not clearly settle between the two options.

berbriar.tn: A plain, single-color round inlay logo.
berbriar.not: Berbriar is a brand of the California-based Briarwood Corp. The pipes are made from ground wood compressed under very high pressure without glue or heat. The same company operated the Manzanita (Mission Briar) source during the Second World War.

town-club.tn: The words "Town Club" within a shield-shaped crest.
town-club.not: Records mention this alongside the Country Club and Royale brands.

rows: Town Club London Made, Made in England

excelsior.tn: "Excelsior de Luxe" lettering with a letter logo enclosed in a circle.

rows: Made in France, Fabrique par BC

vinche.tn: The word "Vinche" together with a triangle motif; the pipe has a meerschaum coating.
vinche.not: The workshop was located in Brussels, at 85 rue du Marché aux Herbes. Precise dating is not possible; records place this pipe before the Second World War based on the old address on the box lid. The French inscription on the side of the box states that the workshop was an appointed supplier to the Prince of Belgium; this title belonged to Albert I, who was king of Belgium from 1909 to 1934.

rows: On the edge of the box
◊― FOURNISSEUR BREVETE DE S.A.R. M GR LE PRINCE ALBERT DE BELGIQUE ―◊
On the edge of the box

the-biltmore.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.
the-biltmore.not: One of National Briar Pipe Co.'s brands. The company's other brands include Forecaster, Honey Brook, Rembrandt, and, after 1960, The Doodler; see also Biltmore.

rows: The Biltmore, Sandblast, Made in London, England

el-bronsa.tn: Logo formed of a plant motif.

flame-grain.not: Records indicate this pipe dates to the postwar period, before the brand was registered. The "Stanwell" name was stamped in handwritten italic letters, and the S on the stem was used only after the brand's registration.

pearl-bee.tn: An inlaid pearl set into the stem; on the shank, "Pearl Bee" and a pipe illustration within an oval.
pearl-bee.not: The pipes have been carved since 2006 by Radka Hofmannová, who works in Prague. As a logo, a natural freshwater pearl is set into the stem, and occasionally into the shank.

north-dane-pipes.tn: A logo formed of an anchor figure.

rows: North Dane Pipes, Made in Denmark

shok.tn: Logo formed from the letters of the brand name; the stamp reads "SYSTEME SHOK SELECT."

westminister.tn: A single-letter logo; the brand, bowl-lining material, and place of manufacture appear on the body.

safferling.tn: Logo consisting of two drop shapes.
safferling.not: The maker of these pipes is Bertram Safferling; the workshop's annual output is roughly 250 pipes. Grading runs in ascending order from 1 to 5, with the rare "A" as the top tier.

la-fond-s.tn: A single-letter L stamp; the words "La Fond's Vintage" on the underside.

richmond-2.tn: Single letter set inside a circle on the stem.
richmond-2.not: The pipe is part of a set called "Three-a-day".

houka.tn: The text "Houka" set inside a frame.

alcazar.tn: A single-letter mark on the stem.
alcazar.not: Records suggest the brand is thought to be a name used by Comoy for the Spanish market (Wilczak and Colwell).

nantua.tn: A handwritten letter "R" on the stem.
nantua.not: Records indicate that Ropp stamped a handwritten letter R on the stem of some pipes intended for export.

rows: Nantua, Made in France, Imported Briar

kaywoodie-silhouette.tn: The underside carries the words "Kaywoodie" and "Silhouette" along with a shape number.
kaywoodie-silhouette.not: The stamp dates to the 1943-1972 period. Silhouette-line pipes were made only with a sandblasted finish and a metal band.

genuine-cherry.tn: A bark-covered cherrywood shank; the underside reads "Genuine Cherry".
genuine-cherry.not: A pipe made of bark-covered cherrywood rather than briar. Ropp stamped a handwritten letter R on the stem of some of its pipes intended for export.

smoker-s-pride.not: A brand belonging to the Lane Ltd. group.

sms.tn: A logo made from the letters of the brand name; no stamp on the meerschaum bowl itself.
sms.not: The import brand for meerschaum pipes made in Turkey. The company was founded in 1980 by Samil Sermet and his wife Beth.

spectator.tn: The wording "SPECTATOR" along with a solid ring motif.

kaywoodie-no-line-stamping.tn: A record with no stamp indicating the product line name on the pipe.

nordstrom.tn: A stamp formed of a bar motif.
nordstrom.not: Records indicate this is an export-oriented brand.

foresti.tn: Instead of a separate logo, the signature "E. Foresti" struck on the left side.
foresti.not: Carries the signature of Italian maker Enzo Foresti (b. 1947). The maker is also known in records by the nickname "Aqualong".

nemerit-s.tn: A stamp featuring a shield-shaped crest and a pipe depiction.

savinelli-bings-favorite.tn: A stamp on the stem shaped like a golf club, evoking a pipe.

savinelli-siena.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; the stamp carries the name "siena" and the shape number "320 KS."
savinelli-siena.not: The same "S" logo was also used on Savinelli's Dry System line. Shape 320 was also produced in other lines as Sandblasted 320KS, 320EX Hercules, and 320EX Erica Fiamma.

man.tn: No separate logo; the "Great Britain" stamp struck under the shank and stem of meerschaum pipes.
man.not: This is the brand of Manxman Pipes Ltd of Old Laxey, Isle of Man. The meerschaum used in these pipes is mostly of Tanzanian origin. See also Manx Meerschaum and Pioneer.

craft.tn: Ring-motif logo; "Craft Briar" stamp on the shank.
craft.not: According to Michael Lindner, "Craft Briar" is a label Julius Vesz used in his early period.

national-cob.tn: On the underside, a squirrel figure at the center of the registered trademark stamp.

kirk-walden.tn: A stamp in the form of an ornamented round dot.
kirk-walden.not: Kirk Walden began repairing pipes in 1998, then turned to carving his own pipes under the KW Pipes label in the early 2000s. Records show no trace of this part-time craftsman after 2007.

ggg.tn: A stamp formed from the letters "GGG" enclosed in an oval.
ggg.not: Records indicate GGG is a product line or sub-brand of the Titanus firm. The Titanus factory in Bassano del Grappa and the town's pipe shop on Via del Macello belonged to the Cavazzon family. Titanus's briar pipe production ran from the 1940s to the 1980s.

vuillard.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem; "Vuillard, Artisan" on the left face.
vuillard.not: Records indicate the brand is associated with the Emile Vuillard & Cie factory.

cybele.tn: Star-shaped emblem; "Butz-Choquin" and "Cybele" lettering on the shank.
cybele.not: The "Cybele" model is always made in the same shape and uses reconstituted exotic wood for the shank extension.

guido-del-vecchio.tn: A multi-letter logo with a solid circle motif.

seemann.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the letters "P M" between two lines.
seemann.not: Grading is not stamped on the pipe: A, B, and C denote pipes with some sand pits, X denotes a special shape or surface treatment, and XX denotes exceptional grain.

salomonica.tn: Word stamp on the left face formed from the letters of the brand name.
salomonica.not: The maker of this Spanish brand is unknown.

electra.tn: Ornate round dot on the stem.
electra.not: The brand has also distributed leather-covered pipes.

sasieni-millennium.tn: On the left side, the text 'Millennium London Made'; on the right side, a single-letter text stamp giving manufacturing and brand information.

sterncrest.tn: A stamp made up of the letters LHS within a diamond shape.

rows: Sterncrest, LHS (within a diamond), Imported Briar

peterson-made-in-ireland-2.tn: On the right side, the 'Made in Ireland' stamp within a circle.

fischer.tn: A stamp reading the brand name "Fischer".
fischer.not: The shop closed in 1978. Records give House of Fischer's address as Orchard Park, New York.

bellezia.tn: A white bison figure engraved on the stem.
bellezia.not: The pipes were made for the Bellezia Tobacco Shop in Buffalo, New York; the white bison on the stem alludes to the city's name. The English maker who produced the pipe is unknown.

mastercraft.tn: A two-letter monogram within a circle and a bird-motif stamp.
mastercraft.not: The brand was founded in 1941 and acquired the Shalom Pipe factory in Israel. It belongs to the Lane Ltd group. Second-quality names include Sparkproof, Legion of Honor, Jet Pipe, and Seville.

knudsen-3.tn: An eagle figure along with the words "Danish Handwork" and "by Teddy" on the underside.
knudsen-3.not: Records mention it alongside comparisons to the Dunhill LC.

penn.tn: A single red dot on the stem.
penn.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's study, PENN is recorded as the brand of the English firm Albert Pengally Ltd (referred to as "Pengelly" in some sources).

jeantet-on-stem.tn: The "Jeantet" stamp formed by writing the brand name on the stem.

buth-royal.tn: A single mark on the stem combining a U above and a B below.

dr-grabow-2.not: Records indicate the stamp is associated with the name "Duke".

a-l-oriental.tn: A single letter G at the center of target-like concentric rings.
a-l-oriental.not: The letter G in the stamp is the initial of the shop's owner, Goldch. The brand operated at the Palais Royal in Paris.

rows: A L'Oriental, Palais Royal... Extra (ornate cursive)

preben-holm.tn: Letter stamp used together with a crown motif on the stem; brand name with a letter or number inside a circle on the underside.
preben-holm.not: The "C5" stamp was used to distinguish pipes sold in the US by CAO, which took over distribution from Lane Ltd. in 1985; it therefore marks the latest production period. The Private Collection series dates from the late 1970s to the early 1980s. There are two separate grading systems: ascending letters A, B, C, D, and ascending numbers 101, 202, 404, 606, and 808. Maker Preben Holm was born in 1947 and died on 8 June 1989; see also Ben Wade, Danish Pride, Frasorteret, Harcourt, Monte Verdi, Pipe-Dan, Pipe Lon, Wengholt.

rows: Preben Holm [Crown] Hand Made in Denmark
Preben Holm Fancy Matt Hand Made in Denmark C5
3 (within a circle) Hand Made in Denmark
A (within a circle) Hand Made Denmark

linkman-s.tn: On the top, the words 'Linkman's' and 'Dr Grabow' together with a metal circle.
linkman-s.not: Based on its stamps, the pipe is dated to 1933-1937; the logo is the propeller mark used before the spear-shaped mark. The earliest Dr. Grabow pipes carry both the Linkman's and Dr. Grabow stamps and are classified as Bruyere or Italian Briar.

airflow.tn: An ornamented round inlay in the stem.
airflow.not: A 1935 brand of the Chicago firm Landon & Warner. Hardcastle also produced a line called Airflow for a time.

briar-workshop.tn: A star motif with "The Briar Workshop" arranged in a curve.
briar-workshop.not: The brand was founded jointly by Elliott Nachwalter and Jorg Jemelka; Nachwalter set up his own business in New York in 1980. See also Pipeworks.

rows: The Briar Workshop (curved), Coral SPG, Designers / Pipemakers (curved), 3

becker.tn: The shank reads 'Becker' followed by a row of heart marks.
becker.not: To mark his split from the 'Becker & Musicò' partnership and his return to working alone, Paolo Becker began stamping the year of production on his pipes from 2002 onward (02 = 2002). The brand has its own distinctive grading nomenclature.

jeppesen.tn: The text "P Jeppesen" on the underside; no separate logo is used.
jeppesen.not: The brand's maker is Peder Jeppesen; annual production is about 3500 pipes. Grading rises from 1 to 8, with 1 denoting sandblasted pipes. Peder Jeppesen also owns the Neerup brand.

dartmouth.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle; "Dartmooth Club, London England" stamp on the shank.

barontini-2.tn: A solid-ring logo; the top face bears the stamp 'Liburnia Ambra.'
barontini-2.not: The maker is Ilio Barontini, cousin of Cesare Barontini. See also Küttel.

lane-era-dc.tn: The letter L enclosed in a circle on the underside, with a grade code beside it.

la-scala.tn: A pipe-shaped emblem and the words "La Scala".
la-scala.not: The logo is identical to that of the "La Strada" brand.

ropp.tn: The text "Ropp" within an oval frame; the stem stamp is a single letter.
ropp.not: The brand's founder was Eugène-Léon Ropp (1830-1907). In 1992 the company passed to Cuty-Fort Entreprises, which also runs the Chacom, Jeantet, Vuillard, and Jean Lacroix brands. See Golden Burl and Versailles.

golden-gnome.tn: A logo on the stem combining a diamond motif and a gnome figure.
golden-gnome.not: Brebbia used the gnome logo on its stems between 1953 and 1956. Records date the example pipe to 1956-1968.

knauer.tn: "KNAUER" on the left side, "Made in England" enclosed in a circle on the right side.

john-kent.tn: A pipe figure on the stem; the words "John Kent, Italy" on the shank.

szabo-koros-pipes.tn: A text-only stamp with no logo: "Bruyer Szabó" and "Hungary" on the underside, the model name on the right side.
szabo-koros-pipes.not: Other pipe brands of the Eastern Bloc include ARK (East Germany), Howal (East Germany), and the Golden Gate brand of Ukraine's "Veresk" company.

baff.not: The maker is David Wagner. Wagner also has another brand called sVen.

sorensen.not: The maker is Kjeld Sørensen. See also Red Hat.

ewa.tn: "EWA" lettering formed from the brand's initials.
ewa.not: EWA is the brand of Michel Waille; the name comes from the abbreviation Établissement Waille, and the firm dropped its former name "Waille" in 1979. The brand belongs to the Berrod-Regad group. Jean Waille, who runs the "Le Pipier de Lunel" brand, is Michel Waille's nephew.

concord.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle.

churchill-s.not: The Churchill's tobacconist shop is at the corner of St Andrew's Street and Bridewell Alley in Norwich. The name is said to derive from the shop's location next to a church and at the foot of two slopes. The shop's former manager, John Elvin, retired on 31 May 2008; as of 2008 ownership was held by Keith Garrard.

bonnie-brier.tn: A crown motif together with one- and two-letter forms; the shank bears the name "Bonnie Brier" and a series name.

rows: Bonnie Brier, Willow Ridge, Imported Briar

kensington.tn: A mark of a single letter set inside a circle.
kensington.not: See also WDC's Kensington product line.

confrerie-des-maitres-pipiers.tn: Crest bearing a crossed sash with three pipes on it.
confrerie-des-maitres-pipiers.not: Two versions of the crest are recorded: the crossed sash bearing three pipes leans left in some examples and right in others. Records associate the brand with pipe production in Saint-Claude.

rocky.tn: White letters CC on a black background.
rocky.not: "France" appears on the underside of the stem.

amorelli.tn: A gold-bar-shaped logo split between the stem and the shank, completing when the two halves align.
amorelli.not: The pipes are made by master carver Salvatore Amorelli. Grading rises from one star to five stars; five-star pipes are sometimes marked with gold-colored stars. The bar logo is normally split in two, though it is left whole on certain special pipes.

rows: Amorelli, [* * * * *], 300 Hand Made, Italy [within an oval]

grande-morez.tn: Single-letter logo together with "Grande Morez" on the shank.

wedgewood.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter set within a circle.

brittany.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle; the word "Brittany" on the shank.
brittany.not: Records indicate this is Jean Lacroix's export brand.

gema.tn: A "Gema" stamp giving the brand name in script form.
gema.not: Belongs to a limited, numbered (14/40) series of ceramic pipes depicting the head of General de Gaulle, made by Marcel Giraud (1897-1985) in 1970-1971.

viggo-nielsen.tn: A single dot on the stem; the name "Viggo Nielsen" and handmade marks on the underside.
viggo-nielsen.not: The brand is associated with the town of Faaborg, Denmark. Records indicate this example was carved by Kai Nielsen under the "Viggo Nielsen" brand and presented as part of a seven-day set.

kalabash.tn: No stamp listing or logo description is on record.

the-yomoc.tn: "The YomoC Pipe" alongside a clover symbol.
the-yomoc.not: The name YomoC is an anagram formed by rearranging the letters of the name Comoy.

peretti.tn: Stamp made up of a single letter inside a circle.

bill-sargent.tn: Three dots in a row on the stem, the last one faint.
bill-sargent.not: The maker was Bill Sargent, a pipe maker, repairman, and tobacco shop owner in Topeka, Kansas; he died in the 1980s.

silverking.tn: White logo featuring a crown motif; the left face carries the text "Silverking."
silverking.not: Records indicate this is not a brand but a series name used by an unidentified French factory; other series from the same factory include Big Ben Reputation and Gold King. The Silverking logo is white, while the Gold King logo is yellow.

rows: EP (within a diamond) L W M (in old-style cursive lettering)

compass.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle.

jody-davis.tn: No stem mark; the underside bears the signature "J. Davis" along with the model and grade names.
jody-davis.not: The stamp on the underside carries the grade name (Bishop, Friar) with a grade letter and a two-digit year of production: "03" denotes 2003, "07" denotes 2007. Some pipes carry no grade stamp.

london-castle.tn: On the left side, 'London Castle'; on the right side, the text 'Made in England.'

larsen.tn: A figure of a man seated in an armchair smoking a pipe, and a single white dot on each of the four faces of the stem.
larsen.not: On some pipes the figure of a man seated in an armchair smoking a pipe is stamped on the shank; the same figure is also used on the brand's boxes. There is a single white dot on each of the four faces of the stem.

rows: W.Ø. Larsen, Handmade, Made in Denmark

claridge.tn: No emblem on the stem; single red dot and an ornamented round inlay.
claridge.not: See Cosmopolitan for a similar logo.

spitfire.tn: A logo of interlocking "P" and "S" letters set axially; the stamp also includes a target-board motif.

smokemaster.tn: The letter B within a diamond-shaped frame.
smokemaster.not: The brand's distinctive filter mechanism consists of a slotted tube and a folded pipe cleaner threaded through two special holes in the tenon. The mechanism was developed in 1934, and the US patent (2166537) was granted in 1939. See also Airo, L. L. Bean, Cavalcade, Hallmark, Sterling Hall.

rows: B (within a diamond) SMOKEMASTER CUSTOM MADE
◊ Custom, [B within a diamond] Smokemaster, Made ◊

english-made-2.tn: Target-like motif of concentric rings on the stem.
english-made-2.not: Records indicate the sample pipe was never smoked; the motif on the stem is therefore considered to be the original factory logo.

rows: Ben Wade Made in London England

bongi.tn: A stamp giving the brand name in plain script; the shank bears the notices "G. Bongi" and "Firenze".
bongi.not: A Florence shop selling gifts, games, and accessories that also carried pipes under its own name. Records give the shop's address as Via Panzani, though Via Cerretani is also mentioned as an alternative.

norup.tn: A stamp consisting solely of the word "Norup".
norup.not: The pipes were made by the now-retired craftsman Lars Christensen. Records indicate Christensen was one of the pipe makers working for Anne Julie; he would finish the briar blanks given to him, including the red-and-white dot on the stem, and Anne Julie would apply the stamp.

van-roy.tn: The stamp of the Van Roy brand; no detailed record data available.

savana.tn: A ring motif alongside the text "Savana."

whitehall.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter set within a circle.
whitehall.not: The brand belongs to the US-based Whitehall Products company. Some of the pipes were carved in Italy. The second-quality line was sold under the name Thinbite.

pipe-shop-stampings.tn: An arched "BARLING'S MAKE" stamp on the right side; the name of the pipe shop that sold the pipe appears on the left side.
pipe-shop-stampings.not: A significant portion of Barling pipes made during this period were distributed to pipe shops and department stores across the British Isles; the stamps also carry the retailer's name, as seen here with Tranter Pipe Shop.

rows: FREDK. TRANTER PIPE SHOP. BATH, EXEL

richmond.not: See also the Richmond entry signed John Redman, which carries the same name.

owl-shop.tn: An owl figure together with the brand name "Owl Shop".

qcp.tn: Letters "QCP" inside an oval on the underside.
qcp.not: Maker Andrew Petersen (b. 1970) began making pipes in 2007 and, as of 2013, has done so part-time; per 2012 figures he made 40-50 pipes a year. Early pipes carried a plain "QCP" stamp; the letters were later placed inside an oval, then replaced by a borderless oval reading "A. Petersen USA" with the pipe number in the center. Records indicate the maker planned to grade his pipes with one, two, or three tobacco leaves.

acire.tn: A stamp on the left side reading "Acire".
acire.not: The name Acire is the word ERICA (Erica arborea), the plant name for briar root, spelled backwards.

curtz.not: The maker of these pipes is "Arley" Curtz, who worked in Utah, USA. Records indicate A. Curts pipes also carry two dots on the stem, one red and one white.

redmanol.tn: "P" set inside a diamond on the ferrule.
redmanol.not: Made by Reiss-Premier Corp., a boxed pipe with a Redmanol stem and shank. Redmanol stems mostly used a bone screw tenon. Brands that used Redmanol stems include BBB, LHS (Redmanol series), and Peterson.

la-pipa.tn: A diamond (rhombus)-shaped logo; both a gold and a white version are seen.

rows: La Pipa, L. Viprati, Fatta a Mano

honey-brook.tn: A single letter set inside a circle.
honey-brook.not: One of the brands of the National Briar Pipe Co. in Jersey City, New Jersey, launched as a counterpart to Yelo-Bole's honey-lined pipes. The company's other brands include The Biltmore, Forecaster, Rembrandt, and, after 1960, The Doodler.

a-metz.tn: Solid-ring motif; curved "Butz Choquin" on the left side of the shank with "A Metz" beneath it.
a-metz.not: The Butz-Choquin brand passed to Berrod-Regad in 1951; this stamp predates that date. Before 1951, Butz-Choquin pipes were made or distributed by various manufacturers, including Berrod-Regad itself.

sasieni-retford.tn: Four dots on the top of the stem.
sasieni-retford.not: A stamp from Sasieni's pre-transitional period, 1924-1945. Four dots appear on top of the stem.

rows: Sasieni (fishtail-shaped cursive), London made, Pat No. 150221/20, "Retford", Made in England (arch-shaped)

savinelli-leonardo.tn: "Monna Lisa" on the top of the shank, "Savinelli Leonardo" on the underside.

pall-mall.tn: A single blue dot on the stem; "Pall-Mall" within a diamond-shaped frame on the left side.
pall-mall.not: According to records, the dot on the stem is light blue.

paykoc.tn: There is no separate logo stamp; the pipe bears no mark at all.
paykoc.not: Paykoc Imports started out as a small Turkish meerschaum pipe seller in Denver, Colorado. The firm later expanded its range to include briar pipes and products from other countries.

fortnum-s.tn: A pipe without a separate logo, stamped with the "Fortnum's" name.
fortnum-s.not: This "hurricane"-type pipe was sold by Fortnum & Mason, the London store founded in 1707. The stem is original, and its mark is the same as the Streamliner brand's stamp. See also Hurricane (Orlik).

hilson.tn: A letter logo consisting of the brand name in script.
hilson.not: Seen on meerschaum-lined pipes. See also Albertson.

nonnenbroich.tn: A monogram formed of the letters H and N on the underside.
nonnenbroich.not: This is a 2006 pipe made for the "Bonner Qualmköppe" pipe club in Bonn. Its maker is Heiner Nonnenbroich, born in 1953, who has made pipes since 2002.

tyburn.tn: The words "Tyburn pipes" on the left face.

de-canori.tn: Lettered stamp reading "de canori" on the left face and "de luxe" on the right face.

di-franco.tn: Single dot on the stem; "C. DiFranco" signature in the stamp.
di-franco.not: The brand's maker, now deceased, was Charles DiFranco, who carved and repaired pipes in the 1960s at a pipe and tobacco shop in Trenton, New Jersey.

bayard.tn: A two-letter logo with a plant motif.
bayard.not: One model is made of olive wood with a briar bowl insert; olive wood darkens over time. Records link production to the Chapuis-Comoy factory.

corsica.tn: Single red dot on the stem; single-letter logo in the stamp.
corsica.not: Corsica is the brand of Henri Vuillard, active in Saint Claude. Not to be confused with the E. Vuillard & Cie firm in the same town.

jones.tn: No stamp data is on record apart from the brand name "Jones".

militaire.tn: A text stamp with the name 'Militaire' above the wording 'Imported Briar.'

tokutomi-pipe-company.tn: No separate logo mark; the words "TOKUTOMI PIPE COMPANY" on the underside, along with name, country, and year.
tokutomi-pipe-company.not: The company was founded in 2012 by Hiroyuki Tokutomi. The pipes are made together as a family: his wife Kazue, daughter Yuki, and the maker himself.

royal-star.tn: Logo made up of two letters.

il-duca.tn: No stamp breakdown or theme information is available in the records for the logo.

ladd-s.tn: A crest-shaped logo echoing the British royal coat of arms, and the words "Ladd's".

siro-taioli.tn: A symmetrical logo with a dot on each side of the stem and a bar in the center.
siro-taioli.not: The distributor of the Croci brand in Spain.

sasieni-ltd-edition-double-four-dot.tn: Two rows of four dots each on the stem.
sasieni-ltd-edition-double-four-dot.not: A transitional double four-dot stamp from 1979. One example bears a solid gold band with a wave pattern along with the L.&J.S. hallmark and British assay marks for 1979. The abbreviation LE denotes Limited Edition, and the accompanying number gives the serial number; unbanded examples from the same series also exist.

rows: Specialy Selected [curved] By, Sasieni [in old-style fishtail cursive]
Made in England [within an oval] LE32
Made in England [within an oval] LE 4

c-p-f.tn: A single dot on the stem; the letters "C.P.F." enclosed in an oval on the stamps.
c-p-f.not: The brand was founded in 1851 by the Consolidated (or Colossus) Pipe Factory and taken over by KB&B in 1883. The Chesterfield model can be compared to Kaywoodie's pipe of the same name.

lewis.tn: On the older logo, a brass dot inlaid within a green acrylic dot; on the current logo, the word "LEWIS" curved above the dot.

paradis.tn: The brand name "Paradis" on the shank.
paradis.not: The brand was founded in 1978; as of 2005, output was about 8,000 pipes per year.

digby.tn: Logo based on a single-letter element; the stamp carries the name "Digby" and the wording "London Made".

bamboo-briar.tn: No logo; the left face bears the stamps "Bamboo Briar" and "Made in Spain."
bamboo-briar.not: Bamboo-like carved decoration has been typical of makers in the Valencia region since the early 20th century. The maker of this particular pipe is not known for certain; another producer active in the same region is Bruken.

pipe-club-of-japan.tn: The stamp reads "The Pipe Club of Japan" and "St Claude", along with year information.
pipe-club-of-japan.not: The pipe bearing this stamp is leather-covered.

rows: 1994, The Pipe Club of Japan, St Claude

weingott.tn: There is no separate logo; the brand name and city appear on the left face, with hallmarks on the silver band.
weingott.not: The hallmarks on the silver band aid dating: a leopard's head indicates London, while an anchor indicates the Birmingham assay office. Records indicate the date letter "n" corresponds to 1908 in the London hallmark and to 1912 in the Birmingham hallmark. The brand also had its own pipe shop, and production continued after the Second World War.

ove-lindall.tn: The brand name "Ove Lindall" on the underside.

biltmore.tn: A stamp made up of a letter enclosed in a circle, two dots, and a star motif.
biltmore.not: Seen on pipes with leather-covered bodies. See also The Biltmore.

gold-fire.tn: A stamp giving the brand name in script form.
gold-fire.not: For a similar logo, see Silver Match.

maxim.not: The Maxim brand was produced for the Hamburg wholesaler Terella, which supplies the Wolsdorff tobacconist chain across Germany. The pipes were made first at Oldenkott and are now made at Design Berlin.

neptune.tn: The word "Neptune" on the left side, with "déposée" below it.
neptune.not: Found on pipes with leather-covered bodies. It is related to the Deauville and Marshall Field brands (see).

kaywoodie-chessman.tn: "Kaywoodie" and "Chessman" lettering on the left face.
kaywoodie-chessman.not: An English-made Kaywoodie produced by Oppenheimer Pipe. Comparable to Yello-Bole's "Checker" stamp (see).

mokin.tn: The lettered "Mokin" stamp, formed from the letters of the brand name.
mokin.not: Records indicate the brand is known for its pipes with a bendable shank.

gardhill.not: The brand of the J. Vincent Fils factory, located at 11 rue Carnot in Saint Claude. The factory has closed.

red-point.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; shank stamped "Red Point, Old Briar".

paul-tatum.tn: A decorated round inlay set into the stem.
paul-tatum.not: The pipes are carved by Paul Tatum; as of 2009 he worked as an engineer at NASA and made pipes occasionally. His distinguishing feature is the taxidermy eye he sets into his own custom-mixed acrylic stem.

old-briar.tn: A single-letter logo with no crown.
old-briar.not: According to records, the "Regd. No." stamp fell out of use between the late 1960s and the very early 1970s.

comoy-s-tradition.tn: A three-part inlaid letter C (two black, one white) on the stem.
comoy-s-tradition.not: This three-part inlay technique was discontinued in the early 1980s.

celius.tn: No separate logo is used; the stamp consists only of text, with the name "Celius" on the underside.
celius.not: In this Danish-made brand, the "Root" stamp indicates pipes left with plateau at the rim; the numeric code in the "Chess" series indicates the shape. A batch of pipes made after the maker's daughter was born carries the "Zenia" stamp, her name. The "Randsborg" or "Randsborg crafted" stamp has no special meaning.

barontini.tn: Logos featuring a single letter within an ornamented circle, three dots, a solid ring, and a pipe depiction.
barontini.not: For related brands from the same circle, see Aldo Velani, Cesare, Esseti Toma, L'artgiana, and Stuart.

pembroke.tn: A stamp consisting of the brand name on the stem; "Pembroke" appears on the top of the shank.
pembroke.not: Based on Wilczak and Colwell's study, it is noted that Pembroke may be a label associated with Britannia.

leonard-s.tn: A logo depicting two separate air channels bored into the stem.
leonard-s.not: The brand belongs to Leonard's Pipe Shop, opened by Arthur Leonard in 1936 and closed in 1989. The logo depicts the twin air channels bored into the stem; for pipes using the same solution, see Beau Nash, Grand Master, Kaywoodie Allbriar, Durobit, Radice, Siam, and Twin Bore. Records indicate pipes stamped "Dover De Luxe" are Comoy's or GBD production; see also the Leonard's entry for Sasieni's second brand.

rainbow.tn: Single-letter emblem on the stem; "Rainbow" and a country-of-manufacture stamp on the left side.
rainbow.not: Records indicate the pipes were made by Wilhelm Bjarne Jørgensen. Other brands that made green-bodied pipes include Peterson, Rattray's, and Savinelli.

mr-paul.tn: A wood-look decorated round inlay on the stem, bearing a letter enclosed in a circle.
mr-paul.not: According to records, the brand's pipe shop in Maryland (Windsor Mill, Kenjac Road) has closed.

benzon.tn: A logo of a single letter within a circle together with a diamond motif.
benzon.not: A Verona-based brand; see also Frabenver and Morel.

bbb.tn: A stamp belonging to the 'BBB' brand; not covered in detail in the casting records.

gianni-davoli.tn: Single-letter logo; the underside carries a figure of a jester or devil smoking a pipe.
gianni-davoli.not: The pipes were made for Gianni Davoli, who ran a pipe shop in Milan, by the team of Peppino Ascorti and Luigi Radice in the late 1960s and early 1970s. See also Caminetto.

design-berlin.not: The first firm to begin pipe production in Germany after the Second World War. Annual production stood at around 30,000 pipes in 2007. Linked in records to Maxim and Ottendahl.

brigham.tn: A row of dots (four, five, or six) on the stem along with a plant motif.
brigham.not: The number of dots on the stem indicates the pipe's grade; on the four-dot stamp the dots are arranged horizontally. The brand is known for its "Rock Maple" filter system, made of maple wood.

rorex.tn: Stamp consisting of a single letter within a circle.

regency.tn: Logo made up of a single letter.

portland.tn: A single red dot on the stem; "Portland" on the left side.
portland.not: Although the stamped example was made in Italy, sources trace the brand to the English Portland Pipe Co. After that company closed, some of its brands were produced by Barling. See also the Portland entry signed BB&S.

heding.tn: A single bronze-colored dot followed by "Heding, Denmark".

tree.not: Regarding the number stamp on the stem, see also Twenty One.

ph-vigen.tn: No separate logo is used; "Ph. Vigen" and "Copenhagen" on the underside, along with a year and a number.

cromwell.tn: "Cromwell" and "Genuine Briar" lettering on the shank.
cromwell.not: Brand information is drawn from Wilczak and Colwell's referenced study.

edward-s.tn: Single-letter mark on the stem; "Edward's Handmade" lettering on the shank.
edward-s.not: Edward's Pipes, based in Tampa, Florida, started out importing pipes from France and continued doing so from 1958 to 1963; afterward it switched to production in Florida using briar of Algerian origin, which continued as of 2010. American pipemaker Randy Wiley began his career at this firm.

knute-of-denmark.tn: A logo of a letter set beneath a crown.
knute-of-denmark.not: The Stanwell and Ben Wade brands also have series bearing this same name. The same logo also appears on the Kingsway and Scott stamps.

captain-stag.tn: A stamp featuring a mammal figure; the name "Captain Stag" and the term "De Luxe" appear on the shank.

canadian-club.not: Records indicate this may be a second line of the Comoy's brand.

rows: Canadian Club, London Made, Made in London, England, 253

lord-hamilton.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

fincato.tn: A stamp formed from a single red dot and a letter enclosed in a circle.

brigham-two-dots.tn: Two metal dots on the stem.
brigham-two-dots.not: Pipes with two dots on the stem correspond to shape numbers in the 200 series (2xx).

coronet.not: The same name was used both by this English brand and by one of Savinelli's second-quality lines.

uncle-paul.tn: The words "Uncle Paul" on the body.

rows: Uncle Paul, Genuine Briar [curved], Styled by Lorenzo, A Product of Italy

longchamp.tn: On the stem, a logo in the shape of a mammal figure.
longchamp.not: At least two versions of the stem logo are known: the earlier form differs slightly from the registered logo, while the newer stem form matches the registered logo exactly. The registered logo was also used on boxes and cases. Production is linked to the Forestier-Bourgeois & Cie factory.

comoy-s-celebration.tn: The blue logo on the stem is made of four separate inlaid pieces; the gold band carries a crown, a leopard's head, and a "B" hallmark.
comoy-s-celebration.not: Comoy's Celebration series was made in London. This example is dated to 1976 and has a lucite stem and an 18-carat gold band. The marks on the band belong to the London Assay Office.

rows: Comoy's CELEBRATION, Made in London, England, 101
Comoy's CELEBRATION, Made in London, England, 139

raskassa.tn: "Raskassa" on the left side; the bowl is made from a wood other than briar.
raskassa.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, the brand was distributed in the US around 1930 by Otto Sevic. The grain of the bowl wood matches mountain laurel.

atlanta.tn: A stamp of a single letter set within a circle.

bauer.tn: A meerschaum pipe; there is no stamp on the shank, the markings appear on the box.
bauer.not: The 'Finest Cultured Amber' wording on the box indicates the stem is amberoid or acrylic rather than true amber. Genuine Andreas Bauer pipes have a real amber stem and a bone screw joint; examples stamped 'Made in Turkey' instead use an amberoid or acrylic stem with a delrin joint.

rows: ― Made in Austria ― ― Finest Cultured Amber ―

savinelli-tortuga.tn: A shield mark together with the words "Savinelli" and "Tortuga" and a model number.
savinelli-tortuga.not: The tortoiseshell-look cap and stem are made from synthetic imitation, not real shell.

tracy-mincer.tn: The words "Tracy Mincer" set between two dashes on the underside.
tracy-mincer.not: The maker, Tracy Mincer (d. 1964), records indicate began carving pipes around 1929. For other records related to the same maker, see Custom-Bilt, The Doodler, Holeysmoke.

bocci.tn: No stamp image or casting is on record.

sir-duke.tn: Letter logo set in a circle; the left face carries the text "Sir Duke."
sir-duke.not: Records associate the brand with the Jeantet factory in Saint-Claude.

carcano.tn: A two-dot stamp; the name "Carcano" and the phrase "Fatta a Mano" appear on the underside.
carcano.not: Records indicate the maker is Ettore Carcano, with the workshop located in Gavirate, in the province of Varese.

ludwig-s.tn: The words "Ludwig's" on the left side of the shank.

hansen.tn: No stamp breakdown or logo description is available in the record.

reiner.tn: No separate logo; "Reiner, Pipe Art Design" and a grade letter on the underside.
reiner.not: Between 1983 and 1989 grades C, B, and A were used in ascending order, with pipes stamped "Handmade" and "reiner". Between 1989 and 1997 the grades expanded to D, C, B, A, AS, S, with stamps reading "Handcraftet", "Reiner", and "Pipe Art Design". Since 1998 the stamp "Reiner Design" has been used.

non-canta-la-raganella.tn: No stamp casting or logo data is on record.

eagle.tn: Logo formed of an eagle figure.
eagle.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's research, the brand originates from either Hudson Universal (USA) or W. J. Palmer & Co (England).

dulcet.tn: Letter enclosed within a circle; "Dulcet" lettering on the left face.
dulcet.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's study, Dulcet may be one of Comoy's second-line brands.

jamesons.not: Records suggest the brand may be a second line named after Horace (Ory) Jameson, one of GBD's pipe makers.

86.tn: Curved "BARLING'S" text on the shank along with the "Ye Olde Wood" line.
86.not: Barling's size codes run SS, S, S-M, M, L, EL, EXEL, EXEXEL, and G; the LF and LLF codes denote long flat shapes. In this example the shape number is two digits.

echt-bruyere.tn: A wide horizontal diamond mark on the stem; "Echt Bruyere" lettering arched on the shank along with a fish figure.
echt-bruyere.not: The stem mark resembles that of the Parker brand, though the diamond here is wider than it is tall. Since "echt" means "genuine" in German, records suggest the pipe may be of German manufacture. The same logo also appears on the Pinehurst brand.

lord-britton.tn: A two-letter logo on the stem.

king-erik.tn: A two-letter stamp; the words "King Erik" appear on the shank.

rows: King Erik, Royale, Custom Made Denmark

kaywoodie-carburetor.tn: A text stamp with "Carburetor" and "Kaywoodie" together with a patent number on the left face.
kaywoodie-carburetor.not: A valve fitted beneath the bowl regulates airflow. The mechanism was used between 1937-1938 and 1948-1976. The same mechanism is also found on the Dunhill Airstream, Duke of Dundee, Passat, and Steel's brands.

matt-bruyere.tn: On the left side, the "Parker Matt Bruyere" stamp; part of it is set within a diamond-shaped frame.

quagliata.tn: An "RQ" monogram and a four-digit number on the underside.

pipe-dan.tn: A stamp formed from the letters of the brand name; the left side reads "DAN Shape-Reformed" and the right side reads "Pipe-Dan Copenhagen".
pipe-dan.not: The stamped pipe is one of the examples carved by Preben Holm between 1963-1968, while he worked for the Copenhagen tobacconist. The brand should not be confused with the Dan Pipe Cigar & Company in Germany or the Pipe-Den shop in the USA. Other craftsmen who made pipes for Pipe-Dan include Gert Holbek, P. Holtorp, Sixten Ivarsson, and Ib Loran.

daniel-jud.tn: Ring-motif logo; "D. Jud" signature stamp on the shank.
daniel-jud.not: The maker of the brand is Daniel Jud, a physician by profession (psychiatry). Other physicians known to carve pipes include Robert Kiess (Dr Bob) and Roman Kovalev.

b-p-l.not: A brand of the Dublin-based firm Briar Pipes Limited.

otomatic.tn: A single dot on the stem and the brand name in plain lettering on the stamp.
otomatic.not: According to records, the brand belongs to Friedland and Jackson Ltd.

andersen.tn: No logo on the stem; the stamps are on the underside.
andersen.not: The maker is Søren Eric Andersen; the SEA stamp comes from his initials. Records indicate this stamp came into use around 2007, before which the signature "Eric Andersen" was used.

rows: Eric Andersen, Handmade [arranged in a curve]

kapp.tn: A mark of two dots on the stem.
kapp.not: Records suggest that a pipe bearing this stamp may be an early product of the Kapp & Peterson workshops.

patent-purex.tn: Two or three dots on the stem; the letters "LHS" enclosed in a diamond on the shank.

rows: LHS [within a diamond], Purex, Pat. N° 1587048, Real Briar
LHS [within a diamond] PUREX, Pat. N° 1587048

comoy-s-prima.tn: "Comoy's Prima" on the left side, "London" in a single line on the right side.
comoy-s-prima.not: Introduced in the early 1900s, the Prima series represented the top grade of its time. In the example's Birmingham Assay Office mark, the date letter "l" indicates 1910. The "Comoy's" stamp, written in flowing, forward-slanted cursive with a tail after the "s", was used from 1900 to roughly 1919.

sigmund.tn: Logo on the stem in the shape of a pipe.
sigmund.not: The maker, Segimon Baulenas, worked at the Salvatella factory from 1973 until its closing, then founded his own brand. Records from 2004 indicate he produced roughly 250 pipes a year. His workshop is in Girona.

willoughby-taylor.tn: A logo consisting of a solid ring motif; the stamp "Willoughby Taylor Genuine Briar" on the left face.

virgin-de-luxe.tn: The word "Ropp" within an oval on the left face, alongside the scripted "Virgin De Luxe" stamp.

rows: Ropp (within an oval) Virgin De Luxe (curved)

trypis.tn: "Trypis" set between dashes on the left side, with the wording "Made in Canada."
trypis.not: Maker Phillip Trypis first worked as production manager at Brigham. After founding the Trypis brand under his own name, he continued to produce for this Canadian brand as well; he had a pipe shop in Toronto.

ventilator.tn: The words "MEDICO Ventilator" and "IMPORTED BRIAR" on the underside.
ventilator.not: This model is designed not to be smoked without a rolled paper filter fitted. Other metal pipe brands in the guide include Alco, Bryson, Duncan, Falcon, Kaywoodie, and Ornsby.

norrna.tn: A single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.
norrna.not: The stamp is the private label of the Norwegian outdoor apparel and sporting goods brand founded in 1929. Mesna, meanwhile, is the series name used for pipes made in Lillehammer.

london-town.tn: On the stem, a logo in the shape of an architectural structure.
london-town.not: The same logo is also seen on the Royal London brand.

everest.tn: "Everest" lettering accompanied by a diamond motif.
everest.not: The brand of the Pipas Nubió workshop, founded in 1933 by craftsman Joseph Nubió. The brand is no longer produced.

rows: 3 a Fumada, Vilanova I La Geltru

comoy-s-rockroot.tn: Stamp consisting of "Comoy's Rockroot" on the left side.

hardcastle.tn: No stamp breakdown or logo description is available in the record.

kaywoodie-standard.tn: Stamp consisting of a single letter set in a circle; the left face carries the text "Kaywoodie Standard Imported Briar."
kaywoodie-standard.not: Brylon is a synthetic material developed by S. M. Frank Co. in 1966, made from a blend of heat-resistant resin and wood flour. It is said to be cheaper than briar and more resistant to cracking. The company also used the same material for its Yello-Bole brand.

nova.tn: A logo consisting of the brand name lettering.

buttner.tn: A double-dotted U together with the word "BÜTTNER" on the stem.
buttner.not: Buttner pipes were made of bakelite fitted with a removable porcelain inner bowl. The brand was distributed under separate patents in the United Kingdom, Germany, and France, and the stamps varied accordingly by country.

americana-edition.tn: A logo of a bird figure; the stamp reads 'Americana Edition.'

danish-crown.tn: Crown figure placed between the words "Danish" and "Crown"; the stamp also includes two letters and a triangle element.

c-b-perkins.tn: A pipe figure and a letter enclosed in a circle on the stem.
c-b-perkins.not: This brand should not be confused with the English Perkins brand of the same name.

rows: C.B. Perkins, Braeburn, Made in London England, 152
CBP Heritage, Ben Franklin, Made in London (within a circle)

devonshire.tn: Lettered stamp reading "Devonshire" on the left face.
devonshire.not: "Mission Briar" is a common name for Manzanita (family Ericaceae), a shrub that grows in the western United States. When briar became hard to find during the Second World War, Reiss-Premier Pipe Co and KB&B (Monterey series) used this wood.

singleton.tn: Letter logo set in a circle; the left face carries the text "Singleton."
singleton.not: One of the brands of Singleton & Cole Ltd. Related brands: Conway and Senator.

clan.not: The pipes were produced by Gasparini on behalf of Koninklijke Theodorus Niemeyer Ltd, whose brands also include Neptune, Schippers, Captain Black, and Flying Dutchman. Clan pipes have been present in the Italian market since late 1984. For other pipes originating from tobacco brands, see Borkum Riff, Prince Albert, and Mac Baren.

conqueror.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter on the stem.

savinelli-linea.tn: A stamp featuring the Savinelli coat of arms beside the text 'Linea' and a grade number.

svend-hangaard.tn: The name "Svend Hangaard" on the underside, with "Denmark" arranged in a circle.
svend-hangaard.not: Svend Hangaard began carving pipes after retiring from prison-guard work in 2007.

muhlensiepen.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.
muhlensiepen.not: The brand belongs to Ernst Mühlensiepen GmbH & Co., a firm dealing in tobacco, cigars, and wine.

firex.tn: A stamp on the stem reading "Paronelli" and "London Real Briar".
firex.not: These pipes were carved by Firex for Paronelli.

chadhall.tn: Crest (shield)-shaped logo bearing a plant motif.
chadhall.not: Records indicate pipes carrying this label share the same source as the Bayard, Omega, Thomas, and Duke of Kent pipes.

gamboni.tn: "Gamboni" on the underside together with the letters "GM".
gamboni.not: Pipes made before June 2011 carry a grade stamp of one digit and one letter. After that date grades were named using golf terms, rising in order: Teeing Ground (sandblasted and rustic), Fairway Blasted (smooth), Putting Green (sandblasted and smooth), Skins Game (special pipes from 2012 onward), and Hole in One (numbered collector pipes). The two-digit number next to the grade gives the year of production; the stamp 12 denotes 2012.

danish-made.tn: Logo consisting of a crown with a letter enclosed within it; on the shank, a stamp reading "Ben Wade" together with a mark indicating Danish manufacture.
danish-made.not: Pipes bearing this stamp were made by Preben Holm.

rows: Ben Wade Golden Walnut Made in Denmark

deauville.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo description is on record.
deauville.not: Linked in records to Neptune and Marshall Field.

doctor-mac.tn: "Doctor Mac" name and "Dry Smoker" wording on the shank.

kaywoodie-early-president.tn: Letters KBB set within a clover on the left side of the shank, along with "Drinkless Kaywoodie" lettering.
kaywoodie-early-president.not: The PAT. APP. FOR stamp allows the pipe to be dated to between 1929 and 1931.

la-torre.tn: A single-letter stamp; the words "La Torre Personal" on the shank.
la-torre.not: The maker of these pipes was Ernesto Ossola, who worked between 1970 and 1990.

frank.tn: "Frank" stamp in lettering accompanied by a star motif.
frank.not: A pipe model with a hinged lid.

sasieni-alfred-s.tn: The name 'Alfred. S.' and a model number on the right face, with the stamp 'Sasieni - London' on the left face.
sasieni-alfred-s.not: The stamp carries the name of Abraham Alfred S. Sasieni, son of Sasieni's founder Joseph Joel Sasieni.

fbc.tn: Letters FBC set within a diamond shape.
fbc.not: FBC is the brand of the Forestier-Bourgeois & Cie factory in Saint Claude. Longchamp pipes were also produced at these workshops.

moritz.tn: "J. Moritz" and "Handmade" wordings on the underside.
moritz.not: The earliest known pipes by Jürgen Moritz date from 2004. The pipes are not graded.

don.tn: Logo based on a single-letter element; the stamp carries the name "Don".

piccadilly.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; the stamp reads "Piccadilly".
piccadilly.not: Records suggest Piccadilly was a brand of either the US maker Weber or England's Baron & Co, citing Wilczak and Colwell's work as the source.

v-f-q.tn: The words "Medico" and "V.F.Q." on the body.

maestrale.not: The pipes were made in the 1970s by Rome-based maker Walter Valenti.

trangoni.tn: Anchor emblem on the shank and a letter set within a circle; the number of anchors on the right side indicates the grade.
trangoni.not: The maker is Fulvio Trangoni; the workshop is in Thiene, Italy. The number of anchors on the right side of the shank indicates the pipe's grade. As of 2006, production was about 600 pipes per year.

peterson-great-explorers.tn: A silver band depicting a ship and sea scene together with "Great explorers".
peterson-great-explorers.not: Great Explorers is a collector series offered by Peterson; each pipe carries the name of an explorer.

thomas-cristiano.not: Grading rises from F to A. See also Calabresi.

linea-roma.tn: A letter-within-circle logo beside the words 'Brebbia' and 'Linea Roma.'

rows: Brebbia, Linea Roma, Export, Made Italy

lisa-gherardini.tn: The text 'Lisa Gherardini' on the shank along with 'Pesaro' and 'Hand Made.'
lisa-gherardini.not: The brand name refers to the woman also known as Lisa del Giocondo, or Mona Lisa.

rows: Lisa Gherardini, Pesaro, Hand Made, Italy

idskov-pipes.tn: No separate logo stamp; the underside bears the brand name along with a country abbreviation and year.

tobacco-world.tn: A pipe-figure logo; the stamp reads "Tobacco World, Cheltenham."
tobacco-world.not: The business owner is Rob Dowding. The shop is located in the Regent Arcade in Cheltenham, England.

morissette.tn: The letters S and M enclosed in a circle.
morissette.not: The maker is Steve Morissette; pipes are stamped with the maker's initials (M over S), and no grading system is applied. See also Medici.

ehrlich.tn: Round wood inlay dot on the stem; single letter enclosed in a circle in the stamp.
ehrlich.not: The letters GB are the mark of George Bushee, a craftsman who worked at Ehrlich; pipes bearing this mark are his work.

sasieni-two-dot.tn: Two dots on the stem, the words "Two dot" on the body.
sasieni-two-dot.not: This stamp dates to the pre-transition period, 1961-1979. The "King Size" mark denotes the largest pipes Sasieni regularly sold, regardless of grade or finish. This stamp should not be confused with the double-stamped One dot mark.

jonas.tn: The stamp "Jonas" written in plain letters.
jonas.not: The brand was founded in 1966; the pipes came from the hand of maker Jonas Bianca. Made from Northern Italian briar, the pipes were sent mainly to Germany and the United States. Production ended in the early 1990s.

enrique.tn: Carries no separate logo; identified by the "D. Enrique" stamp on the underside.
enrique.not: David Enrique's workshop is part of the Chretin factory. Records also link it to Dunhill's LC series.

kaywoodie.tn: A plain round inlay on the stem; a clover-leaf motif in the stamp.
kaywoodie.not: Pipes stamped with a four-digit number are, per this numbering logic, dated to 1931-1938.

jacobean.tn: A logo of two letters inside a diamond shape, with the text "Jacobean" on the shank.
jacobean.not: Jacobean is the name of Leslie Wood's early production line, predating Ferndown.

goc.tn: A logo formed from the letters of the brand name.
goc.not: GOC is the brand of the Gros, Grenier, Ostorero et Cie factory, which has closed. See also Prior, OSA, and Sicana.

jirsa.tn: A stamp of a letter set inside a circle.
jirsa.not: Maker Goldrich Jirsa (b. 1962) has been making pipes since 1994.

vincenzo-lombardi.tn: The name "Vincenzo Lombardi" set on two lines together with a fleur-de-lis motif.
vincenzo-lombardi.not: This stamp is identical to that of Cellini, another Brebbia second brand. Other fleur-de-lis-marked stamps include Ajustomatic, Duke of Kent, Fleur de Lis, Harrington Park, Omega, and Thomas.

gert-konrad.tn: A single-color round dot on the stem.

da-vinci.tn: Star-shaped emblem; "Da Vinci" and "Master" lettering on the shank.

haddon-hall.tn: A single red dot on the stem.
haddon-hall.not: On the brand's pipes the stem dot is normally red; the color of the dot on the example examined may have faded.

rows: Haddon Hall, De Luxe, Made in London, England, 36

marxman.tn: Stamps combining an arrow motif with letters within a circle; on some examples, a bright stone set into the stem.
marxman.not: The brand was founded in 1934 and merged with Mastercraft in 1953. For the "Kings Cross" stamp, see also the brand of the same name and Savinelli's Kings Cross series.

rows: Marxman, Hand Carved, Imported Briar, Italy

kilimanjaro.tn: A stamp depicting a mammal figure.
kilimanjaro.not: One of the brands of the Tanganyika Meerschaum Corporation, under Amboseli Pipes. For other names under the same umbrella, see Countryman, Kiko, Kikob, Kudu, Merlin, Twiga, Sportsman.

jumbo.tn: A logo consisting of a letter enclosed in a circle; the words "Jumbo" and "Briar Italy" on the shank.

paronelli.tn: A single blue dot on the stem; the brand name "Paronelli" stamped together with anchor and pipe figures.

rows: Sardinian, [star] Briar, Hand Made in Italy

whitewall.tn: A single-letter logo; the stamp reads "Medico Whitewall Imported Briar."

the-guildhall.tn: A brand stamp bearing the name "The Guildhall."

straight-grain.tn: A single-letter logo; a grade letter stamped on the top surface.
straight-grain.not: Pipes in Savinelli's Straight Grain line are graded by letter. The brand's other graded lines are the Autograph, which uses numbers, and the early Giubileo d'Oro, which uses stars.

golden-square.tn: A stamp on the shank reading "Golden Square London Made".
golden-square.not: The brand of the London-based John Redman Ltd.

rows: Golden Square, London Made, Made in England 1077

dinwoodie.tn: Letters "KB & B" set within a clover, with "Dinwoodie" lettering arched above it.
dinwoodie.not: Dinwoodie is a brand KB&B began using in November 1919. The brand was discontinued before 1924, replaced by the Kaywoodie line.

westbrook.tn: The brand and maker's name on the left face; the model information along with a patent number on the right face.
westbrook.not: Records indicate this stamp belongs to one of the brand's earliest pipes, from its RJ Reynolds period.

weiner.tn: A logo consisting of a round wood inlay.
weiner.not: The brand's maker, Steve Weiner, died in 2002. The stamp number carries both a sequence and a year: the number 15598 indicates the 155th pipe carved in 1998. Records indicate that around 200-250 pipes per year were produced as of 2002.

jrgen-nielsen.tn: A single-dot mark; the words "Jørgen Nielsen" on the left side.
jrgen-nielsen.not: Jørgen Nielsen is the brother of Kai Nielsen and the son of Viggo Nielsen.

sasieni-10-dots-5-on-each-side.tn: Ten dots total, five on each face of the stem.
sasieni-10-dots-5-on-each-side.not: Dates to the transition period, 1979-1986; the lucite stem carries five dots on each face. Records indicate this model is also referred to as "Rare Smoke" in that source. See also "Superb Six".

rows: Perfect ten, London Made by Sasieni

seville.tn: Logo consisting of an "S" set horizontally or vertically.
seville.not: The Seville name was also used by the William Demuth Pipe Company (WDC) for one of its product lines.

el-morjane.tn: "El Morjane, El Kala - Algerie" lettering on the left side.

howal.tn: A logo of a letter set inside a circle.

caesar.tn: A crown figure on the stem.

gresham.tn: A diamond-shaped logo together with "Gresham" on the shank.

rows: Gresham Magnum, Made in London England, 810
Made in London (within a circle), England, 127

molina.tn: "Molina" wording on the left side; a pipe emblem is used within the stamp family.
molina.not: The brand's maker is Giovanni Carollo, formerly of the Rossi factory. Production is machine-made and done in series; the pipes are aimed mainly at the German and U.S. markets.

lincoln.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter enclosed in a circle along with a star motif.
