hans-fred-brandt.tn: No separate logo; "BRANDT" on the top face, and "FRED. BRANDT" with a star emblem on the underside.
hans-fred-brandt.not: The brand covers pipes carved by the father, Hans Brandt, and his architect son, Fred Brandt. The son's stamps are distinguished from the father's by the addition of "FRED." Records indicate that Hans Brandt's father, Frederik Brandt, also carved pipes and stamped them with the initials "FBR".

streamliner.not: Although the stamp looks the same as the one Weber used, the wording "Made in France" points to a different source of production. This pipe also lacks the aerodynamic shape distinctive of the pipes Weber sold under the Streamliner name.

ben-wade.tn: A target-shaped motif of concentric circles on the stem.
ben-wade.not: Records indicate the pipe from which this stamp was taken was never smoked, so the logo on the stem is considered original.

rows: Ben Wade Made in London England, IVORY

mark-tinsky.tn: Stamps consisting of an ornate circle, a letter group, and a star motif; on the left side, the text 'Mark Tinsky.'
mark-tinsky.not: Mark Tinsky and Curt Rollar founded The American Smoking Pipe Co. in 1978; Rollar left the company in 1990. Stamps include pipes dated 2001, carved for Pipes and Tobaccos magazine's pipe of the year and for members of the alt.smokers.pipes (A.S.P.) forum. In the "Reg n° 382" stamp, the letters G P M T correspond to a reading of the date March 1982 and the maker's name.

rows: American, Reg n° 382 G P M T

duncan.tn: Stamp elements consisting of a crown motif, a letter enclosed in a triangle, and the brand name.
duncan.not: The brand was founded in 1899 by John Louis Duncan. The founder's grandson, John Duncan, sold the brand to Peter Wilson in the 1990s. Duncan is counted among the brands producing filtered metal pipes.

samirva.tn: An animal figure alongside the text "Samirva Select."
samirva.not: Records suggest this may be a Charatan second-quality brand made during the Lane era. The same logo was also used on the Tobacco Pouch brand.

rows: Samirva Select, Made in, London England

savinelli-alligator.tn: 'Alligator' on the shank, with Savinelli's shield-shaped stamp on the underside.
savinelli-alligator.not: For other pipes with a similarly green body, see Peterson, Rainbow, and Rattray's.

holborn.tn: A single letter set inside a circle.

osma.tn: "OSMA" wording on the left side; the letters "RJ" within an oval on the band, together with English hallmarks.
osma.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's study, Osma may be a brand of the French company La Bruyère; given the company's history, the English hallmarks on the band do not contradict this possibility. The "RJ" within the oval is a silversmith's mark (recorded as Reuben Jordan), while the letter [g] is the London Assay Office's date letter for the year 1922.

city-de-luxe.tn: Hollow, silver-colored star on the stem.
city-de-luxe.not: The pipe features a patented mouthpiece design called "Tuskan Lip", with three draw holes at the bit. Another brand carrying the same design is Beau Nash. Records indicate the stem logo on the example stamped "T 182" is very rarely seen.

rows: City de Luxe, Made in England 357

lindner.tn: An animal figure is used in the stamp instead of a logo; one example shows a frog.
lindner.not: The number in the stamp gives the year of manufacture: a pipe stamped "01" dates from 2001, one stamped "2007" from 2007. On the second pipe, the grade "A 2" indicates a smooth (polished) finish, while the frog figure indicates the Magnum size.

hermes.tn: A logo of a single letter set inside an octagonal frame.
hermes.not: The production slip accompanying the pipe gives the date 1949 and names Jeantet as the maker; the octagonal logo is Jeantet's characteristic mark. For other luxury-brand pipes, see Gucci, Pierre Cardin, and Vuitton.

rosa-dei-venti.tn: Stamp in the shape of a star.

kaywoodie-super-grain.tn: "Super Grain" and "Kaywoodie" stamped one above the other on the left side.
kaywoodie-super-grain.not: The four-digit number stamp places production between 1931 and 1938; since the "Imported Briar" stamp came into use in 1935, the pipe can be dated to 1935-1938. On early Super Grain pipes, the "Super Grain" wording is stamped above the "Kaywoodie" wording.

rows: Kaywoodie (at the top) Super Grain, Imported Briar

greenwich.tn: "Greenwich" on the shank along with "Imported Briar".

persiani.tn: "Persiani" and "Italia" on the shank, series name on the left side.

alpha.tn: A single-letter logo; the stamps carry the 'Alpha' brand.
alpha.not: A brand of Shalom Pipe Co. For the same maker's other brands, see Mastersen, Mastercraft, and Mark V.

scandia.tn: Brand mark consisting of two letters; the shank carries the text "Scandia Fine Bruyere."
scandia.not: The pipes were made at Stanwell's workshops in Borup.

red-dot.tn: Round logo in the form of a solid ring.

savinelli-extra.tn: "Savinelli Extra" lettering accompanied by a crown emblem.
savinelli-extra.not: The same crown logo also appears on model 4001.

abdulla.tn: Single-letter stamp; "Abdulla Dribaccy, Patent" on the left side.
abdulla.not: One of the brands of Abdulla & Co Ltd.

stamford.tn: Stamp made of two letters; the shank carries the text "Stamford."
stamford.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell, pipes bearing the name "Stamford" were made by Sasieni as part of a series of English city names; this particular example, however, is not a Sasieni product. The same source notes that a "Stamford" brand may have been distributed in England by R. M. Littaur.

waverly.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.
waverly.not: This brand should not be confused with "Waverley," Sasieni's second brand.

markle.tn: No separate logo stamp; on the underside, the text 'MARKLE Pipes.'
markle.not: Maker Ernie Markle was born in 1978 and began pipe making in 2010. He progressed by working alongside Brad Pohlmann and Jeff Gracik.

sculptured-purex.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

royal-danish.tn: Stamp in the shape of a crown.
royal-danish.not: The brand is one of the second lines made at Stanwell's workshops in Borup; other names in the same group include Christian, Danish Natural, Danish Sovereign, Danske Club, Henley, Majestic, Royal Guard, and Scandia. The same crown logo is also used on Danish Natural.

botang.tn: A text stamp with the name "Botang" and the series name "Dead Root" on the underside.
botang.not: Records show the brand accompanied by the date 2002 and a memorial mark. Another joint work by the same makers is known under the name Gotang.

favorit.tn: Logo formed of a star-shaped element.

rettalb.tn: Two dots on the stem; "Rettalb" on the shank.
rettalb.not: The name Rettalb was formed by reversing the letters of the name Blatter.

nioe.not: According to records, the pipes were distributed by Intraflug AG or Transeurop Eisenbahn AG; these two Swiss companies successively operated the same famous train route.

sasieni-four-dot-appledore.tn: "Four Dot" series stamp and "Appledore" shape name on the underside.
sasieni-four-dot-appledore.not: A Four Dot stamp from the pre-transitional period (1946-1979). "Appledore" is a shape name; "Ruff Root" is the name given to the sandblasted finish.

two-brothers.tn: The inscription "兄弟烟斗" ("brothers pipe") on the left face.
two-brothers.not: The brand's shop is on Yandaixiejie street in Beijing, also known as "Pipe Street"; as of 2012 records, it was run by a Mr. Liu. The pipes are made from a wood known in Chinese as ji chi mu (鸡翅木), called "chicken wing wood" for its dense, feather-like grain. Botanically the wood belongs to the genus Ormosia.

rows: 兄弟烟斗 [兄弟 = brothers, 烟斗 = pipe]

moretti-2.tn: A crowned letter M on the stem; on some examples, a pipe figure accompanies the crowned M.
moretti-2.not: The maker of these pipes is Igino Moretti (d. 2005), father-in-law of Marco Biagini. Igino's stamps use capital letters, while Marco Biagini's stamps are handwritten.

kaywoodie-original.tn: "Kaywoodie" and "Original" wordings on the left side.
kaywoodie-original.not: This stamp points to production between 1961 and 1970.

nu-old.tn: A logo consisting of the brand name lettering.
nu-old.not: The Nu-Old brand was sold in Wally Frank stores in the 1960s. The same name is also used for one of Civic's series; see Civic.

emerson.tn: Letter-shaped logo enclosed in a circle.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England, 409

rouge-et-noir.tn: Stamp featuring a crown motif; the shank carries the text "Rouge et Noir."

rows: Rouge et Noir, Finest Briar Italy

stanton.tn: Stamp consisting of a single dot; the shank carries the text "Stanton."

alco.tn: A bird-shaped mark on the stem.
alco.not: The brand was produced in Britain by Merton and Falcon Co. Alco and Falcon bowls are not interchangeable.

dr-boston.tn: "Dr Boston" brand-name lettering together with a single-letter mark.
dr-boston.not: An export brand of the Berrod-Regad group, aimed chiefly at the German market with pipes fitted with 9 mm filters.

s-yanik.tn: No stamp on the meerschaum bowl; the brand name appears only on the underside of the stem.
s-yanik.not: The maker of these pipes is Sadık Yanık.

john-eells.tn: The signature "J H Eells" filled with white enamel on the stem.
john-eells.not: Maker John H. Eells's signature on the stem is engraved with a pen that tapers toward the tip and filled with white enamel, so that when the stem is polished the mark does not fade — instead it becomes more pronounced.

cragmoor.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the brand and country stamps arranged in a curve.
cragmoor.not: Linked to the BB&S record. According to Wilczak and Colwell's compilation, the brand is said to have been marketed by Britannia, though this information is not certain.

rows: 512, Cragmoor, London made, Made in England [curved]

cap-blanc.tn: A two-letter stamp; the words Chacom and Cap Blanc on the shank.

hickok.tn: A logo of a single letter; the text "Hickok" on the left face.
hickok.not: These leather-covered pipes are recorded as having been made for Hickok by the Belgian maker Hilson.

rows: Genuine Leather, Imported Briar, Made in Belgium

comoy-s-l-r-1904.tn: The letters "L.R" on the left side and the words "London Made" in an oval; London assay marks on the band.
comoy-s-l-r-1904.not: The assay marks on the band were struck at the London Assay Office.

skapi.tn: Instead of a separate logo, the word "SKAPI" is used on the left side.
skapi.not: The name SKAPI is an abbreviation of Skandinaviska Pipfabriken in Sweden.

newbok.tn: An initial stamp with the brand name given in plain lettering.

uhle-s.tn: A "U" letter together with horizontal bars on the stem.
uhle-s.not: The Uhle's pipe shop was founded by Jack Uhle in the 1930s. The business later passed to Jeff Steinbock, a former employee of Uhle's.

gefapip.tn: No logo description or stamp record on file.

sparkproof.tn: A stamp made up of "Sparkproof" and "Weatherproof" on the left side.
sparkproof.not: A pipe type intended for outdoor use, known as the "Hurricane."

falcon.tn: Logo featuring a bird of prey (falcon) figure.
falcon.not: The casting method originates in Ireland, though only part of the bowls were produced there. Other metal pipe brands featured on the site include Alco, Bryson, Dr Plumb, Duncan, Kaywoodie, Medico Ventilator, and Ornsby.

sasieni-coventry.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the line name and maker's stamp.

shamrock.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; one face carries the "Shamrock" stamp.

rows: Made in the Rep. of Ireland

danmore.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter.
danmore.not: The factory has closed; the brand's pipes were produced by third parties.

sasieni-stag.tn: "Stag" and "Sasieni" on the underside; the country stamp sits within a rugby-ball-shaped frame.

savinelli-2.tn: An architectural figure; the left face carries the line name "Melita," the right face the Savinelli crest.

savoy.tn: The left face carries the text "Savoy" and "Dr Grabow."

grading.tn: A record relating to the Wallenstein grading scale, without a separate logo.

sina.tn: Word logo formed from the letters of the brand name.
sina.not: Records associate the brand with the Maréchal Ruchon & Co factory.

savinelli-4001.tn: "Savinelli" in an oval on the underside, with a crown-crested shield emblem.
savinelli-4001.not: The four-digit shape number points to early Savinelli production; the same layout also appears on the Cadet and Capri lines. This crown logo was also used on the Extra line.

j-alan-pipes.tn: The text "J. Alan Pipes . USA ." set inside a circle on the underside, with the letter A inside a circle.
j-alan-pipes.not: Jeffrey A. Burt-Gracik (b. 1979) began carving pipes as a student in 2004 and moved to full-time production in 2006. The first number in the stamp gives the pipe's production order, and the two-digit number gives the year of production; for example, 231 08 denotes the 231st J. Alan pipe made in 2008. Grading is not used except for select examples marked with a wave symbol.

rows: J. Alan Pipes . USA . (within a circle)

e-oslo.tn: Carries no separate logo; "E. Oslo" lettering appears on the underside.
e-oslo.not: E. Oslo is Mic Burns's secondary brand. The pipes are not made from scratch; standard-shaped pipes from Italian or English makers are reworked by the craftsman.

samson.tn: The underside carries the "Samson" stamp spelled out in the letters of the brand name.

atlantic.tn: A stamp of an anchor emblem together with a single letter set within a circle.

vollmer-nilsson.tn: No logo stamp on the stem; the words "Vollmer & Nilsson" on the left face of the body.
vollmer-nilsson.not: The brand comes from stepbrothers Martin Vollmer and Anders Nielsson, who have worked together since 2001. Pipes are not graded or dated; there is no mark in the stamp distinguishing the two makers. The pair each also hold stamps registered in their own names.

ruth.tn: No pictorial logo; the stamp consists only of the maker's name.
ruth.not: Pipes are usually stamped with a five-digit number.

jacono.tn: The text "Jacono" used together with a bar motif.
jacono.not: The brand's maker, Tonino Jacono, is the brother-in-law of Vitaliano Posella. Grading is based on chess pieces, rising in order through Knight, Bishop, Rook, Jack, Queen, and King; the letter "E" denotes surface finish, and "Checkmate" denotes an unusually large size. Starting in 2011 the year of production has been stamped as a two-digit number, and that same year a silver logo began appearing on stems.

rows: Jacono, Hand Made in Italy, Queen

zettervig.not: The maker of these pipes was Ole Zettervig, who died in 2010. The workshop is in Kolding, Denmark.

the-academy-award.tn: A cup-shaped emblem on the stem.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) , England, 30

negarville.not: Records indicate this is the brand of an importer active in Turin during the 1980s.

starkov.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries "Starkov" set between two lines.
starkov.not: Maker Boris Starkov was born in 1982 and took up pipemaking full-time in 2009. His pipes carry no grade or date stamp.

gracik.tn: No stamp or logo data on record.

pohlmann.tn: A logo-free stamp; the lower left side has the arched wording "Handmade By Pohlmann", with the country and state name below it.

holtorp.tn: No separate logo; the text "Holtorp Handmade Denmark" on the underside.
holtorp.not: Maker P. Holtorp was, in the 1960s, one of the regular pipe carvers for Pipe-Dan in Copenhagen.

robert-s.tn: Logo made up of a diamond motif.
robert-s.not: Resembles the logos of the Coronado and Union brands.

gbp.tn: A logo formed from a crown motif and the letters "GBP".
gbp.not: The abbreviation GBP comes from the initials of Great Britain Pipes.

monterey.tn: The letters KBB set within a clover leaf.
monterey.not: The number 55 on the stamp (bent billiard) matches Kaywoodie's shape numbering within KB&B's system; the Carburetor patent number 2082106 is also the patent used on Kaywoodie's Carburetor pipes made from 1948 onward. Records indicate this suggests that manzanita-bodied pipes stamped Mission Briar continued to be produced well after the Second World War, once the briar supply had returned to normal.

rows: KBB [within a clover], Monterey, Specimen Briar

leslie-wood.tn: A letter logo combined with a crown motif.
leslie-wood.not: The pipes are made by craftsman Leslie (Les) Wood. Pipes going to the European market are stamped "L. Wood", those going to the U.S. "Ferndown"; combined annual output for both brands is about 2000 pipes. For the origin of the logo, see also Elwood.

courrieu.not: Records indicate the figure in the logo represents Vercingetorix.

terminus.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.
terminus.not: The pipe carries the anti-clog system patented by Jean Masson.

converti.tn: "Converti" and "Serie III" lettering on the shank.
converti.not: Because the "Serie III" wording in the stamp resembles Mauro's "Serie II" stamp, the brand is thought to be Armellini's second-quality line.

danske-club.tn: Logo consisting of two letters; "Danske Club" stamp on the shank.
danske-club.not: Production took place at Stanwell's workshops in Borup.

thermofilter.tn: The "Thermofilter" stamp, made up of a letter within a circle.

alexej-kharlamov.tn: An ornamented round inlay on the stem.
alexej-kharlamov.not: The pipes are made by master carver Alexey Kharlamov. Grading rises in the order E, D, C, B, A; records indicate the mark on the stem was discontinued some time before 2010.

house-of-lords.tn: A logo of a crown figure used together with bar motifs.
house-of-lords.not: The brand belongs to Samuel Gordon. Records suggest it may be one of Sasieni's second-grade lines.

rows: House of Lords, Made in England
House of Lords, De Luxe, Made in England

simplex.tn: Multi-letter word logo; the left face carries the words "Simplex" and "Unbreakable."

h-r-h.tn: A multi-letter logo on the stem.
h-r-h.not: The stem logo and stamps identify this pipe as a version of Sasieni's "His Royal Highness" sub-brand; examples bearing the same logo along with a "Sasieni Made" stamp confirm this link.

chp-x.not: Maker Michael V. Kabik began making pipes in the early 1970s and stopped in 1989-90. The brand name comes from Chuck Holiday, who left the workshop in 1971, with Kabik taking his place. The workshop closed in 1973; Kabik later produced the Sven-Lar brand together with Glen Hedelson.

esseti-toma.tn: "Esseti Toma" lettering on the left side, "Suprema" wording on the right side.
esseti-toma.not: A tobacconist's private label; the pipes were most likely produced at the Barontini workshop in Livorno. Records are not certain that Salvatore Toma is the person the label was named after.

casseloni.not: Records link the brand to Calypso in Israel.

aksenov.tn: Letter A combined with a pipe emblem on the underside.
aksenov.not: The pipes are made by Yuri Aksenov, born 1964; he has worked part-time since around 2009. He paused production for a time in 2011 due to health issues.

amarcord.tn: A logo consisting of three dots.
amarcord.not: Pipes belonging to the Pesaro school.

smoker-friendly.tn: A two-letter logo; "Smoker Friendly" on the shank.
smoker-friendly.not: The house brand of the "Smoker Friendly" tobacconist chain. As of 2008 the chain had about 600 stores across the United States.

royal-dutch.tn: Stamp in the shape of a crown.
royal-dutch.not: The pipes are a Royal Dutch Pipe Factory product; see Big Ben, Roermond, and Amphora.

rows: Royal Dutch Sandgrain Importec Briar 1611 R Made in Holland

ronson.tn: Logo consisting of two dots and a single letter.
ronson.not: A brand of Ronson Corp., known for its lighters. Other lighter brands that also distributed pipes include Flamidor, Myon, S.T. Dupont, and Silver Match.

vacher.tn: A logo on the underside alongside the word "Vacher."

admiral.tn: Single-letter stamp; "Admiral, De Luxe, 5" on the shank.

wally-frank.tn: Variable stamps appear on the stem: a single blue or red dot, two dots, a bar, a star, or a letter in a circle.
wally-frank.not: The brand was founded in 1930. Through the "Pipe of the Month Club," members received a new pipe by mail once a month. Pipes were sourced from English, French, Danish, Italian, and American makers.

rows: Wally Frank Limited Made in London England 53
Wally Frank Limited, The Macauley, Briar warranty, Made in England 36

park-lane.tn: The letters "LHS" within a diamond-shaped frame, with "Park Lane" next to it.

rows: Park Lane, LHS [within a diamond], De Luxe

empire.tn: Logo said, per records, to resemble a sun rising over water.

rows: Empire, de Luxe, London Style, 59 L

buescher-s.tn: The word "Buescher's" on the underside together with a Washington, Missouri production notice.
buescher-s.not: Buescher's, based in Washington, Missouri, made pipes from hickory wood. This example's bowl follows the shape of some corncob pipe models.

english-pride.tn: Monogram-style logo made of two letters.

rows: English Pride, Made in London, England

champion.tn: Letter "C" with a dot above and below it.

garrick.tn: Single letter enclosed in a circle on the stem.

blatter.tn: Colored dots struck on the stem; the number and color of the dots indicate the pipe's type of manufacture and period.
blatter.not: Blatter & Blatter Inc. has made pipes in Montreal since 1907, according to records; one of its makers was Robert Blatter. Dot color aids dating: after a pre-1964 factory period, green dots were used 1964-1967, and red dots after 1968. A single red dot marks a machine-made pipe, red paired with a gray dot marks an exceptional machine-made pipe with fine grain, and two red dots mark a limited hand-made pipe; see also Rettalb.

rows: Blatter Bros (in Gothic lettering), Make, Montreal, Selected, 51.77

refbjerg.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; "Refbjerg" on the shank.

gregg-peevey.tn: A single red dot on the stem.

carsipe.tn: A two-dot inlaid mark on the stem.
carsipe.not: Master Carlos Royo i Porta (b. 1955) began pipemaking in 2007. Output is approximately 30 pipes a year.

christian.not: The pipes were produced at Stanwell's workshops in Borup. Model number 11 shares the same size and shape as Stanwell's identically numbered shape.

duke-of-dundee.tn: Double D letters separated by a diagonal line within a circle.
duke-of-dundee.not: This example is made not of wood but of a bakelite-type material; a valve beneath the bowl regulates airflow. In 1953, Henry Leonard & Thomas acquired the Royal Duke, Duke of Dundee, and Honeydew brands, previously produced by the Continental Briar Pipe Co. of Brooklyn.

savinelli-gold.not: For other lines carrying shape number 623, see Molinella and Sherwood.

ivan-holst-nielsen.tn: The maker's name set inside a circle on the right face.
ivan-holst-nielsen.not: Ivan Holst Nielsen was a well-known pipe maker in the late 1960s and 1970s. After a long hiatus he resumed pipe making around 2008.

beldor.tn: A logo of a single letter within a circle, with a ring motif.

londoner.tn: A letter-shaped logo on the stem; some examples use a single letter, others a letter group.
londoner.not: After the Barling brand left the family in 1962, pipes — especially the brand's second-quality production — were made in France, Italy, and Denmark; this example is Danish-made. See also BB&S and Cragmoor.

hjerte-brier.tn: No separate logo; the underside bears the brand name along with the city and country name.

amalfi.tn: A logo of bars arranged side by side; the stamp reads 'Illenhall Amalfi.'

9104.tn: "Brebbia Italy" brand and model number 9104 on the underside.
9104.not: Brebbia's logo changed from the MPB (Manifatture Pipe Brebbia) abbreviation to a plain diamond shape in 1968; a pipe bearing this stamp predates that change.

kaywoodie-liberty-bell.tn: The words "Liberty Bell Commemorative by Kaywoodie" on the shank.
kaywoodie-liberty-bell.not: The pipe was made in 1976 for the 200th anniversary of American independence. See also the pipe produced for the 200th anniversary of the French Revolution.

pipas-o.tn: No separate logo; "Pipas + O" on the underside.
pipas-o.not: Maker Félix Massó-Milleiro began making pipes in 2008. The brand has no grading system, nor is there a stamp for dating the pipes.

titan.tn: No logo; the words "Made in England" and "TITAN Pats Pend" on the underside.
titan.not: The briar bowl attaches by screwing onto a threaded fitting seated in the center of the metal cup; the shank and cup are stainless steel. The pipes were sold with interchangeable bowls in six different shapes, offered in either smooth or rusticated finish.

kaj-rasmussen.tn: A multi-letter mark on the stem.
kaj-rasmussen.not: The brand belongs to Danish maker Kaj C. Rasmussen. Poul Rasmussen, Anne Julie Rasmussen, and Kent Rasmussen, who share the same surname, are separate pipe makers.

match.tn: The text "Match" and the wording "St Claude" on the shank.

monte-verdi.tn: A letter logo set beneath a crown.
monte-verdi.not: The maker of these pipes is Preben Holm (d. June 8, 1989).

rows: Monte Verdi, Made in Denmark, By Hand, Golden Tan

barok.tn: A single-letter logo; the left face bears the stamp 'Barok.'
barok.not: Records link the brand to Stanwell.

glaus.tn: A logo formed from a triangular motif.

sasieni-mayfair.tn: A single-letter logo within a coat of arms.

rows: Sasiεni Mayfair, Made in England (curved), London Made, 95

peterson-peterson-1895.tn: Cursive "Peterson's" between diamond shapes and a patent number on the left side.
peterson-peterson-1895.not: Peterson's distinguishing feature is the gap between the shank and the stem; the slightly tapered tenon ensures a tight fit even as the wood or stem material expands, and lets the stem be removed and refitted while the pipe is still hot. In the early years, horn condensers were used in the Deluxe and Premier series, giving way to Bakelite in the 1940s and to aluminum today.

sutliff.tn: "SUTLIFF San Fransisco" on the shank and a "Made in England" stamp within a circle.
sutliff.not: Records suggest this pipe may be Comoy production.

keith-owen.tn: A mark of a single letter set inside a circle; the text "Keith Owen" on the left face.

d-p-pipes.tn: "D & P. Genuine Briar" lettering on the left face.
d-p-pipes.not: D & P Pipe Works was a business owned by D. P. Levitas, located in Sparta, Alleghany County, North Carolina. The company was first named Sparta Pipe Works, then Sparta Industries; the factory produced Trapwell pipes.

s-s-pierce.tn: Word stamp formed from the letters of the brand name; some examples show a letter "R" set in a circle.
s-s-pierce.not: The history of the S.S. Pierce & Co brand goes back at least to 1831; the company ceased operations in the early 1980s. Records indicate the pipes were made by Savinelli.

rows: S.S. Pierce Co, Overland, Made in England 250
R (within a circle) Round Table, Assembly W
S.S. Pierce Co, Made in England, 363

tivoli.tn: A single-letter logo; the words "Centura Tivoli" on the top face.
tivoli.not: Records indicate Tivoli may be a sub-brand of L H Stern; Centura appears as a label used by Yello-Bole.

anima.tn: An ornate round dot of red clay (kaolinite) inlaid in the stem.
anima.not: Made by Brian McNulty; the red clay dot in the stem is the "soul" symbol that gives the brand its name. Grade is shown by one to four circled crosses in ascending order, while the source of the briar is indicated by a letter: S for Spain, M for Morocco, C for Calabria. Dating relies on the month-and-year stamp struck on the shank.

moth.not: One of the Oppenheimer group's brands, alongside BBB, Civic, Comoy, GBD, Loewe, and Orlik. Records indicate the pipes were made at the now-closed Marechal, Ruchon & Co factory in Saint-Claude, France.

stanhope.tn: Stamp made of multiple letters; the shank carries the text "Stanhope."
stanhope.not: The brand belongs to L&H Stern.

sir-bruce.tn: Logo consisting of a letter and a triangle motif within a circle; the left face carries the text "Sir Bruce."
sir-bruce.not: Records indicate this is one of Jeantet's sub-brands; other brands in the same group include Duke of Kent, Grand Duke, Hermes, and Sir Duke. Other brands sharing the same logo are Luxor and Lord.

sommer.tn: The wording "Sommer Paris" used together with a sun emblem; the stamp includes ornate circle and bar motifs.

kulpinski.tn: "R. Kulpinski, Poland" on the left side, a model number on the right side.
kulpinski.not: Maker Ryszard Kulpinski worked together with Ryszard Filar between 1981 and 1983.

piazzolla.tn: Two-letter logo; the stamp reads "P. Piazzola, Confrere Pipier".
piazzolla.not: The pipes are made by Pascal Piazzolla; his workshop is in the village of Aviernoz, France. Records indicate the pipes use a magnetic joint.

joura.tn: The word "JOURA" on the underside, used together with plant and infinity emblems.
joura.not: Pipes stamped with the infinity symbol belong to the "Infinity" series; the letter beside it indicates the grade. C.A.O. International Inc. was for a time the U.S. distributor of Joura pipes, and these pipes are stamped "Exclusively for CAO" within a diamond.

rows: [Plant: indicates the source of the briar]

learned.tn: A crescent-moon emblem intertwined with the letters L and S on the underside.

jet-pipe.tn: A bird-figure logo with the text "Jet Pipe".
jet-pipe.not: Pipes stamped "Century Old" were generally made by Lorenzo for the US market. For other names carrying the same stamp, see Lloyds, T.V., and Century Old.

bonet.tn: A stamp outlining the island of Mallorca.
bonet.not: The pipes were made by Joan Bonet i Nadal, born 1929 and known as 'Bonet de ses pipes'; the maker is now retired. The name is struck in block letters on the stamp, and the maker has written four books on pipes: Les rondalles de la pipa (1978), ...I fumant en pipa (1981), Pipades i vivències (1983), and Las Pipas (1989). See also Johan Kock for another stamp using an island silhouette.

royal-dental.tn: Stem stamp consisting of a single letter.
royal-dental.not: The letter logo on the stem together with the "Popular" stamp on the right face of the shank link the brand to Duncan.

rows: Popular, Made in England, Pat. No 382443

merton.not: Merton is the former brand of Harold Merton, who had a factory in Saint-Claude, France. See also Paul Guilland Merton.

rows: Merton, Bruyere fine de St. Claude

comoy-s-guildhall.tn: A logo of a single letter and bars on the stem.
comoy-s-guildhall.not: The stamp belongs to Comoy's "Guildhall" line. See also Everyman, The Lumberman, The Mansion House.

rows: Made in London (within a circle), England, F126

son.tn: The wording "SON" formed from the brand name's letters.
son.not: The brand arose from the two-year partnership between Søren Skovbo and Erik Nording in the 1960s.

heibe.tn: A plain, single-color round dot on the stem.

freestyle.tn: Letters BBB set within a diamond shape.

greaves.tn: A script stamp reading "Greaves" formed from the letters of the brand name.
greaves.not: Greaves is the brand of the Marechal Ruchon company, which later took the name C.G. Verguet Frères and operated under the Oppenheimer Holding group. The stem shape resembles Peterson's P-Lip design, but the hole is drilled straight through and does not direct smoke toward the palate; similar stems are also found on Bontemps pipes.

rows: Greaves, Patent (curved) Extra, Made in France

sasieni-lords-of-london.tn: A "Made in England" stamp arranged in the shape of a rugby ball on the underside.

royal-duke.tn: Stamp in the shape of a rhombus.
royal-duke.not: The Royal Duke line was launched in 1969.

savinelli-non-pareil.tn: Usually two, rarely a single dot on the stem.
savinelli-non-pareil.not: In the Non Pareil line, the shape code has three or four digits; this falls outside Savinelli's usual three-digit shape code system.

pool-smythe.tn: Brand stamp made up of several letters; "Pool & Smythe Ltd" on the underside.
pool-smythe.not: The brand appears in the 1979 catalog of the US tobacconist Tinderbox.

rows: Pool & Smythe Ltd, Magnum, Made in London, England, 804

sren-holm.tn: The name "Søren Holm" and a single-letter grade stamp on the underside.
sren-holm.not: Grading runs from lowest to highest as D, C, B, A.

barrister.tn: A logo featuring two dots and an arrow element.
barrister.not: Pipes bearing this stamp were finished in France and distributed in the US by L & H Stern. See also Britannia.

caminetto.tn: A mustache-shaped inlaid mark on the stem; the word Caminetto on the shank.
caminetto.not: A thin mustache inlay points to the early Caminetto period, a thicker one to the later period. The stamps list Cucciago, in the province of Como, as the place of manufacture.

rows: Caminetto Business 121, Handmade in Italy Cucciano (Co)
(Coat of arms) Ascorti, Radice, Cucciago, Cantu - Italy, KS

morris.tn: A single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.

garnet-grain.tn: "BARLING London England" and "Garnet Grain" on the shank.

bittner.not: The pipes came from master K. Bittner.

l-artigiana.tn: A logo consisting of a letter enclosed in a circle; the stamp reads "L'Artigiana".

bjarne.tn: The word 'Bjarne' on the shank; no separate logo on the stem.
bjarne.not: Pipes made in Copenhagen are graded and stamped accordingly; a single letter struck on the underside indicates the pipe's grade.

conway.tn: Single letter enclosed within a circle on the stem.
conway.not: Conway pipes are widely accepted to have been made by Singleton & Cole; this is reinforced in examples carrying a shape number. According to Wilczak and Colwell's record, Loewe also had a line called Conway.

rows: 91 Conway Standard, Made in London, England

royal-british.tn: Stamp in the shape of a crown.

frederiksen.tn: Letters N and F set within a pipe-shaped mark.
frederiksen.not: Danish craftsman Nils Frederiksen (b. 1953) first worked as a wood turner. He began making pipes in 1992 and trained under Tom Eltang.

hettinger-s.tn: A logo of a single letter; the shank bears the text "Hettinger's".

plm.tn: A stamp formed from the letters of the brand name: "PLM".

art-craft.tn: A stamp of a single letter set within a circle.
art-craft.not: A brand of the Art-Craft Pipe Co. The same maker's other brand is Anzio.

duca.tn: Crown motif and the brand name "Duca" lettering.

orlik.tn: A stamp combining ring and concentric-circle target motifs with anchor and crown emblems.
orlik.not: This is one of the Cadogan company's brands, alongside BBB, Civic, Comoy, GBD, and Loewe. The cross-shaped logo appears only occasionally on Orlik stems. See also Hurricane, Royal Sovereign.

rows: Orlik Giant Made in England GX22
Orlik Hurricane, Made in England, X 77

leeds-period.tn: The words "Ben Wade" in an oval on the left side.
leeds-period.not: These stamps belong to the pre-Lane period, when Ben Wade pipes were made in Leeds, England.

rows: Ben Wade (within an oval), Selected Grain

gottschling.tn: A stamp on the underside giving the maker's name, "Handmade", and country of origin; no logo on the stem.
gottschling.not: Dieter Gottschling is one of the German makers who settled in Denmark; for a similar case, see Ingo Garbe.

rustique.not: The same arrow logo is also used on the Shelton Square brand.

utor.not: The brand's maker was Uwe Thormann. Production ended in the late 1970s.

pastuch.tn: No separate emblem is used; the stamp consists of the words "W. Pastuch" and "Hand Made" on the underside.
pastuch.not: The pipes are made by the craftsman Wojtek Pastuch. The brand has no grading system.

sans-tare.tn: The shank carries the two-word text "Sans Tare."
sans-tare.not: The French phrase "sans tare" means flawless. The "St Claude France" stamp on this pipe is identical to the one seen on examples marked Madame.

1921-hallmark.tn: Curved "Barling" text on the shank, initials and hallmarks on the silver band.
1921-hallmark.not: The initials E.B and W.B on the band denote Edward Barling and William Barling. The date letter [f] indicates the piece was assayed by the London Assay Office in 1921.

hawthorne.tn: A logo of a single letter set inside a circle; the stamp reads "Hawthorne, Imported Briar".

lamberthod.tn: There is no separate inlaid logo; the stamp consists solely of the word "Lamberthod" on the left side.
lamberthod.not: The brand's pipes were produced using a duplicating machine. Records associate the brand with the name Louis Lamberthod.

meier-frank.not: Meier & Frank was the name of a department store chain founded in 1857 in Portland, Oregon, USA, which later closed.

sasieni.tn: Colored dots inlaid on the stem, their number (one, two, four, five, or ten) varying by line.
sasieni.not: Sasieni stamps fall into three periods: pre-transition (1919-1979), transitional (1979-1986), and post-transition (1986 to present); the number of dots on the stem identifies the line. The script "Sasieni" signature was changed by Alfred Sasieni after the Second World War, and from 1986 the "FOUR DOT" stamp was replaced by "4DOT." The double-row, two-dot model appears in the 1939 catalog but not in the 1936 or 1943 catalogs; these examples are noted as using Algerian briar, with "Ruff Root" being the name of the sandblasted finish.

rows: The Alternative, London made, by Sasieni
Sasiεni, Four Dot, London Made, Made in England
Sasieni 4DOT Ruff Root Dark Made in London [within a circle] F , 5

claessen.tn: No logo; the underside carries the curved lettering 'Claessen', an emblem, and the word 'Pipes'.

askwith.tn: A stamp bearing a five-petaled English rose plant motif.
askwith.not: The maker is Chris Askwith. Until 2010 the pipes were stamped with the maker's initials and the year of production; after 2010 only the 'Askwith' stamp was used. The grading, which rose from zero to three silver dots, was discontinued in 2010.

sunway.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle.

rows: Sunway, De Luxe, Made in Denmark

herreria.tn: A monogram of the letters H and E on the left face.
herreria.not: The maker of these pipes is Ezequiel Herreria, born in 1977; he carved his first pipe in 2009 and began selling his work in 2010. According to 2013 figures his annual output is about 80 pipes.

sticker-variants-under-the-bowl.tn: An entry collecting label variants affixed under the bowl.

cannoy.tn: No separate logo; the maker's name, a serial number, and grade are stamped on the underside.
cannoy.not: Walt Cannoy sold his first pipe in 1999. The serial number gives the date the pipe was finished; the stamp 042204 means April 22, 2004. The surface letters C, A, J, and M denote smooth, carved, sandblasted, and mixed finishes respectively; grading rises from 1 to 6.

rovera.tn: An ornamented round stamp on the stem.
rovera.not: The maker, Damiano Rovera, is the son of Dorielo Rovera; see Ardor and Angelo. Other brands using a map-shaped logo are Bonet and Johan Koch.

rows: Daniano Rovera, Pietra, Italy, Fatta a Mano

breezewood.tn: The "Breezewood" stamp, with the brand name given in plain script.

onyx.tn: A letter logo enclosed in a circle; the stamp reads "Medico", "Onyx", and "Brylon".
onyx.not: Brylon is a synthetic material developed by S.M. Frank Co in 1966; it is made from a mixture of heat-resistant resin and wood flour. Compared to briar, this material is cheaper and more crack-resistant, but it is heavier and heats up more during smoking. The same company also used Brylon for the Yello-Bole brand.

peterson-k-p.tn: The letters "K&P" enclosed in a circle.

chap.tn: Logo consisting of the brand name enclosed within a ring.
chap.not: The brand was founded in 1920 by the Chapel brothers. After a period under Gefapip, it passed to the Berrod-Regad group in 1988. Production took place at the Chapel Frères & Cie factory.

tortuga-babes.tn: An embossed turtle figure on silver, along with the letters "T B."
tortuga-babes.not: The pipes are made by Achim Menzel, who works in Recklinghausen.

vottis.tn: A single letter stamped within a circle on the stem.
vottis.not: This is the brand of maker Pat Vottis. Production ended in the early 1970s.

wilhelm-tell.tn: A logo consisting of a single blue dot; the stamp "Wilhelm Tell Bruyere" on the left face.

velani.tn: The stamp of the Velani brand; no detailed record data available.

viking.tn: The words "Big-Ben" and "Viking" on the left face.
viking.not: This Viking stamp appears on Big-Ben-made Dutch pipes. For another brand of the same name, see Viking (Bjarne).

le-pipier-de-lunel.tn: A fleur-de-lis-shaped logo and the name "J Waille".
le-pipier-de-lunel.not: Maker Jean Waille is the son of André Waille, a pipe maker from Saint-Claude, and the nephew of Michel Waille, owner of the EWA brand. Records indicate Captain Patty is also his second brand. For other brands using the fleur-de-lis logo, see Ajustomatic, Cellini, Duke of Kent, Fleur de lis, Omega, Thomas, Vincenzo Lombardi.

becker-3.tn: The letters B and W stacked inside a circle, with two paw prints.

rows: B (at the top) W (at the bottom), daire içinde

stefano.tn: A crown-shaped stamp; "Stefano Exclusive" on the left side.
stefano.not: An export brand aimed at the German market.

calibano.tn: A round wooden inlaid mark on the stem; the word Calibano within a band on the left face.

ardor.tn: Two dots and a solid-ring logo on the stem.
ardor.not: The brand name comes from the makers' initials: AR (Angelo Rovera) and DOR (Dorelio Rovera). The two-dot "Venere" stamp marks the top grade of production; records indicate only one in every 250-300 pipes carries this stamp. See also Fe-Ro ("Figli di Federico Rovera"), Rovera, and Roverart.

rows: Dorielo, Rovera, Ardor, Venere, 2 P, Italy, Fatta a Mano, 2007
DR Ardor Urano Italy Fatta a mano
Ardor Mercurio Italy, Fatta a mano, 2006
Ardor, Giove, Italy, Fatta a mano, Fantasy, 2006
On the underside of the stem

sasieni-2-dots-1-on-each-side.tn: One dot on each face of the stem.
sasieni-2-dots-1-on-each-side.not: A pre-transition layout, dating 1920-1939, known as the doubled single dot. The phrase "Specially Selected By" indicates that Joel Sasieni himself selected the pipe for release under the side-dot logo. Records indicate this rare form is a holdover from the brand's logo experiments of the 1920s.

rows: Sasieni (fishtail cursive) London Made, PAT. No. 150221/20
Specially selected (curved), by, Sasieni (fishtail cursive) London Made, PAT.N°150221/20, Made in England (curved)

heyl.tn: The text "GER RIT" set between lines on the underside, with a lily emblem and the letter beta.
heyl.not: The pipes are made by Gerrit Heyl.

sasieni-pickwick.tn: Besides the name "Pickwick", the stamp carries the wording "London Made" and "Made in England".

rows: 19, Pickwick, London Made, Made in England, by Sasieni

country-club.not: See also the Town Club and Royale records.

rows: Country Club London made, Made in England 9465

kaywoodie-regent.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; "Kaywoodie" and "Regent" on the left side.
kaywoodie-regent.not: This stamp was used between 1963 and 1972. The Regent model was regularly produced with a Cumberland stem.

peabody.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle.
peabody.not: An English brand; its maker is unknown.

london-royal.not: Other brands using a hat-shaped logo include Churchill, Lobbia, Man About Town, and Sabatini. Records link the brand to the LHS factory in Brooklyn; this information relies on Wilczak and Colwell's study.

dr-hardy.tn: Concentric rings resembling a target, along with "Dr Hardy" brand-name lettering.
dr-hardy.not: Records mention examples with leather-covered bodies; the stamps indicate production was carried out by Tagliabue.

becker-2.tn: A logo formed by two pipes merging into the letter 'P'.
becker-2.not: The earliest Becker stamps were hand-engraved by the maker; this method was replaced by true stamps around 1985–86. The 'R / Paul Becker / Handarbeit' stamp was used until 2003, after which the two-pipe 'P'-shaped logo stamp was adopted (per a 2011 record).

beau-nash.not: The model uses a three-hole stem called the 'Tuskan Lip'; the same patented design also appears on some models of GBD's secondary brand City De Luxe. Other brands with two-hole stems include Grand Master, Kaywoodie Allbriar and Durobit, Leonard's, Radice, Siam, and Twin Bore.

trocadero.tn: "ROPP" within an oval, with the name "Trocadero" beside it.

peterson-avon.tn: A single-letter logo; the left face bears the stamp "Avon."
peterson-avon.not: The pipe was made in England. It is connected to the Captain Peterson records, which bear the same "A \"Peterson\" product" stamp.

pax.tn: A stamp consisting of the brand name on the stem.
pax.not: One of the Wolf Bros. company's brands.

mastro-beraldi.tn: A single dot on the stem; the text "Mastro Beraldi" on the shank.
mastro-beraldi.not: The maker of the brand is Aldo Pierluigi. Records indicate that the name "Mario Grandi," begun in 2006, was used for the brand's lower-priced pipes.

magner.tn: On the underside, the words 'Magner,' 'Handmade,' and 'Canada' set between short dashes.
magner.not: Canadian maker Colm Magner (b. 1961) began carving pipes in 1998. He is also an actor who has appeared in films and television series shot in Toronto.

gloredo.not: One of the brand's founders is Leslie Ng, referred to in the stamp by the abbreviation "L.NG". The brand name derives from a combination of GLORY and DO (Hall). Grading rises in the order 1, 3, 6, and 9.

rows: Gloredo Hand Made, [Chinese ideogram] Humility, 9, L.NG

liskey.tn: On the underside, the text 'S. Liskey' and the initials LS; there is no separate logo stamp.
liskey.not: The pipes were made by maker Steve Liskey.

cambridge.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's compilation, this English name can be linked to several different makers or sellers, including Hall & Fitzgerald, Comoy, GBD, and John Aylesbury. The same logo is also seen on the Passat brand.

kaywoodie-fine-line.tn: A stamp on the left side reading "Kaywoodie" and "Fine Line".
kaywoodie-fine-line.not: The Fine Line model's period runs from 1956 to 1976. The model was also produced in England.

wembley.tn: A single-letter logo; the brand name and place of manufacture appear on the body.

walls.tn: A single dot on the stem.

lord-clive.tn: A coat-of-arms (shield) logo on the stem.

rinaldi.tn: Two-letter inlay on the stem; "J. Rinaldi" on the underside.
rinaldi.not: Maker Jon Rinaldi was formerly a photographer and began making pipes in the early 2000s.

early-patent-pipe.tn: Letters BBB set within a diamond.
early-patent-pipe.not: Carries the early red diamond logo.

challenger.tn: Logo consisting of two letters on the stem.

heckmann.tn: Letters "Hh" set within a diamond-shaped field; the stamp also includes a crown figure.

john-sterling.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem; a brand-name stamp on the top face.
john-sterling.not: John Sterling is an export brand; the pipes are made at the Chapuis-Comoy factory in Saint-Claude, France.

passat.tn: A stamp with a crown above the lettering.
passat.not: A valve set into the underside of the bowl is designed to regulate airflow. The same mechanism appears in the Duke of Dundee, Kaywoodie Carburetor, Dunhill Airstream, and Steel's brands. The same logo is used on the Cambridge brand.

kingsway-2.tn: A crown figure combined with a letter.
kingsway-2.not: The same logo also appears on Knute of Denmark, Karl Erik's second brand, and on the Scott brand.

mark-v.tn: On the top, the text 'Mark V' and 'Made in U.S.A.'

savinelli-melita.tn: A logo with architectural elements; the Savinelli coat of arms appears on the right side.
savinelli-melita.not: For a similar, possibly identical logo, see Honey-Swete and La Ruche.

corsican-briar.tn: Logo consisting of a crown-shaped emblem.
corsican-briar.not: The pipes were made in France for the US market; records indicate they were sold by Mastercraft. The same crown logo also appears on the Royal Ascot brand.

balleby.tn: A triangular-motif logo; the stamp reads "Balleby, Hand Made, Denmark."
balleby.not: The maker is Kurt Balleby. A silver dot is inlaid at the junction of the shank and the bowl. Grading rises in the order sandblasts, C, B, A, and Select; annual production is about 200–250 pipes.

bolton.tn: A stamp made up of a letter enclosed in a circle together with a star motif.
bolton.not: Seen on pipes with leather-covered bodies.

albatross.tn: A bird-shaped mark on the stem.
albatross.not: The same bird mark also appears on the Savinelli Sport brand.

cassano.tn: An anchor-shaped inlaid mark on the stem together with a plain round dot.
cassano.not: The anchor mark on this model is set into the stem as an inlay; records describe it as an embossed metal piece.

hartmann.tn: A logo of a single letter; the underside bears "Hartmann, Design" and a circular "Hand made in Denmark" stamp.
hartmann.not: The brand of Hans Hartmann, now retired from production. Early in his career he sold his pipes through the Pipe-Dan shop. Grading runs from A, the best, down to E, below which come the HH1-HH4 lines.

comoy-s-virgin-briar.tn: The scripted word "Comoy's" on the left face, with the "Virgin Briar" stamp beneath it.
comoy-s-virgin-briar.not: This pipe was made for the 1933 Chicago World's Fair; the right-face stamps on the shank match those of the Chelsea example issued for the same fair. The *2 stamp and patent number on the underside indicate the pipe contains a metal filter rod called the "Grand Slam." The "Virgin Briar" line began in 1933 and no longer appears in Comoy's 1965 catalogs.

rows: Made in England (within a circle) U.S.PAT. 2001612, 389

bounty.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle; the words "Bounty" and "Real Briar" on the shank.

pipe-lon.tn: A two-letter logo; on the left side, a pipe-and-smoke drawing accompanies the words "PIPE LON".
pipe-lon.not: The brand belongs to the pipe shop run by Lon Schwartz. Schwartz was the first U.S. dealer of Preben Holm pipes, from 1967-1968.

rows: PIPE LON (with a pipe and smoke drawing)

golowacz.tn: Initials "JSG" stamped on the underside; no logo on the stem.
golowacz.not: The brand's maker is Jan Szymon Golowacz.

dr-bob.not: The brand's maker is physician Robert C. Kiess. The finish was indicated by SL, SM, SD for smooth pipes and RL, RM, RD for rustic or sandblasted pipes; these abbreviations were discontinued in 2011. In grading, the entry grade carries P, PP, PPP, and the top grade carries H, HH stamps; the two-digit number gives the year of manufacture, followed by the pipe's sequence number for that year. For the same logo see John Surrey.

satou.tn: A single dot on the stem; the underside carries "Smio Satou" together with ideograms.
satou.not: Maker Smio Satou was born in 1944 and has since stopped production. Records from 2010 indicate he made 40-50 pipes a year and was known for high-grade freehand pipes with bamboo accents.

elba.tn: Single-letter logo; "Elba, Bruyere" lettering in the stamp.

ailarov.tn: No mark on the stem; the stamp consists only of the text "S. AILAROV" on the underside.
ailarov.not: The pipes are made by Sergey Ailarov, born 1973. The stamp bears only the maker's name; no date or grading mark is struck.

octogonal-logo.tn: A logo consisting of a letter enclosed in an octagonal frame.
octogonal-logo.not: Pipes bearing the "Jeantet Production" stamp were made for export.

rows: JEANTET Production since 1807 CORSICAN BRIAR Made in France

juls.tn: The stamp "JULS" written in plain letters.
juls.not: Maker Julian Schäffer began carving pipes in 1982 and largely gave up the work in the early 1990s. In his 2001 collection he brought together fourteen high-grade pipes.

telmy.tn: A two-letter stamp on the stem.

kallenberg.tn: A logo consisting of a single stylized letter "K".
kallenberg.not: The brand was founded in 1919 by Heinrich Kallenberg, with production continued by his grandson Hans Kallenberg. Following Hans Kallenberg's retirement, production has, as of 2011 records, been carried on by his student Frank Peter Filß.

rows: THURINGIA Hand made (with the stylized "K" logo used since 1990)

buckingham.tn: A single letter on the stem.
buckingham.not: Made at a factory in London.

proctus.tn: No logo on the stem; "Proctus De Luxe" on the top.
proctus.not: Records list Bari as the brand's manufacturer; this is unconfirmed.

coulshaw.tn: Logo shaped like a rum barrel.
coulshaw.not: One of the brands under British Pipe Co.

loran.tn: No logo on the stem; the stamps consist of text only.
loran.not: Maker Ib Loran began pipe making around 1955. In the 1960s and 1970s he was, like Gert Holbek, among the makers working for Pipe-Dan. As of 2010 his daughter Tine Loran carries on his work.

kaywoodie-setter.tn: The underside carries the "Kaywoodie," "Setter," and "Imported Briar" stamps.
kaywoodie-setter.not: A model produced by Kaywoodie between 1955 and 1968, named for its flat base. It was made in panel, billiard, and poker shapes, with no stinger system, fitted instead with a push (friction) stem.

savory.tn: A red "S" combined with a crown motif.
savory.not: The brand was founded in 1885 by H.L. Savory & Co. and later passed into Dunhill's hands.

europe.tn: "Pipe Europe" lettering arranged with letters enclosed in a circle.

brentwood.tn: A single-letter stamp; the shank is marked with the name "Brentwood" and a shape number.
brentwood.not: The same logo also appears on the Bel-Air brand. Because the 335 and four-digit 9518 shape numbers on the stamps follow GBD's numbering system, the brand is thought to be GBD's second line.

york.tn: The word "York" alongside a single-letter motif.
york.not: Records suggest the brand may be a sub-brand of KB&B.

savinelli.tn: One, two, or three dots on the stem; the stamp carries the Savinelli crest.
savinelli.not: Savinelli shape codes are generally three digits; the Non Pareil line is an exception, stamped with a three- or four-digit code. Some examples carry no line-name stamp at all; shape 320 KS appears in the smooth-polished Siena line and also as 320 EX in the Hercules line.

alfred-baier.tn: A wooden round inlay on the stem.
alfred-baier.not: The maker Alfred Baier has been making pipes since 1986.

falcon-2.tn: Logo featuring a bird of prey (falcon) figure.
falcon-2.not: The same logo also appears in the Royal Falcon entry.

wilshire.tn: A logo with a single letter and three dots; the "Wilshire" stamp on the top face.

sir-edwin.tn: Logo featuring a crown motif; the stamp carries the words "Sir Edwin" and "Made in England."

sasieni-the-alternative.tn: A single blue dot on top of the stem, with the letter "S" on its side.
sasieni-the-alternative.not: A blue dot appears on top of the stem with the letter "S" on its side; examples also exist that carry no dot, showing only the blue letter "S." The stamp belongs to Sasieni's 1979-1986 transition period and is recorded as contemporary with the Claret line.

rows: The Alternative, London made, by Sasieni
The Alternative, London England, By Sasieni

holger-danske.tn: A logo of two letters; the stamp carries the text "Holger Danske".

kudu.tn: A logo depicting a mammal figure representing the kudu antelope.

borkum-riff.tn: A two-letter stamp; the words "Borkum Riff" on the shank.
borkum-riff.not: Borkum Riff is Swedish Match's tobacco brand. The pipe bearing this name is Savinelli-made and identical to the firm's model 440KS.

doncaster.tn: Logo made of several letters; the stamp carries the name "Doncaster".

ducale.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter.

jandrew.tn: The text "Jandrew" on the left face; no separate logo is used.
jandrew.not: The brand's maker is J. Andrew Kovacs.

brakner.tn: A single blue dot on the stem; the shank bears the name "Brakner", a series name, and a shape number.
brakner.not: The brand of the Danish master Peter Brakner. Most of his pipes have a rustic finish; smooth-finish examples are rare.

rows: Brakner De Luxe, Royal Danois, 37152, Hand-Cut., Straight Grain, 810

dejarnett.not: The brand's maker is Horace DeJarnett. The number identifies the pipe by year and its sequence within that year: 0310 denotes the third pipe carved in 2010. The top grade is AAA, followed by the eagle emblem grade.

old-vic.tn: The lettering "Old-Vic", formed from the letters of the brand name.

tortoise.tn: The letters "BBB" within a diamond-shaped frame, alongside the word "Tortoise."

mr-pipes.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.
mr-pipes.not: Records indicate the brand is based in Las Vegas while the pipes were made in London.

barbados.tn: A letter B within a circle on the stem.
barbados.not: Big-Ben's sub-brand Thompson also has a series called Barbados.

london-made.tn: A stamp on the stem giving the brand name as text.
london-made.not: Pipes bearing this stamp were carved at Charatan's Prescott Street factory, and the stem stamp is placed vertically. On examples carved at the English factory, the same text is struck horizontally on the stem.

rows: Ben Wade, Selected Briar, London Made, 38

peterson-killarney.tn: A single-letter stamp; the word "Killarney" appears on the underside.

sasieni-four-dot-rustic.tn: Asterisk mark and "FOUR DOT RUSTIC" stamp on the underside.
sasieni-four-dot-rustic.not: A Four Dot stamp from the pre-transitional period (1946-1979). "Rustic" is the name given to the textured (embossed) finish; a single asterisk appears beside the word "Four".

sasieni-slendaline.tn: "Slendaline, London Made, by Sasieni" on the left side.

savinelli-320-ks.tn: Two dots on the stem; "Savinelli" with a shield emblem on the underside.
savinelli-320-ks.not: This example has no stamp naming the product line. Savinelli's other two-dot lines are Non Pareil and Gold; the same 320 KS shape also appears as 320 EX in the smooth-finish Siena and Erica Fiamma lines, and in the Hercules line.

pow.tn: A single plain, undecorated round dot on the stem.
pow.not: Records indicate the brand's pipes were made by G. M. Frame.

navigator.tn: A star-shaped stamp on the stem.

waldorf.tn: A clover-leaf motif stamped on the stem.

bryson.tn: The word "Bryson" and a serial number on the shank.
bryson.not: The brand of the Briarwood Corporation, based in Palo Alto, California. The replaceable bits were made from ground briar, compressed under very high pressure without powdered adhesive or heat.

enricoro.tn: Ornate round inlay on the stem shaped like a brass clock-movement bearing.
enricoro.not: The pipes are made by craftsman Enrico Marola, who works in Vercelli (Piedmont) and is also a watchmaker.

stohr.tn: The letters ES within an oval.
stohr.not: Eckhart Stöhr, born 1954, has made pipes part-time since 1990. His pipes generally carry only the ES stamp within the oval and are not graded.

tower.tn: A tower-shaped building figure; the stamp is split across both faces, with the word "Tower" between diamond marks.
tower.not: Similar logos appear on the Castleford, Moorgate, and St James brands.

st-andrew.tn: A letter set in a circle with the text "St Andrew."

grand-duke.tn: A logo formed from the letter "D" enclosed in an octagon.
grand-duke.not: The stamp's shape, typeface, and wording support the view that Duke of Kent, Sir Duke, Sir Bruce, and Grand Duke were all made by Jeantet. These brands are thought to have most likely been used for export.

twiga.tn: A brand logo in the form of a mammal figure.
twiga.not: One of the brands produced by the Tanganyika Meerschaum Corporation under its Amboseli Pipes line. For the same maker's other brands, see Countryman, Kiko, Kikob, Kilimanjaro, Kudu, Merlin, and Sportsman.

jon-s.tn: The word "JON'S" enclosed in an oval.

knudsen-2.tn: "S. Knudsen" on the underside, along with a Moor's-head figure.
knudsen-2.not: Sven Knudsen did not use a grading stamp on his pipes.

filto.tn: A stamp on the left side reading the brand name "Filto".
filto.not: The patent taken out in Robert L. Smith's name is dated 1965. The bowl and stem were produced in numerous color options; a spring clip on the tenon holds the filter in place.

rows: Filto, Burgaw. N.C., Pat. Made in U.S.A.

union.tn: A diamond-shaped logo on the stem, the word "Union" on the left face.
union.not: The same stem logo also appears on the Coronado and Robert's brands.

gold-king.not: The Gold King logo is yellow, while the Silverking logo is white. For the same logo, see Big Ben Reputation and Silverking.

two-stars.tn: The letters "BBB" within a diamond, together with two stars.

rows: BBB [within a diamond] [two stars], Made in England

hildebrand.tn: A wolf's head flanked by the letters P and H.
hildebrand.not: The stamps are mostly laser-engraved and white. The four-digit number gives the production date, and the three-digit number gives the serial number. The trailing two letters are believed, per records, to belong to a grading system and are absent on some pipes; the meaning of the leading single letter is unknown.

rows: [wolf head logo flanked by the letters P and H]

weber.tn: A single dot or a letter-in-circle stamp on the stem.

aerosphere.tn: A metal inlay on the side of the stem; "Aerosphere, Duncan Hill" on the shank.
aerosphere.not: The metal piece beside the stem is not a logo but an air-adjustment mechanism. Similar mechanisms are also seen on the Amphora, Carey, Dialite, Dunhill Airstream, Kaywoodie Carburetor, and Passat brands.

comoy-s-specimen-straight-grain.tn: "Comoy's," "Specimen," and "Straight Grain" stacked on the left side.
comoy-s-specimen-straight-grain.not: In Comoy's 1965 catalogue, the Specimen Straight Grain is described as the brand's rarest and highest grade. Weekly sets of seven Specimen Straight Grain pipes were also produced.

rows: Made in London (within a circle), England, 434

wells.tn: A single-letter logo; the brand name appears on the top face.

hollycourt.tn: A single letter set inside a circle.

castleton.not: The same mark is also seen on the Middleton brand.

old-antiquari.tn: A stamp consisting of the words "Castello" and "Old Antiquari" on the underside.

rows: Castello, Old Antiquari, Made in Cantu, Italy, 11.230

yeco.tn: The word "Ropp" set in an oval alongside a rod motif.

fribourg-treyer.tn: Five dots on the stem; the letters "F&T" combined in the stamp.
fribourg-treyer.not: A pipe of the wind-cap "hurricane" type. Other brands producing this type include Orlik, Dr Plumb, Butz Choquin (Auto-Sport), Cyclone, Mastercraft (Sparkproof), and Fortnum's (Windward).

rows: Shipmate (within a diamond), Made in England, X49

masson-cie.tn: The text "Masson Tabacs" and "Lausanne" on the shank.
masson-cie.not: The business, located on Rue de Bourg in Lausanne, is owned by Dominique-Paul Frainier. Records indicate that the writer Georges Simenon was among its customers.

kilkenny.tn: A single-letter stamp enclosed in a circle.

rows: Kilkenny, Finest Briar, Made in London, England, 73

elf.tn: Logo formed from the letters of the brand name.

national.tn: A single black dot on the stem.
national.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's study, National may be a second brand of Comoy or Maurice Pipes. The black dot can also appear on the right side of the stem.

saci.tn: No logo; the underside carries a number and the maker's signature.

dialite.tn: Bar-motif logo; "Dialite, Aircooled, Pat. Pend" lettering on the left face.

felt-fur.tn: A pipe with its bowl covered in a synthetic fur-like material, no stamp on the shank.
felt-fur.not: The recorded pipe carries no shank stamp; the bowl is covered with a synthetic fur-type material.

osa.tn: The stamp "OSA", formed from the letters of the brand name.
osa.not: The pipes were made at the Gros, Grenier, Ostorero & Cie factory. For brands associated with the same factory, see also the entries for GOC, Prior, and Sicana.

thoroughbred.not: The same horse logo also appears on the Derby brand.

elie-2.tn: No stamp image or logo data available.

tsuge-ikebana.tn: "Tsuge" and "Made in Japan" within a circle on the underside, with the series name "Ikebana."

reiner-thilo.tn: No logo on the stem; "Reiner Thilo" name, the word "Freehand", and a letter-number code on the underside.
reiner-thilo.not: Maker Reiner Thilo Bindschädel (b. 1961) began selling his pipes in 2002. The code in the stamp consists of one letter and one digit: the digit indicates the surface finish (3 rustic, 2 partly rustic, 1 and 0 smooth), while the letter shows a quality grade rising from "e" to "a"; "Premium" grade pipes are stamped with his name instead. Annual production is about 120 pipes.

heritage.tn: A logo in the shape of a diamond (rhombus).
heritage.not: Heritage Pipe Inc. closed in 1971. The brand is one of S.M. Frank's sub-brands.

goodwill.not: The brand of Danish maker Georg Jensen.

medico.tn: A two-letter logo within a coat of arms; a ring-motif variant also exists.

civic.tn: Logo formed from the letters of the brand name, accompanied by a plant motif.
civic.not: Civic is one of the brands of the Cadogan company, which also includes BBB, Comoy, GBD, Loewe, and Orlik. The "CIVIC" stamp appears both in letters with forked tails and in a plain form without them. See also Nu-Old.

dura.tn: Carries no separate logo; "Dura Sweden" lettering appears beneath a triple-crown mark on the underside.
dura.not: The pipes were made by craftsman Dura Semjaniv (1954 - January 2008). On pipes made after 2004, the stamps were machine-engraved and Sweden's Three Crowns (Tre Kronor) coat of arms was added above the word "Dura". The two-digit number indicates the year of manufacture; production for 2004 was approximately 75 pipes.

marina.tn: The text 'Marina Filter' on the shank.

chatham.tn: Single letter within a circle on the stem.

bdl.tn: A stamp consisting of a triangular motif.
bdl.not: Records indicate the brand's stamp includes the wording 'BDL Supreme 393'.

nationale.tn: On the stem, three vertical bars resembling the French flag.
nationale.not: A similar logo based on the French flag is also seen on the Vincent brand.

cats-paw.tn: A depiction of a cat's paw on the underside together with the brand name; there is no separate logo mark.

la-normandy.tn: A star motif with the words "La Normandy" beside it.
la-normandy.not: The pipes were designed by Pierre Morel and manufactured by Chacom. The brand is the Cuty-Fort group's export brand aimed at the U.S. market.

delacour.tn: Logo consisting of two letters enclosed within a circle.
delacour.not: The brand was founded by Alix Delacour in the late 19th century; production took place at the factory at 14 bis rue Carnot in Saint-Claude. The A.D and J.D letters on the silver marks refer to Auguste and Joseph Delacour, who ran the affiliated company Delacour Brothers Ltd in London; the hallmark belongs to the Birmingham Assay Office. The firm's activity ended in the late 1950s.

atwood.not: The brand is based on a registered US patent; the patent number is stamped on the underside of the pipes.

best-make.tn: The letters 'BBB' within a diamond, with 'Best Make' beside it.
best-make.not: The logo is made of brass inlaid into the stem.

kuziel.tn: The words "Kuziel, U.S.A." on the shank.
kuziel.not: Maker Paul Kuziel was born in 1968 in New Haven, Connecticut; he is a painter, photographer, and craftsman. Records indicate he was living in East Haven as of 2009.

erix.tn: A single letter within a circle.

sasieni-john-bull.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem; the words "John Bull, Sasieni Made" on the shank.

masso-milleiro.tn: No documented stamp or logo depiction exists for this brand.

l-anatra.tn: A duck-themed brand stamp; an egg-shaped emblem on the stem, the words "L'Anatra dalle Uova d'Oro" on the left side.
l-anatra.not: On the brand's higher-grade pipes, the logo is worked in three dimensions on the stem; this treatment is seen on very few brands.

ajustomatic.tn: A single dot on the stem; some examples have a target-like concentric-ring mark.
ajustomatic.not: Patent number 2461905 in the stamp belongs to the Synchro Stem mechanism. Records indicate other brands also carry the same fleur-de-lis mark: Cellini, Duke of Kent, Fleur de lis, Harrington Park, Omega, Thomas, Vincenzo Lombardi.

rows: Van Roy Arista Imported Briar, Ajustomatic Pat. Pend.

tabac-mesange.tn: A logo made up of bars set side by side.

hallmark.tn: The letter B inside a diamond shape, with the text "Hallmark", in the stamp.
hallmark.not: See also Smokemaster, L.L. Bean, Cavalcade.

international.tn: The letters GBD set inside a rounded rectangle, with the word "International" beside it.
international.not: GBD International pipes were marked both with this rounded-rectangle stamp and with the brand's usual "GBD in an oval" stamp.

rows: GBD (within an oval) International, London Made

kaywoodie-hi-bowl.tn: The stamps "Kaywoodie" and "HI-BOWL" on the shank.
kaywoodie-hi-bowl.not: This stamp was used between 1961 and 1966.

pipeworks.tn: A star-motif stamp; the shank reads "Pipeworks, New York City, U.S.A.".
pipeworks.not: Elliot Nachwalter ran the Wilke pipe shop in New York together with his former wife Carol Burns from 1980 to 1995. This stamp dates from that period.

lamboley.tn: A monogram-style logo formed by the combination of two letters.
lamboley.not: This is the brand of Roger Lamboley, a pipe wholesaler in Paris; the same type of business is also seen with J. Bayle. The pipes were made in Saint-Claude, France.

danish-natural.not: The same crown logo also appears on the Royal Danish brand.

mathias.tn: No documented stamp or logo depiction exists for this brand.

gigi.tn: A hand holding a pipe on the left side; a target motif of concentric rings on the stem.
gigi.not: Because of the "hand holding a pipe" emblem on the shank, this pipe, which carries no brand name, is attributed to Crugnola. Maker Luigi "Gigi" Crugnola worked in Gavirate, in the province of Varese. See also Crugnola.

protter.not: Maker Ben Protter (b. September 13, 1900) entered the pipe trade first as an importer and distributor. In the late 1940s he began making his own pipes in his Brooklyn workshop.

king-of-denmark.tn: A stamp in the form of an ornamented round dot.

rows: King of Denmark, Made in England

kaywoodie-magnum.not: The Magnum line was produced from 1974 to 1989. Its pipes were always finished half smooth, half rusticated.

ljung.tn: On the left side, the text 'Arne Ljung Sweden' and a number giving the year of manufacture; there is no separate logo stamp.
ljung.not: Maker Arne Ljung (1913-1998) began making pipes in 1963. Early stamps read "LJUNG of SWEDEN" in a straight line; later stamps read "Arne Ljung Sweden" arranged in a circle. The year of manufacture is struck inside the circle.

captain-fortune.tn: An anchor-motif stamp; the words "Captain Fortune" and "London Made" appear on the left face.
captain-fortune.not: Records indicate the brand was made at a factory in London.

hennen.tn: A snake-shaped emblem set between two lines on the underside.
hennen.not: The maker is Hermann Hennen, born 1946, a retired furniture designer. The snake-like emblem is the only mark found on his pipes.

jost-s.tn: The words "Made in London" enclosed in a circle.

rows: Made in London [within a circle], England, J126

briarmeer.tn: Two dots on the stem; the stamp shows a letter B set within a diamond.
briarmeer.not: One of Briarcraft's two-dot second-grade brands; Arcadian belongs to the same group.

rows: B (within a diamond) Briarmeer, Genuine Briar

denicotea.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle; "Denicotea" lettering on the left face.
denicotea.not: The brand was founded in Cologne in 1932 by Willy Heineberg. The Denicotea name actually belongs to a silica-gel filter. Pipes bearing this stamp were made for the brand by another manufacturer in England and sold under the brand name.

super-briarbark.not: One example is dated 1950. A more recent Parker Super BriarBark carrying no date code instead bears the group code (a 4 within a circle) Dunhill used after 1952.

rows: 5/F Parker, Super (within a diamond) Briar Bark
Made in London, England 0, PAT. No. 116989/17
Parker, Super (within a diamond) Briar Bark
Made in London, England, 4 (within a circle)

brigham-six-dots.tn: Six dots arranged in a row on the stem.

o-ke.tn: A logo consisting of the brand name lettering.

brigham-one-dot.tn: A single dot on the stem.
brigham-one-dot.not: Pipes with a single dot on the stem correspond to the shape series numbered in the 1xx range (the 100 series).

town-and-country.tn: No recorded stamp breakdown or logo description available.

coronation.not: Records indicate the Coronation grade came into use between 1965 and 1979. During this period the stamp carried the full wording "Made by hand in the city of London".

vanguard.tn: The word "Vanguard" on a single line, with "Real Briar" beneath it.

pipstar.tn: A star-motif stamp; the shank reads "PiPstar".
pipstar.not: This is the brand of C.J. Verguet Frères, a company from Saint Claude that closed in 1970. The same company also owned GBD between 1903 and 1970.

sasieni-4-dots-2-on-each-side.tn: Two dots on each face of the stem.
sasieni-4-dots-2-on-each-side.not: A pre-transition, doubled two-dot layout dating 1927-1939. The model appears in the 1939 Sasieni catalogue but not in the 1936 or 1943 catalogues. The briar used is of Algerian origin.

mauro.tn: A plain round inlay on the stem and a single-letter "m" logo.
mauro.not: Sources sometimes attribute the brand to Mauro Bartoli; however, the dot and "m" letter logos link the brand to Mauro Armellini instead.

fillenwarth.tn: A record without a separate logo; the underside reads "Fillenwarth".
fillenwarth.not: The pipes' maker, Tony Fillenwarth, has reportedly been making pipes since 2002.

aiwon.tn: A single-letter mark on the stem.
aiwon.not: The brand of the La Bruyère firm. La Bruyère merged with Chapuis-Comoy in 1932.

kaywoodie-stembiter.tn: A stamp made up of "Stembiter Kaywoodie" on the left side.
kaywoodie-stembiter.not: The stem has a three-branch smoke channel: two branches end at the tip of the stem, the third at the notch on the top surface. The model appeared in the early 1950s; the same notch is also seen on the "All Briar" model.

nazarenko.tn: No separate logo is used; the underside is stamped with the maker's name and the words "handmade."
nazarenko.not: The maker of these pipes is Maksim Nazarenko.

hall-of-fame.tn: A logo of a single letter and a plant motif on the stem.
hall-of-fame.not: For the same logo, see Atwood. Judging by the stamps, the Saint-Claude-marked example must have been made in a different workshop from the other.

ornsby.not: These pipes, which have a metal shank-to-stem tenon, were marketed by the Ornsby Pipe Company Ltd, located in the Pennywell district of Sunderland, Tyne & Wear, England.

oxford.tn: A crown figure together with the brand name "Oxford".
oxford.not: The stamps are thought, according to records, to be associated with a subline or second-quality range of Hardcastle; the crown figure is similar to those of the Royal Bruyere and Royal Crown stamps. The same brand name was used by at least around ten English and French makers and dealers (Wilczak and Colwell).

poul-winslw-for-stanwell.not: In this example the crown that normally sits above the "S" in the Stanwell stamp is absent.

rasmussen.tn: No logo or stamp information is recorded.

sasieni-6-dots-3-on-each-side.tn: Six dots total, three on each face of the stem.
sasieni-6-dots-3-on-each-side.not: The "Superb Six" series of the transition period, 1979-1986; the lucite stem has three dots placed on each opposing face. Records indicate the series is contemporary with "The Perfect Ten" and shares the same stem and stamp layout.

rows: Superb Six, London made by Sasieni, Made in England

c-est-bon.tn: The words "Butz-Choquin" and "C'est bon" on the shank.

peter-stokkebye.tn: "Peter Stokkebye" on the shank and a crest-shaped stamp.
peter-stokkebye.not: Peter Stokkebye pipes were generally shaped by the Danish maker Jorgen Larsen. Records suggest these stamps indicate either an early period or pipes not made by Larsen.

rows: Peter Stkkebye, Made in Denmark, H

lillehammer.tn: Two small square marks placed to align the shank with the stem; the letters "GL" and a star motif in the stamp.
lillehammer.not: The letters "GL" are the initials of Gudbrand Larsen (d. 1902), who founded the brand in 1844. The alignment squares are red on some pipes and white on others. When sales declined in the 1960s the brand passed to Kriswill, and the Norwegian factory was run for a time by this Danish company; see also Norrøna.

oliver-brandt.tn: A single solid dot on the underside of the stem.
oliver-brandt.not: The maker Oliver Brandt is the father of Max Brandt, who uses the MB stamp; his own pipes carry the "Olive" stamp, while the "Brandy" series is a joint production of father and son. Grading on "Olive" and "MB" pipes runs, in ascending order, AA, EX1 through EX12, Artline, and the rarely seen Rune. In the "Brandy" series, grades are numbered from 1 to 12.

rows: On the underside of the stem

jrn-larsen.tn: The words "UP town's" and "Jørn Larsen Denmark" on the underside.
jrn-larsen.not: Maker Jørn Larsen, born 1949, exports most of his pipes to the United States; according to 2007 records his annual output is about 400 pipes. Pipes bearing this stamp were carved for Uptown's Smoke Shops in Nashville, Tennessee.

heinz-nolte.tn: Round stone inlay on the stem.
heinz-nolte.not: The workshop's annual output is roughly 200 pipes.

gotang.tn: A stamp on the underside reading "Gotang" together with the year of production.
gotang.not: Gotang is a collaboration between Tom Eltang and Kei'ichi Gotoh. In the example pipe, the bowl is made of lemonwood lined inside with briar. See Botang.

zeus.tn: The word "Zeus" set between diamond shapes above the stem.
zeus.not: This is a filter pipe designed to hold two cigarette halves to act as the filter.

ace-of-spades.tn: An ornamented round inlay in the stem and a letter enclosed in a circle.

brishuta.not: Master carver Alex Brishuta was born in 1970; he made his first pipe in spring 2009 and began working as a full-time pipe maker in 2011. The first two digits of the number on the stamp give the year of production. Another maker who stamps his pipes with a cat is Ken.

fikri-baki.tn: A meerschaum pipe record with the brand name given in script.
fikri-baki.not: No stamp appears on the meerschaum body. Other brands featured on the site with block meerschaum examples include Altinok, CAO, Man, Manx Meerschaum, Nørding, Pioneer, SMS, and Vercingetorix.

pehem.tn: A stamp with no separate emblem, consisting of the word "Pehem".
pehem.not: The brand was used by Pierre Morel (father), who has since passed away.

mullins-westley.tn: A two-letter "CT" stamp on the stem.
mullins-westley.not: The brand belongs to a tobacconist in Covent Garden, London, who also blends their own pipe tobacco. The letters CT on the stamp are an abbreviation of "Covent Traditional".

rows: Mullins & Westley Ltd Covent Garden, London

straus.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle.
straus.not: Henry Straus was a pipe maker who worked at Charatan. From roughly the 1940s to the late 1950s he also carved pipes under his own name.

rows: Straus, Private Stock, Made in England, 43

micke.tn: A logo formed from the letters of the brand name.

flamidor.not: These pipes were distributed by the Flamidor lighter brand.

auto-sport.tn: The left face bears the stamp "Butz-Choquin, Auto-Sport."
auto-sport.not: One of the wind-protected "Hurricane" type pipes.

paolucci.tn: The brand name "Paolucci" stamped together with leaf figures.
paolucci.not: The briar used comes from Calabria, Tuscany, and Corsica; the stems are handmade from ebonite or acrylic. Grading is shown by the number of leaves, ranging from one leaf up to five.

rows: Right side, lower part, within a cartouche

royal-london.not: The same castle logo also appears on the London Town brand.

true-grain.tn: "Dr Grabow" and "True-Grain" on the left side, a patent number on the underside.
