true-grain.not: This example carries no model-number stamp. Records date the pipe to Dr. Grabow's Chicago period, 1940-1953.

castleford.tn: A mark featuring an architectural motif.
castleford.not: Maker Colin Fromm; see Invicta Briars. For similar marks see Tower, Moorgate, and St James.

ciro.tn: Round wooden inlay on the stem.
ciro.not: Maker Angelo Chirico has been carving pipes since 2005. The workshop is located in Carugate, near Milan. According to 2009 data, annual production is around 60-70 pipes.

bentley.tn: A single red dot on the stem.
bentley.not: Records note that the original boxes accompanying these pipes indicate the product is a Kaywoodie second grade. See also Willmer's Bentley pipe line and Former's Danish brand Bentley.

la-rocca.tn: A two-letter monogram stamp; the words "La Rocca" on the left side.

briarcraft.tn: A letter B set within a diamond; a crown motif also appears on the stamps.
briarcraft.not: Records list Briarcraft's second-grade brands as: Airo, Arcadian, Briarmeer, Cavalcade, Hallmark, L.L. Bean, Smokemaster, Sterling Hall, Wimbledon.

belvedere.tn: A two-letter 'Belvedere' script used together with a Charatan signature on the left face.

bartoli.not: The workshop is run by master carver Mauro Bartoli together with his daughters. The brand was founded in 1950 by Mauro's father, Pietro Bartoli.

arlington.not: A brand of the Arlington Briar Pipe Corp.

morell-mackenzie.tn: The letters BBB enclosed in a diamond.
morell-mackenzie.not: The brand name comes from the English physician Sir Morell Mackenzie (1837-1892), considered a pioneer of laryngology in the United Kingdom. Mackenzie is also known for failing to diagnose the throat cancer of German Emperor Frederick III. The hallmarks on the band belong to the London Assay Office.

salmastro.tn: The text "Salmastro Italy" set in a circle, with a wave symbol beside it.
salmastro.not: The maker, Michele Mellone, was born in 1968 and made his first pipe in 1999. Guidance from Teddy Knudsen, support from briar cutter Mimmo, and collaboration with Luca Di Piazza brought him recognition in international pipe circles. The Italian word "salmastro" means brackish, salty water.

graco.tn: A logo on the stem formed from the letters of the brand name; the shank reads "Graco" along with the model name.
graco.not: Graco is the brand of the Grappin Fils & Cie factory in Saint Claude. The company was formed in 1924 from the merger of Grappin-Brochot and Grappin-Dalloz, and closed in 1968.

tinder-box.tn: A stamp consisting of a shield-shaped emblem and letters.

rows: Charatan's, Made By Hand in City of London

il-ceppo.tn: A logo of a single letter.
il-ceppo.not: On early pipes the "Il Ceppo" stamp is slightly curved; it uses a letter from A to H, a four- or five-digit number, and a group number inside a triangle. In the later period the stamp is struck straight, and the digit denotes surface finish: 1 sandblast, 2 partial rustic, 3 partial sandblast, 4-5-6-7 smooth finish in rising grain quality, 9 rustic. The brand's sub-brand is Amarcord.

rows: E 3892 Made by Hand (curved), In Italy, 6 (within a triangle)
Il Ceppo, Freeline, 1 (within a circle), Hand Made, Italy

grandolfo.tn: A plant-motif logo along with the "Grandolfo" signature on the underside of the shank.
grandolfo.not: Maker Alessandro Grandolfo (b. 1969) has made pipes full-time since June 2009. Records indicate an annual output of 250-350 pipes. His pipes carry only the signature; no date or grade stamp is used.

fait-main.tn: Stamp arrangement reading "Butz Choquin, Maitre Pipier" on the left side and "Fait Main" on the right side.
fait-main.not: Pipes in the "Maitre Pipier" series were first made by Paul Lanier; after his retirement, production was carried on by Alain Albuisson.

howell.tn: No separate logo stamp; the underside bears a curved "Howell" script, initials, and a year.
howell.not: A handmade brand. Jack Howell became known after attending the 2004 Chicago pipe show.

ebony.tn: Letter mark enclosed in a circle on the stem; "Medico Ebony" lettering on the shank.

larrysson.tn: A single inlaid dot on the stem.
larrysson.not: Maker Paul Larrysson Hubartt (b. 1973) first lived in the U.S. state of Indiana, then settled in Cornwall, England, in 2002. Records indicate he had made 50 pipes by 2006. The code in the stamp consists of the pipe number and the year of manufacture; as of 2011 the brand has no grading system.

husky.tn: A logo of a single letter.

elliot-nachwalter.not: Elliot Nachwalter settled in Arlington, Vermont, in 1996; pipes bearing this stamp date from after that time. See also Pipeworks and The Briar Workshop.

gasparini.tn: Single letter enclosed in a circle and a single dot on the stem.
gasparini.not: The letter "M" in the stamp is the initial of founder Mario Gasparini; later the "G" from Mario's signature was adopted as the brand logo. According to Mario's daughter Marisa Gasparini, the brand's owner as of 2013, this pipe dates to 1965. Pipes stamped Gasparini M.G.M. do not come from Mario's firm but from a different company that engaged in unfair competition in the late 1970s and went bankrupt within two years; that brand's second-line names are Il Ponte and MGM.

kuttel.tn: "Kuttel, Rubina" on the left side, a model code and maker's name on the underside.
kuttel.not: A private-label brand of a Swiss tobacconist. According to the stamp on the underside, the pipes are made by Ilio Barontini.

benaderet-s.tn: A logo of a letter set within a circle and diamond.
benaderet-s.not: Other stamp variants of the brand and the shop's history are covered in separate records.

rows: The Californian, Made in England (curved), Benaderet's London Made 127

the-golden-arrow.tn: "The Golden Arrow" alongside a single-bar-and-arrow motif.
the-golden-arrow.not: One of Comoy's second-quality brands. The same single-bar logo also appears on the Carlyle, Charles Cross, St James, Town Hall, and Trident stamps; see also Golden Arrow.

rows: 550, Made in England, By Comoy, K

denovic.not: The brand's maker is Davorin Denovic, who signs his pipes with the Croatian angular form of the letter "Dobro" (D) from the old Slavic Glagolitic alphabet. The brand uses no grading or date stamp.

1913-1938.tn: "GBD" on the shank, anchor and lion hallmarks on the silver band.
1913-1938.not: The hallmarks on the band belong to the Birmingham Assay Office.

upper-ten.tn: The words "Upper Ten" and a registered trademark number on the left face.

bee-hive.tn: A letter stamp with 'Bee Hive' on the shank.
bee-hive.not: No information on the brand is found in the records.

rows: Bee Hive, Honey Lined, Genuine Briar

abbott.tn: Two-letter brand stamp; "Abbot, London Made" on the left side, "Made in England" in an oval on the right side.
abbott.not: One of the brands of the Andersen & Abbot firm.

meerschaum.tn: On a meerschaum pipe, a multi-letter logo.
meerschaum.not: This meerschaum pipe's stem is made of horn; examples of this material carved as a P-Lip are rare. The band is silver but carries no hallmark, so the pipe cannot be dated. Because the "P" stem logos resemble one another, Peterson meerschaum pipes should not be confused with Pioneer pipes.

pioneer.tn: A "P" logo made up of a single letter; meerschaum pipes carry a "Genuine Block Meerschaum" stamp.
pioneer.not: The brand's "P" logo can be confused with the "P" stamp seen on Peterson's meerschaum pipes; the two are separate stamps.

howal-2.tn: A logo made of a chevron (inverted V) motif.

the-exmoor.tn: "The Exmoor Pipe" arranged in a curve on the underside, along with a single-letter motif.

rows: The Exmoor Pipe, Made in England (curved)

marco-polo.tn: The letters KB & B within a clover; beside them, the text 'Marco Polo.'
marco-polo.not: The ampersand in the clover logo (KB & B) was discontinued in the 1930s.

rows: Marco Polo, KB & B (within a clover)

twistel.not: This is a private brand commissioned by Walter Twistel GmbH & Co. under its own name; the pipes were distributed as promotional items.

tilshead.tn: No stamp description available in the records.

lord.tn: On the stem, a triangular logo containing a single letter.

light-weight.tn: The words "Hardcastle's British Made Light Weight" on the shank.

bentley-us.tn: A single red dot on the stem along with a single-letter logo.
bentley-us.not: Records note that the original box accompanying this pipe indicates the product is a Kaywoodie second grade. See also Willmer's Bentley pipe line.

theydon.tn: A single-letter logo; "THEYDON" on the shank.

casino.tn: A letter-shaped mark enclosed in a circle.

potpourri.tn: Letter inside a circle, with "Potpourri" on the shank.
potpourri.not: Records attribute the brand to an unidentified Italian maker.

eden-roc.tn: Single-letter mark on the stem; "Eden Roc Classic" lettering on the shank.
eden-roc.not: This pipe does not belong to GBD's Eden Rock series.

lord-kirk.tn: A filled-ring logo on the stem.

cdl.tn: A stamp made up of the words "Dr Grabow", "CDL", and "Imported Briar" on the shank.
cdl.not: The CDL line was test-marketed in several US cities between 1975 and 1983 and never reached full production.

irc.tn: A stamp of letters and a star motif; on Dutch-made examples the letters on the stem are set inside a circle.
irc.not: French-made IRC pipes typically carry an "IR" stamp on the stem. Those made at the Royal Dutch Pipe Factory instead show an IRC stamp set inside a circle on the stem. See also Big-Ben, Iwan Ries & Co, IRC ThreeStar.

rows: Big Ben, Houston, X-tra, 124, Made in Holland

roland.tn: Logo spelling out the brand name; the stamp carries the text "President by Roland."
roland.not: Roland is a brand made for the Japanese market by Fukashiro Co.

barling.tn: No logo depiction or stamp casting is recorded.

missouri-meerschaum.tn: A Missouri Meerschaum entry whose stamp casting was not recorded.

sasieni-8-dots-4-on-each-side.tn: An inlay of eight dots total, arranged in fours on each face of the stem.
sasieni-8-dots-4-on-each-side.not: This stamp belongs to Sasieni's pre-transition period, 1927-1939. Because the four-dot arrangement is repeated on both faces of the stem, an eight-dot layout results.

rows: Sasieni (fishtail cursive) "Grosvenor" London Made, Made in England (curved) Pat. No. 1513428
Sasieni (fishtail cursive) "Marlow" London Made, Made in England (curved)
Sasieni (fishtail cursive) London Made, Made in England (curved) PAT. No. 1513428

alternative-stem-marking.tn: A stamp consisting of the name 'Barling', the wording 'London England', and a model number.

nikotex.tn: The letters "SA" enclosed in an oval; a gnome figure on the right side.

the-briar-squire.tn: A two-letter stamp on the stem.
the-briar-squire.not: The Briar Squire Ltd. was a pipe and tobacco shop that operated from 1977 to 1983 at 6000 Northwest Highway in Crystal Lake, Illinois. Records also note the name Squire Briar was used on one of Linkman Co.'s product lines.

fabrizio-romeo.tn: "Fabrizio Romeo" lettering in two lines on the left side.

aurelia.tn: A clover motif; the left face bears the stamp "Aurelia Saint Claude veritable."

david-jones-sydney.not: David Jones is an Australian department store chain founded in 1838. Since the three-pronged spear stamp on the stem matches that of Britannia, another Comoy's sub-brand, the pipes are considered to have been made in Comoy's workshops.

derby-2.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle; "Derby De Luxe Briar" lettering on the left face.
derby-2.not: The identity of the English firm using the Derby label is not definitively known. Records indicate this stamp has no connection to the leather-covered Italian-origin Derby pipes.

executive.tn: "Charatan Make, London England" and "Executive" lettering on the shank.
executive.not: After 1965, some Executive pipes had the bowl top carved to give a plateau-briar appearance.

kaywoodie-coral-white-briar.tn: "Kaywoodie" and "Coral White Briar" lettering on the lower left face.
kaywoodie-coral-white-briar.not: This stamp was used between 1958 and 1972. All pipes in the Coral line carry the same rustic finish. See also the White Briar stamp for the related line.

brio.not: A brand of Ibéricas de Pipas.

rows: Brio High Class Briar Made in Spain

danny.tn: Logo consisting of a letter enclosed within a circle.
danny.not: Records indicate the pipes carried the inscription "Best French Briar".

savinelli-long-john.tn: On the underside, the Savinelli stamp struck alongside a shield figure.
savinelli-long-john.not: The model's shank is made of two interlocking pieces, giving it an unusually long Canadian shape. The same construction is also used in Savinelli's Doppio series and in KB&B's The Pickwick pipe.

york-2.tn: The words "York De Luxe" alongside a single-letter motif.

salvatella.tn: An "S" on the stem that can also be read as two bent pipes.
salvatella.not: In Catalan, "bosc" means forest. One example has a wide briar disc set on the left side of the stem; the light-colored shank on the same pipe is not briar, and records suggest it may be boxwood or lemon wood. Other brands producing pipes with briar shanks include Barnaby, Il Ceppo, Kaywoodie Allbriar, and LHS (Purex Allbriar).

pipe-maker.tn: A logo in the form of a solid ring.

sasieni-preston.tn: Four dots on the stem; a fishtail-style cursive "Sasieni" stamp on the underside.
sasieni-preston.not: This four-dot stamp belongs to the pre-transitional period of 1924-1945.

savinelli-garda.tn: A star motif on the stem.
savinelli-garda.not: Other Savinelli series carrying the same stem logo are Savinelli Antique Shell, Savinelli Oscar, and Savinelli Sila.

roger-s.tn: Motif made of bars arranged side by side.
roger-s.not: A brand of the Roger's Imports company.

w-h.tn: A clover-leaf motif stamped on the stem.
w-h.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, the brand belongs to William Hendrix of Ulster Park, New York.

sasieni-8dot.tn: Eight dots total, four on each face of the stem.
sasieni-8dot.not: A post-transition stamp, dating from 2001 onward. Production of this double four-dot layout began in the same period as the 5Dot.

rows: Made in London (within a circle), England

modernage.tn: A two-letter text stamp with the name "Modernage" on the left side and a French production notice on the right side.

big-bill.tn: A two-letter logo set within a diamond.
big-bill.not: Big Bill is a brand of The Briar Pipeworks Ltd., founded in 1933 in Marsa, Malta. See also Grandmaster.

duke.tn: "Duke" and "Dr Grabow" lettering on the left face.
duke.not: Dr. Grabow's Duke line went into production in 1969.

pollner.tn: Logo-free stamp; "OP - Studio" on the underside.
pollner.not: Otto Pollner Jr (1925-2004) was the third generation of a pipe-making family founded by his grandfather Karl in 1878. He also wrote books on pipes; the workshop is now carried on by his son Otto-Karl.

sasieni-sashar.tn: The stamp carries the text "Sashar" alongside the inscription "By Sasieni."

ole-holm.tn: An "Ole Holm" stamp with the maker's name spelled out on the underside.
ole-holm.not: The pipes were made by the Danish craftsman Ole Holm, who is no longer living.

rows: Ole Holm, Danish Hand Made, 79 N

raganella.tn: A single dot on the stem (red on some models) or a letter inside a diamond; "Raganella" name on the shank.
raganella.not: The DAC stamp abbreviates the name Duranti Anselmi Castelfidardo. The brand has been stamped as Raganella, La Raganella, Non Canta La Raganella, and NCLR; the name means "the frog doesn't croak," referring to tobacco juice not gurgling. Some models were made for the Montanari pipe and tobacco shop in Modena, others for Lubinski Ltd., Italy's largest pipe importer as of 2005; see also Anselmi (Adriano).

wimbledon.tn: A diamond-shaped logo; the stamp "Wimbledon 810" on the body.
wimbledon.not: Records indicate that the shape of the logo alone is enough to identify the pipe as a Briarcraft product.

papalia.not: The workshop's maker is Gerardo Papalia; as of 2007, output was around 100-120 pipes per year. The bow-tie-shaped stamp is recorded as having been discontinued around 2009.

versailles.tn: The word "Versailles" on a single line, with "Made in France" beneath it.
versailles.not: Versailles is the export brand Ropp used for its leather-covered pipes.

comfort.tn: Single red dot on the stem.

saint-clair.tn: Word stamp on the left face formed from the letters of the brand name.

rows: Saint Clair, The modern styling of St Claude

grosvenor.tn: The stamp text "Charatan, of London, Grosvenor" along with a model number.
grosvenor.not: Pipes bearing this stamp are believed to have been carved in France. Distinguishing marks include a small difference in how the letters C and P are joined, the phrase "of London" used instead of "London England", and a "France" stamp beneath the stem.

age-bgelund.tn: Multi-letter word stamp; the name "Åge Bøgelund".
age-bgelund.not: Åge Bøgelund headed production at the Bari workshop from 1978 to 1993.

anselmi.tn: Single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.
anselmi.not: Made by Adriano Anselmi. He worked alone at first, then together with Alcide Duranti ("Non Canta La Raganella"). See also AAA.

bel-air.tn: A letter stamp with 'Bel-Air' on the underside.
bel-air.not: The same logo also appears on the Brentwood brand.

rows: Bel-Air, London Made, Made In England, 392

mickles.tn: A text stamp combining a two-dot motif with the name 'Mickles,' the country, and the year.
mickles.not: The pipes of this brand were made by Clarence Mickles; records list him among deceased makers.

tao-ilsted.tn: An anchor symbol in the stamp.
tao-ilsted.not: The brand is used for work Jens "Tao" Nielsen and Poul Ilsted occasionally produce together. Nielsen previously worked at sea.

s-e-thile.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo data is on record.

brigham-three-dots.tn: Three dots on the stem, arranged horizontally, vertically, or in a triangle, sometimes as one large dot with two small ones.
brigham-three-dots.not: Three dots set side by side on the stem correspond to the 600 series shape numbers, while three dots in a triangle correspond to the 300 series.

tokutomi.tn: No separate logo mark; the inscription "H. Tokutomi" on the left face, along with the country name and year.
tokutomi.not: The maker, Hiroyuki Tokutomi, was born in 1948 and learned pipe making from Sixten Ivarsson. The letters "B N" in the stamp pay tribute to Bo Nordh. Records indicate annual production of around 150-200 pipes as of about 2007.

certified-purex.tn: The letters "LHS" enclosed in a diamond (rhombus).

rows: Certified Purex, LHS [within a diamond], Imported Briar
Certified Purex, LHS [within a diamond], Imported Briar, Caboose

after-hours.tn: "Charatan's Make" and "London England" lines on the underside; "After Hours" on the extension piece.

dino-da-campione.tn: "Dino da Campione" lettering used together with two snail figures.

pipe-den.tn: A single dot on the stem.

blue-spot.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.
blue-spot.not: Some examples show the blue dot faded with age. The word 'BLUE' appears above the dot on some pipes and below the light-blue dot on others.

rows: Real Briar, Foreign (within a diamond), Blue Spot, Regd. No. 8732445
Real Briar, Foreign (within a diamond), Blue Spot

rasmussen-2.tn: Decorative round-dot mark; no stamp on the pipe.

redonian.tn: Letter set inside a circle as the logo; "Redonian" on the shank.
redonian.not: A brand of John Redman Ltd.; records associate it with the Palace Factory building in London. See also Buckingham.

rows: De Luxe, London Made, Made in England

tatu-pipe.tn: An emblem made of two pipes side by side.
tatu-pipe.not: The maker is Tatsuo Tajima, born 1955; he came from a background in film and graphic design and began making pipes in 2005. On the pipes, the first two digits of the number indicate the year of production (10 = 2010), and the following two or three digits indicate the production sequence within that year.

lars-of-denmark.tn: A two-letter monogram; the letters most likely read "dK".
lars-of-denmark.not: This brand is not related to Lars Mikael Ivarsson, the son of Sixten Ivarsson.

danish-design.tn: Logo with a mammal figure; the "Danish Design" stamp appears on one face of the shank.
danish-design.not: Records link it to the Oldenkott and Eminent brands.

sasieni-ivory.tn: A blue letter S on the stem.
sasieni-ivory.not: The blue "S" logo appears in some examples set perpendicular to the stem axis and turned on its side, and in others placed above the stem parallel to the axis.

reputation.tn: Crown-motif logo; "Big Ben Reputation Made in France" on the shank.
reputation.not: Records question the link between this stamp and the Dutch Big-Ben brand: there is no hyphen between "Big" and "Ben", and the same stamp and logo layout also appear on pipes named "Silverking" and "Gold King".

rows: Big Ben Reputation Made in France

vox-pop.tn: A ring motif on the stem; an emblem together with the words "Vox Pop" on the body.
vox-pop.not: Vox Pop is one of the brands of the Penn Tobacco Company, founded in 1901 in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, by Russell Uhl (d. 1914) and Henry Weigand (d. 1942). The company had four pipe lines: Bruce Peters, Silver Mac Duff, Vox Pop, and Broadcaster. The pipes were made for Penn by Henry Leonard & Thomas, and were sold only through coupons from the company's tobacco packages.

kovalev.not: Maker Roman Kovalev (b. 1971) makes pipes alongside working as a neurologist, hence the "DOC" stamp on his pipes. His pipes carry no grading or dating stamp. Records indicate he has also used strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo) wood in addition to briar.

vander-elst.tn: The name "Vander Elst" in a two-letter arrangement on the left face, together with the phrase "Selected Briar."
vander-elst.not: Vander Elst is a brand of Tabacofina Vander Elst NV, a cigar and tobacco manufacturer based in Antwerp.

antoniewski.not: Made by Bartlomiej (Bart) Antoniewski, born 1961. He apprenticed under Ryszard Filar for two years, 1985-1986, before founding his own brand in 1989. The BAC in the stamp refers to BAC ART PIPES (owned by Marek Lejzorowicz), which took over US distribution as of 2012.

gourvelos.tn: A logo on the underside consisting of the maker's name, a star grade, and the letters "KG".
gourvelos.not: The grading rises from one star to four stars.

fader-s.tn: "FADER'S" lettering accompanied by a target motif of concentric rings.
fader-s.not: Fader's is a tobacconist that has been in business since 1891.

rows: FADER'S Filter pipe, Imported Briar, Italy

briarcliff.tn: A single dot on the stem; the shank reads "Briarcliff."
briarcliff.not: A brand of the Penn Tobacco Company. The firm was founded in 1901 in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, by Russell Uhl (d. 1914) and Henry Weigand (d. 1942). See also Bruce Peters, Broadcaster, Vox Pop.

lhs.tn: The letters "LHS" within a diamond-shaped frame.
lhs.not: The abbreviation LHS denotes the firm L&H Stern. Barrister, London Royal, and Stanhope are second brands of the company. A grading chart dated 1944 is on record for the brand.

rows: Barrister, LHS (within a diamond) Real Briar
LHS (within a diamond), Purex, Pat. N° 1587048, Real Briar

perlux.tn: "Super Perlux Ecume" on the left side.
perlux.not: Pipes bearing this stamp have meerschaum-lined chambers.

frey.tn: An oval inlay of ivory and brass on the stem.
frey.not: These stamps are from the brand's early period. The maker, Michael J. Frey, has stopped production.

forester.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle, topped with a crown motif.

gurra.tn: No logo; the underside bears "Gurra" and a country stamp.
gurra.not: The pipes are made by Lars-Göran "Gurra" Markunger, born in 1960. Alongside his work at a glass factory, he has made pipes since 2005.

weaver.tn: No logo stamp on the stem; the letters "BAW" and a Latin phrase appear on the underside.
weaver.not: The Latin phrase in the stamp, "Vepres Tubuli Fumantibus," roughly means "briar pipes for smoking"; vepres means bramble/thicket.

invicta-briars.tn: A faintly struck rearing-horse figure; a round, wood-colored dot on the stem.

savinelli-capri.tn: A shield-shaped crest stamp with two crossed pipes at the top; the words "Savinelli Capri" and "Root Briar" appear on the shank.
savinelli-capri.not: The example uses Savinelli's early four-digit shape code. In the crest logo the two pipes are crossed at the top; Savinelli's crest logos vary in this detail by period.

rows: Savinelli Capri, Root Briar [Coat of arms]

jolly-roger-2.tn: A logo featuring a human figure; the words "Jolly Roger" on the underside.

banker.tn: A crown motif; the left face bears the stamp "Banker."

mis-loisirs.tn: On the left side, 'Mis Loisirs' in two lines; on the right side, the text 'St. Claude.'
mis-loisirs.not: One of many brands to come from an unidentified factory in Saint-Claude.

antique.tn: Logo formed of a single letter and a star motif.
antique.not: Antique is the brand of German pipe importer and dealer Hans Richter (deceased). This label was used mainly to distribute pipes made by Pierre Morel Senior; some were also of Danish origin.

jacky-berrod.tn: The name "Jacky Berrod" on the left face, with "Fait Main" and "St Claude France" on the right face.
jacky-berrod.not: Records indicate the pipes are tied to the Berrod-Regad factory in Saint-Claude.

rows: G, Fait Main, St Claude France

lindstrom.tn: A single blue dot on the stem; diamond- and triangle-shaped inlays are also seen.

safari.tn: Logo depicting a mammal alongside the text "Safari."

guinea-grain.tn: The handwritten word "Barling" and the Barling cross in the stamp.
guinea-grain.not: The Guinea Grain line is the only Barling line, in the pre-transition period, to have the brand name stamped in script. The letters EB in the stamp denote Edward Barling, while EL denotes the size.

woodart.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter set within a circle; the stamp "Woodart" on the left face.

nordh.tn: No stamp casting or logo data is on record.

anne-julie.tn: Ornamented round inlay in the stem.
anne-julie.not: Made by Anne Julie Rasmussen, born 1940; wife of Poul Rasmussen. See also Norup (Lars Christensen) and Suhr.

rows: Anne Julie, of Denmark, By Hand, 2

playboy.tn: A stamp featuring a mammal figure; the shank reads "PLAYBOY".
playboy.not: The pipes were distributed by the American men's magazine of the same name.

tally-ho.not: The name Tally Ho was used both by the French firm Vuillard & Strauss and by the English firm Hardcastle. Since its stamps and logo match those of Argyle, another Hardcastle sub-brand, this pipe is recorded as English-made.

albertson.tn: A single-letter mark on the stem.
albertson.not: The brand was produced at the Hilson factory.

rows: S 16, Alberston, Special, Made in Belgium

br.not: Records link the brand to the French Berrod-Regad group, though this connection is not confirmed.

fremont.tn: Two dots on the stem; a letter P enclosed in a diamond in the stamp.
fremont.not: The brand belongs to the Reiss-Premier Co company.

rows: P (within a diamond), Fremont, Italian Briar

71.tn: "Stanwell" stamp without the crown emblem on the underside, along with registration number 969-48.
71.not: In this example the brand name is stamped in its form without the crown emblem.

rows: Stanwell, Regd. No. 969-48, Hand Made, Made in Denmark, 71

j-paul-tucker.tn: The text "J. Paul Tucker" on the shank along with a London-made mark.

rows: J. Paul Tucker, Made in, London. England

pierre-cardin.tn: Logo made up of a single letter.
pierre-cardin.not: Records indicate that pipes sold under this brand were mostly carved by Jean Lacroix. Other luxury brands, such as Gucci, Hermès, and Vuitton, have also produced pipes.

santambrogio.tn: A crown motif alongside the text "Santambrogio."
santambrogio.not: The brand was founded in 1912 by Stefano Santambrogio (1867-1951). His sons Renzo and Armando ran the factory until 1981, after which Renzo's son Stefano (b. 1952) took over production. The script-lettered stamps are of more recent date; the name Stefano is recorded as having been used for the second-quality line.

rows: Stefano Santambrogio, fatta a mano, Italy

snahti.not: The maker is Hans Wormit. Grading, in ascending order, runs copper, brass, and silver dots; the finest pipes are marked with five silver dots.

twin-bore.tn: The words "Twin Bore" on the left face.
twin-bore.not: This is a model produced with a twin-bore stem. Records indicate it is one of Comoy's secondary brands. Other brands using a twin-bore stem include Beau Nash, Grand Master, Kaywoodie Allbriar, Durobit, Leonard's, Radice, and Siam.

peterson-made-in-ireland.tn: The 'Made in Ireland' stamp struck in block letters over two lines.
peterson-made-in-ireland.not: This pipe dates to the pre-Republic period, i.e. before 1949. The country-of-manufacture stamp is struck in block letters over two lines.

kaywoodie-early-suntan.tn: Letters KBB set within a clover on the left side of the shank, "Suntan" lettering on the right side.
kaywoodie-early-suntan.not: The X to the right of the shape number (7002) was stamped by Kaywoodie to indicate the bowl had been replaced under warranty. The Suntan finish was produced between 1928 and the late 1950s; examples bearing the "Made in England" stamp date from later.

old-rarity.tn: A target-shaped logo made of concentric rings.
old-rarity.not: Because it bears the same target logo, records suggest this may be a second brand of Linkman's.

werner-burmann.tn: A logo consisting of the letters WB on the stem; in some examples embossed, in others rendered as a white inlay.
werner-burmann.not: The brand's maker, Werner Bürmann, died in June 2012. Records indicate that the technique of embossing the logo onto the stem was first applied by the maker Rainer Barbi.

celtic-tobacco.tn: A silver-colored crest bearing a Celtic cross.
celtic-tobacco.not: Made in the Czech Republic by Dušan Doubek. Grading is shown by the number of dots struck on the shank, from one to six; higher dot counts indicate higher grades.

rows: Logo: silver blazon with a Celtic cross

dolly.tn: "DOLLY" lettering used together with a multi-bar motif.
dolly.not: A similar logo also appears on the Ercole Bogni brand.

early-stampings.tn: "Wallenstein Germany" block-letter stamp in two lines on the underside, along with a code number.
early-stampings.not: The first digit of the code number gives the year, and the last two digits give the production sequence; number 611 denotes the 11th pipe made in 2006. This coding was discontinued in 2008, and the last coded pipe bears number 849 (April/May 2008).

bridge.not: Information on this brand is drawn, according to the records, from the work of Wilczak and Colwell.

rows: Bridge, London Paris New York, Meerschaumlined 79

savinelli-capt-warren.tn: A text stamp with "Capt Warren" on the left face.
savinelli-capt-warren.not: This Savinelli series shares its name with Ser Jacopo's system pipes. See also the Captain Warren brand.

carmignani.not: Pipes made for this tobacconist between 1970 and 1979, before Fritz Becker established his own brand.

ruthenberg.tn: No logo; the left face carries a compass emblem along with the words "Ruthenberg," "USA," and "Handmade."
ruthenberg.not: Brian Ruthenberg began carving pipes part-time in 2001 and moved to full-time production in 2005. Until October 2002 his pipes were stamped with the maker's initials "BAR"; after that date he used an arched "RUTHENBERG" with "USA" and "HANDMADE" set in a straight line beneath it, the two digits in the stamp giving the production year (03 = 2003). The early grading scale, discontinued in 2002, ran in ascending order 04, 03, 02, 01, 00; semi-rustic and rustic finishes are marked R1 and R2, the compass stamp is applied to top-tier pipes with flawless smooth or evenly ring-grained surfaces, and pipes marked "F" for flawed or filled are not offered for sale.

chacom.tn: No stamp casting or logo detail is on record.

henley.tn: Single-letter logo; the shank carries the "Henley" name.
henley.not: The pipes were made at Stanwell's workshops in Borup.

savinelli-3.tn: An architectural figure alongside the text "Pisa."

matzhold.tn: On the underside, the text "Matzhold" with a small sperm-shaped mark beside it.

danet-s.not: The brand was imported from Denmark to the US by BRANDT IMPORT; the stamp is sometimes struck as DANET. Records suggest this may be a label used for pipes made by Georg Jensen.

kaywoodie-the-drinkless-shellcraft.tn: "07 The Drinkless Shellcraft" on the underside and a white logo echoing the shape of the Drinkless mechanism.
kaywoodie-the-drinkless-shellcraft.not: The white logo echoes the shape of the Drinkless mechanism used on these pipes from 1924 onward. The interlocking tenon on this example dates the pipe to before 1930; the shank carries no KB&B clover stamp. See also Kaywoodie's Shellcraft line and the current Italian-made Kaywoodie Shellcraft.

bruyere.tn: A butterfly figure on the stem.
bruyere.not: Records indicate this pipe cannot be linked to a specific brand; the stamp points only to the Saint-Claude production center in France. The butterfly figure on the stem is a rarely seen logo.

pipelane-ltd.tn: A crest-shaped logo; the stamp reads "Pipelane, Ltd., Perfection".
pipelane-ltd.not: The company, which operated tobacco shops and sales stands, was founded in 1961; it is headquartered in Seattle.

siam.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; the left face carries the "Siam" and "London Made" stamps.
siam.not: Records indicate the example pipe was made with a double-bore stem.

humidor.tn: A logo of a single letter.
humidor.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, the brand was marketed by R. Wheatley & Son, a dealer in fishing tackle. It is also possible the brand was a house label of a cigar and tobacco shop.

altinay.tn: An ornamented circular logo, used on meerschaum pipes.
altinay.not: Altinay Pipe Co. Ltd. was founded in Eskişehir in 1964. No stamp appears on the meerschaum body.

fuhrmann.tn: A single dot on the stem; a figure of a man smoking a pipe on the left side.
fuhrmann.not: Records indicate the pipe, judging by its craftsmanship, can be dated to the 1930s and is most likely a private label for a Viennese tobacconist. Am Hof, named in the stamp, is the largest and oldest square in Vienna's inner city.

newmarket.not: The Charatan family era spans 1910-1960. Shape number 58 is known as the "Newmarket".

karl-erik.tn: A stem mark of two letters used together with a crown motif.
karl-erik.not: The brand is associated with Ottendahl, Champ of Denmark, Golden Danish, Knute of Denmark, and Shelburne.

le-chevalier.tn: A figural logo in the shape of a knight's head.
le-chevalier.not: There is also a separate brand bearing the name "Chevalier". For another brand using a knight's-head figure, see Royal York.

former.tn: Overlapping letters G and H on the underside, together with the "Former" signature.
former.not: These stamps belong to Former's early period. Records indicate the pipe was made during the maker's time in Switzerland for the Georg Huber tobacco shop in Munich; the overlapping G and H near the signature refer to that shop.

citation.not: Linked to the Alpha Citation record (see).

peterson-made-in-eire.tn: On the right side, the curved 'Made in Eire' stamp.
peterson-made-in-eire.not: The "Made in Eire" stamp within a circle dates the pipe to between 1938 and 1947.

tinsky.tn: No stamp description available in the records.

dover-pipes.tn: Logo based on a single-letter element; the stamp carries the name "Dover" in quotation marks and the wording "Pipes".

merlin.tn: An animal-motif logo featuring an antelope figure.
merlin.not: For the same antelope logo, see Safari.

howard.tn: No separate logo stamp; the text "Tom Howard" appears on the left face.

captain-black.tn: An anchor-motif stamp; the name "Captain Black" and the series name "Helmsman" appear on the left face.
captain-black.not: Captain Black pipes were made in both England and France. The Helmsman series, however, is always made in France.

kaywoodie-custom-grain.tn: "Kaywoodie", "Custom Grain", and "Imported Briar" lettering on the left face.
kaywoodie-custom-grain.not: This stamp was used during the 1960-1971 period.

tsuge.tn: A single red dot or three dots on the stem; the "Tsuge" brand name on the shank.
tsuge.not: Azuma and Esterd are recorded as the brand's second lines.

la-strada.tn: A pipe-shaped emblem and the words "La Strada".
la-strada.not: An export brand seen in the Tinder Box catalog.

gordon-nesbit.tn: A multi-letter logo on the stem; the left side reads "Gordon Nesbit Ltd" together with a patent number.
gordon-nesbit.not: Although the stamp reads NESBIT, the 1951 patent document spells it NISBET.

la-salle.tn: A triangular-motif logo; the words "La Salle" on the left side.
la-salle.not: La Salle is the import brand Iwan Ries & Co. used for its leather-covered pipes made in France. These pipes appear in a 1962 tobacconist catalog.

la-ruche.tn: A hive-shaped motif and the words "La Ruche" in quotation marks.
la-ruche.not: The same logo is also used on the Honey-Swete brand; the logo on Savinelli's Melita series is similar to it.

bromage.tn: A B set inside a diamond (rhombus) on the stem.
bromage.not: The brand of A. Bromage & Co Ltd.

connoisseur-2.tn: "Connoisseur" lettering on the stem with a handwritten "Burak" signature.
connoisseur-2.not: Connoisseur pipes were not fitted with a ferrule by the maker; stamps were struck on the stem only when there was no room left on the shank. Examples with a ferrule or a stamped stem are therefore exceptions to the rule.

bowles-son-ltd.tn: A single-letter stamp; the words "Bowles & Son Ltd" and "Cardiff & Newport" on the shank.
bowles-son-ltd.not: The own-name brand of a tobacconist operating in Cardiff and Newport.

savinelli-rock-grain.tn: Logo bearing an animal-figure emblem; the stamp reads "Savinelli" and "Rock Grain".
savinelli-rock-grain.not: This model does not use a shape code or shield stamp. The logo on the stem is the same as that of the "Hand Made" series.

sasieni-friar.tn: A diamond motif on the stem.

holiday.tn: A logo of two letters; the stamp carries the text "Holiday".

douwe-egbert.tn: No separate logo; "Douwe Egberts House Blend" lettering on the top surface.
douwe-egbert.not: This pipe was made under license by an unidentified Danish manufacturer. The Douwe Egberts company is the maker of Amphora pipe tobaccos; see Amphora.

purdy.tn: Turtle figure on the underside along with the name "Will Purdy" and the production year.
purdy.not: Maker Will Purdy (b. 1958) is a self-taught pipe maker; he finished his first pipe in 2000.

rainer-barbi.tn: Raised letter emblem on the stem; curved "Barbi" stamp on the shank.
rainer-barbi.not: The raised emblem and curved stamps were used from 1981 to 2011. The "Styled by Barbi" stamp dates from 1975-1981; stamps combining the first and last name also appear on the stem.

marshall-field.tn: A shield-shaped logo with a ship motif; the text 'Marshall Field Smoke Shop' on the shank.
marshall-field.not: For other brands using the same ship-motif logo, see Deauville and Neptune.

frank-pfeifen.tn: Letter F enclosed in a circle.
frank-pfeifen.not: The brand belongs to German craftsman Frank Stollenwerk (b. 1977), who trained under craftsman Rainer Barbi. The F in the stamp is the initial of the maker's name.

redwood.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; "Redwood" on the left side.

martel.tn: A single-letter logo; the text 'Martel' on the shank.
martel.not: Maker Paul Martel worked in Herbignac. The workshop was later sold to Patrice Sébilo; when Sébilo stopped carving pipes, Trever Talbert began working at the same location in 2002.

boschetto.tn: A logo shared with the Grandmaster brand; no detailed stamp casting is on record.
boschetto.not: Records mention an example made from olive wood. The same logo is also seen on the Grandmaster brand.

gabrieli-pipes.tn: A star mark on the underside together with "Gabrieli" and the place of manufacture.
gabrieli-pipes.not: Maker Dan Chlebove carved his first pipe in 1998.

five-stars.tn: A star-motif stamp; the left side reads "Five Stars".

rows: Five Stars, Senior, Made in France

pol.tn: The letters "POL" enclosed in an oval or triangle.
pol.not: This is the brand of Paul Morand of Saint Claude; the business has ceased operations.

golden-burl.not: One of Ropp's export brands. The same name was also used for a product line by John Surrey.

marchetti.tn: An oval dot on both the top and bottom of the stem.
marchetti.not: The maker of the brand is Phil DeFant.

rows: [one oval dot on the top and bottom sides]

kaywoodie-collector-s.tn: The text "Collector's Kaywoodie" on the left face.
kaywoodie-collector-s.not: The Collector's line appeared around 1968, initially offered in six styles (1C-6C) with smooth and sandblasted finishes.

sun.tn: A gnome silhouette on the stem.
sun.not: The gnome silhouette on the stem differs in small details from the figure used in Brebbia's Golden Gnome line.

pino.tn: Cursive "Pino" on the shank, with the words "Sandflame" and "Italy".

kayne.tn: A mark of three dots on the stem.

paul-s-cayuga.tn: A single letter or several letters on the stem; the shank reads "Paul's Cayuga".
paul-s-cayuga.not: The shop was founded in 1913 in Flint, Michigan. As of 2008 records, its operator was Paul T. Spaniola.

rows: Paul's Cayuga, Oil Cured, Algerian Briar, Made in England

andre.not: The maker is André Mermet, a French craftsman who emigrated to the US; his son later carried on production. The pipes were made for the Barclay Rex and Wilke pipe shops. Some examples have the year of production stamped on them.

steve-johnson.tn: "S. Johnson" spelled out on the left side, along with a grade stamp.
steve-johnson.not: The pipe is recorded as having been made in the 1980s. The part-time maker worked at Holt's Tobacco Shop in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

hiland-s.tn: The text "Hiland's" accompanied by a bird figure.

freshman.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.

flame.tn: A stamp with "Castello" and the maker's name on the left side, and a year number within the logo.
flame.not: The number 52 in the logo corresponds to 1999, also the year the finish was introduced. In its first two production years Flame pipes did not carry the "Flame" stamp. The Flame finish replaced Epoca and was carved by the same maker who made the Epoca pipes; production ceased after his retirement around 2009-2010.

rows: 21 24 Castello, Made in Cantu Italy, Carlo Scotti

kaywoodie-shellcraft.tn: The underside carries a four-digit shape number along with the "Shellcraft" and "Kaywoodie" stamps.
kaywoodie-shellcraft.not: These stamps belong to a Shellcraft pipe made in the early 1930s with a Synchro-stem system; early Shellcrafts had a rustic finish, whereas this example is sandblasted. The drinkless logo on the stem was replaced by a clover, and the assignment of a four-digit shape number shows the model had been folded into the Kaywoodie lines. See also early Shellcraft and Made in Italy Shellcraft.

gordon.tn: A crown-and-diamond logo on the stem; the shank reads "Bruyere" within a diamond.
gordon.not: An English brand; records indicate it was founded around 1910-1920 by Samuel Gordon.

rows: GORDON, E...A, Bruyere (within a diamond) Made in France

jarl.tn: A logo of a single letter beneath a crown motif.
jarl.not: Records indicate the brand's maker is Jørgen Larsen. See also Thayne.

collection-3.tn: The Castello logo on the left face along with the text "Occhio di Pernice" and the Carlo Scotti signature.
collection-3.not: "Occhio di Pernice" (partridge eye) refers to the birdseye grain. Dating is done by the number inside the castle emblem; the number 54 corresponds to the year 2001.

munalli.tn: A two-letter stamp on the stem.

allerton.tn: A logo in the shape of an oak leaf with an acorn.

sicana.tn: Logo variants consisting of the brand name lettering and a single letter; the left face carries the "Sicana" stamp.
sicana.not: Records indicate Sicana is among the older brands of the Gros-Grenier-Ostorero & Cie factory. Other brands from the same maker include GOC, OSA, and Prior.

blakemar-briars.tn: No stamp image or casting is on record.

hansen-briar.tn: No separate logo; the text "Hansen Briar Handmade" on the left face.
hansen-briar.not: Hansen Briar is Poul Hansen's brand.

dr-john.tn: Stamp with the brand name written in its own lettering style.
dr-john.not: Records indicate the brand's factory building is in London.

von-erck.tn: A greenish-blue mother-of-pearl dot inlaid into an exotic-wood spacer on the stem.
von-erck.not: The letters "MM" in the stamp indicate the briar block was cut by Mimmo (Romeo Domenico) in Taggia, Italy.

festival-of-britain.tn: Single-letter logo; the stamp reads "Festival of Britain".
festival-of-britain.not: It is not known which English manufacturer the brand belongs to.

gianini.tn: Single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.

telford-s.tn: A single-letter stamp on the stem.

britannica.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle; the word "Britannica" on the shank.

georg-jensen.tn: A stamp consisting of a star motif and "Georg Jensen".
georg-jensen.not: Several stamp forms appear on the shank. Pipes destined for the U.S. market were stamped only "Jensen". The same star logo was also used by the Cortina and Stern brands.

rows: Georg Jensen Made in Denmark Pipes

guardsman.tn: A logo of a single letter on the stem.

alpha-kappa-omega.tn: A single-letter logo; the stamps read 'Alpha Kappa' and 'Alpha Omega.'

talamona.tn: A ring-and-concentric-circle target motif on the stem.

golden-gate.tn: Two-letter logo on the stem; "Golden Gate" written on the lower left of the shank.
golden-gate.not: The source lists this alongside other pipe brands of Eastern Bloc origin: ARK and Howal (East Germany), Nagykörösi/Szabó Körös (Hungary). Records indicate the "Veresk" firm's pipes were sold with a warranty card.

wombaroo-pipes.tn: No separate logo is used; the letters "WBR," three diamonds, and a model number are stamped on the underside.
wombaroo-pipes.not: The maker, Marty Simm, has been carving pipes in Toronto since around 2007.

comoy-s-golden-grain.tn: A stamp reading "Comoy's Golden Grain" on the left side.

talbert.tn: Two metal dots in place of a brand emblem on the stem; "Talbert" on the shank.
talbert.not: Trever Talbert worked from 2002 to May 2009 in the workshop he took over from Patrice Sébilo in Herbignac (Brittany); the raw material for his bog-oak pipes also came from Sébilo's stock, from oak recovered from the Brière marshes and radiocarbon-dated to 1497-1171 BC. The letters S and C in the stamps indicate the Signature and Collector grades. Records indicate that for roughly six months around 2006, molten metal dots equal in number to the grade were set into the stems of Ligne Bretagne pipes.

lee.tn: Brass- or gold-colored five- or seven-pointed stars on the stem.
lee.not: The number and shape of the stars inlaid on the stem vary from pipe to pipe: one or three seven-pointed brass stars, or two or three five-pointed gold-colored stars, are seen.

lorraine.tn: The word "Lorraine" in a single line on the left side of the shank.
lorraine.not: The maker of this French-origin brand could not be determined from the records.

danish-pride.tn: Crown-figure logo; "Danish Pride by Ben Wade" stamp on the underside.
danish-pride.not: Danish Pride is one of Ben Wade's sub-brands (or production lines) from 1972-1989. During this period the British brand's pipes were carved in Denmark by Preben Holm.

rows: Golden Tan, Hand made in Denmark

gotoh.tn: A stamp on the underside reading "K. GOTOH" signature, date, and country of origin; no logo on the stem.
gotoh.not: The brand's maker is Kei'ichi Gotoh, born 1956.

jobey.tn: A stem mark bearing the brand name; the stamp "Jobey" on the left face.

yashtylov.tn: No emblem on the stem; the name "Yashtylov" set between lines on the underside.
yashtylov.not: Made by Victor Yashtylov; he began pipe making in 2001 and became known after his work appeared online in 2006. Only the maker's name is stamped on the pipes.

m-g-m.not: The abbreviation M.G.M. comes from the name Mario Gasparini Milano. The brand has a wax-drip-surfaced line called "Collectionist."

rows: Briar 1912, Rock Italy M.G.M. [curved beneath the logo] 15

everyman.tn: Motif of multiple bars arranged side by side.
everyman.not: The source links it with the Guildhall, The Lumberman, and The Mansion House brands.

savinelli-estar.tn: "Estar" lettering alongside a shield-shaped emblem and crown motif.

jan-harry.tn: A handwritten "Jan Harry" stamp on the underside.
jan-harry.not: The brand's maker is Jan Harry Seiffert.

shellmoor.tn: Logo on the stem consisting of the letter "S"; the shank carries the "Shellmoor" stamp.
shellmoor.not: On some Shellmoor pipes the "S" on the stem is replaced by the Jobey logo.

lmb.tn: A logo formed from the letters 'LMB' arranged in an arc.

egloff.tn: Plain, single-color round dot on the stem.
egloff.not: Records indicate Egloff Tobaccobar AG ceased operations in 2007.

tagliabue.tn: A round wood-colored inlay and ring motif on the stem.
tagliabue.not: The pipes were carved by Lorenzo Tagliabue (d. 1987) before he took over the Lorenzo firm in 1969. Tagliabue's second brand is Dr Hardy.

quest.tn: Lowercase "quest" on the left side, with a place-of-manufacture stamp.

ivarsson-3.tn: The text ". An Ivarsson . Product" set inside a circle on the underside, with a year stamp beside it.
ivarsson-3.not: Sixten Ivarsson (1910-2001) is one of the leading figures in Danish pipe making. The stamps reflect the maker's long-running collaboration with the Pibe-Dan tobacco shop.

montmartre.not: The windmill motif also appears in the logos of the Fireside and Steffen Müller brands.

savile.tn: A letter logo set within a ring, together with the text "Savile."
savile.not: One of the Beney Ltd. brands.

yello-bole.tn: The letters "KBB" set within a clover and the word "Yello-Bole"; stamps also use letter-in-circle, arrow, ring, and crown motifs.
yello-bole.not: The Yello-Bole line was added in 1932 by Kaufman Brothers & Bondy alongside the KB&B, Reiss-Premier, and Kaywoodie brands. The logo can appear on either the shank or the stem. In the Nova Brylon examples, Brylon is a heat-resistant synthetic material developed by S.M. Frank Co. in 1966 by blending resin with wood flour; the same material was also used for the Medico brand.

rows: Yello-Bole, Reg US Pat Off, Imperial, Cured with real Honey 3024 B

KBB (within a clover), Chinrester, Yello-Bole, Cured with Real Honey
Yello-Bole, Cured with Real Honey, Imperial, Imported Briar

KBB Yello-Bole Premier Cured With Real Honey, Imported Briar

giorgio-orsini.tn: No logo description or stamp record on file.
giorgio-orsini.not: Giorgio Orsini is a master pipe maker working in the Livorno area.

georgetown.tn: Single-letter logo; the left side reads "Georgetown".

radford-s.tn: A gold-colored "R" set axially on the stem.
radford-s.not: Radford's is a house brand of Pöschl Tabak GmbH & Co.; the pipes were made by Chacom.

savinelli-sport.tn: A bird-figure logo; "Sport" on the left side.
savinelli-sport.not: The other Savinelli model bearing the same logo is the Albatross.

auld-erin.not: "Auld" means "old" in Scots, and "Erin" is an old poetic name for Ireland. Records indicate these pipes were made at Peterson's facilities in both Dublin and London.

mr-hyde.tn: No logo or stamp data exists for this brand.

royal-castle.tn: Stamp consisting of a single letter.

rows: Royal Castel, Made in London England

warwick.tn: A motif of a single dot or several bars on the stem; the "LHS" stamp set within a diamond on the left face.
warwick.not: Records indicate the brand is a sub-brand of Comoy or Singleton & Cole. Not to be confused with the Warwyck brand.

worobiec.tn: A logo with a single letter and a star motif; the stamps "H. Worobiec" and "Poland" on the underside.
worobiec.not: The maker, Henryk Worobiec, has continued the pipe-carving craft founded by his father Paweł in Przemyśl since 1979.

hyde-park.not: The same unusual logo was also used on GBD's "Himalaya" and "International" lines.

maxima.tn: A logo formed from the letters of the brand name, with one letter emphasized.

savinelli-doppio.tn: "Savinelli Doppio Filtro" lettering used together with the Savinelli crest.
savinelli-doppio.not: The stamp belongs to a three-piece pipe. Its construction is of the same type as Savinelli's "Long John" and KB&B's "The Pickwick" models.

saillard.tn: Brand name set within an oval.
saillard.not: A stamped horn stem is an uncommon feature.

golden-natural.tn: A single-letter script logo on the stem; the left side reads "Golden Natural".
golden-natural.not: The script "B" logo on the stem appears when the pipe was made for Cellini.

comoy.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo description is on record.

bo-nordh.tn: No logo on the stem; the words 'B. Nordh' on the underside.
bo-nordh.not: The pipes were made by master Bo Nordh (1941-2006); output never exceeded fifty pipes a year. Records indicate the initial "B." was not used until at least the late 1960s, with pipes marked simply 'Nordh' and 'Hand made'. See also Botang, Dollar.

castello-kkkk.tn: A white bar inlaid mark on the stem.
castello-kkkk.not: The white bar was originally made of ivory, later replaced with plastic. The bar has no standard length.

savinelli-la-milano.tn: A bar (line)-motif stamp; the brand and series name written on the left side.

peter-kent.tn: "Peter Kent" inside an oval on the left side, series name and shape number on the right side.
peter-kent.not: The number 9436 in the stamp is GBD's billiard shape number.

pioverna.tn: Solid-ring-shaped logo; the stamp reads "Pioverna" and "Fatta a Mano".

kaywoodie-red-root.not: Red Root was not part of the original Kaywoodie line. It is a pipe shape introduced in 1976, after S.M. Frank acquired Kaywoodie.

morena.tn: A single-letter logo enclosed in a circle.
morena.not: A brand frequently found in the German market, although its maker is unknown.

knightsbridge.tn: "Knightsbridge, London Made" on the left side, "Made in England" on the right side.

holbek.tn: No separate logo; the stamps carry the name "G. Holbek".
holbek.not: Gert Holbek carved these pipes for Pipe-Dan in Copenhagen. Examples bearing only the "G. Holbek" stamp, with no reference to Pipe-Dan, belong to the maker's own production.

rows: 750 REI F 614, [3 stars] A2568 G. HOLBEK

savinelli-punto-oro.tn: A single brass dot on the stem; "Punto Oro" stamp on the shank.
savinelli-punto-oro.not: The dots on Punto Oro pipe stems are made of brass. "SUPER"-stamped Punto Oro models were introduced in the early 1980s and discontinued a few years later.

schowa.tn: No separate logo; the left face carries "Schowa" set between two lines.
schowa.not: The brand of the Schum family, based in Bad König (Odenwald, Hesse). The brand name is derived from syllables of the surname Schum and the place name Odenwald. The factory produced both briar and porcelain (Bavarian-type) pipes.

kikusui.tn: A ring-motif stamp; the characters "榎作" appear in the stamp.
kikusui.not: The character 作 in the stamp means "made by" or "product of", while 榎 corresponds to the name Enoki. The stamp is one of the marks used by a tobacconist in Tokyo.

windsor.tn: A stamp consisting of "Windsor" on the left face and "Saint-Claude" on the right face.

burak.tn: No stamp data is on record.

sahin.tn: Star-motif logo used as a red star or shooting star, together with the text "Sahin."
sahin.not: The brand was founded in 1980. Its address is Anadolu Han on Arpacılar Caddesi in Eminönü Bahçekapı, Istanbul.

sven.tn: "sVen" within a circle, ending in an exclamation mark.
sven.not: The maker of the brand is David Wagner. The same maker also has a brand called Baff.

grc.tn: A decorated round logo on the stem with a single white dot and a single red dot.
grc.not: The maker is Darius Eruch Dah; the letters GRC come from his wife's name, Grace Rachel Christian. The two digits after the slash in the stamp give the year of manufacture; the example pipe dates to 2007. The relative position of the white and red dots varies from pipe to pipe.

the-mayflower.not: The same arrow-motif logo also appears on the Rustique and Shelton Square stamps.

omb.tn: The letters "OMB" enclosed in an oval together with an anchor emblem.
omb.not: According to records, it has not been confirmed whether the stem on this example is original.

rows: Real Briar, OMB (within an oval) Extra

swiss.not: The source links this stem shape to Peterson's P-Lip stem and its variants.

charatan.tn: No stamp rubbing or logo detail is on record.

ark.tn: A stamp in which the brand name is rendered in a lettered script.
ark.not: ARK is a brand produced by Firma A. R. Kuhn in the German Democratic Republic. Other Eastern Bloc pipe brands include Howal (GDR), Nagykörösi Pipes / Szabó Körös Pipes (Hungary), and the Veresk Company's Golden Gate brand (Ukraine).

kaywoodie-la-roche.tn: The words "Kaywoodie, La Roche, St Claude - France" on the shank.

rows: Kaywoodie, La Roche, St Claude - France

stetson.tn: A stamp made up of a letter within a circle; "Stetson Imported Briar" on the shank.

rows: Stetson Imported Briar Made in Italy

lozano.tn: The words "Lozano Briar" on the left side of the shank.

commodore.not: Records indicate the brand was sold by either Comoy or Charatan.

sasieni-windsor.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter set within a circle, together with a crown motif.

brigham-four-dots.tn: Four dots arranged in a diamond or horizontal pattern.

grant-s.tn: A crest-shaped logo together with "Grant's" on the shank.
grant-s.not: The brand is associated with the Sutliff and Corinthian names.

larry-roush.tn: A ring-motif logo; the stamp "Roush" on a silver band.

dr-berger.tn: Brand-name lettering and the two-letter abbreviation "Dr".
dr-berger.not: The brand was created by La Bruyère in the 1930s. Since the firm resumed the name "Chacom" in 1957, examples bearing the "Made by Chacom" stamp are considered to date from after that year.

brewster.tn: A multi-letter stamp; the left face reads "Brewster."
brewster.not: An export brand of an unidentified Italian firm.

dupont.tn: Single-letter logo; "S.T. Dupont" lettering on the shank.
dupont.not: The pipes were produced at other workshops on behalf of the S.T. Dupont brand, known for its luxury goods. Lighter brands Flamidor, Ronson, Myon, and Silver Match also distributed pipes in a similar way.

twibi.tn: "Twibi" and "Old Briar" on the left side.

sportsman-2.tn: A bird-figure logo together with the wording "Sportsman."
sportsman-2.not: Recorded as one of Sasieni's second-line brands; not every example is stamped with the Sasieni name. "London Made By Sasieni" on the right side and "PAT. D-170067" on the left side may also be seen.

savinelli-champagne.not: Savinelli's crown-shaped logos vary by period; this stamp is one of them.

ferndown.tn: A logo spelling out the brand name in letters; the underside carries a starred size stamp.
ferndown.not: The size stamp is given in ascending order with one, two, or three stars. Surface finishes are distinguished as Bark (sandblasted or rustic), Root (smooth, light brown), and Chestnut (smooth, brown or red).

rows: Hand Made In England, Les Wood

bennington.tn: A single-letter logo; the left face reads 'Bennington.'

lacroix.tn: A two-letter monogram on the stem, set to resemble a round stone.
lacroix.not: The brand was founded in 1962; its maker, Jean Lacroix, died in 2007. On some examples the monogram on the stem has an extra flourish. The same maker is also associated with the Pierre Cardin and Brittany brands, while the family is linked to the A. Lacroix and JPL brands.

rows: Jean Lacroix Paris 115G2 Maitre Pipier a Saint-Claude

crown-of-england.tn: Emblem made up of five crowns.
crown-of-england.not: Records indicate "Crown of England" may be the brand of H. Perkins & Sons Ltd., which produced a line of the same name.

wdc.tn: The letters "WDC" set within a triangle; a two-dot stamp on the stem.
wdc.not: WDC is an abbreviation of William Demuth Pipe Company. Kensington and Wellington are among the company's lines; Waldorf was used as WDC's imported second brand. The brand should not be confused with the Demuth tobacconist label from Pennsylvania.

rows: WDC (within a triangle) Milano Imported Briar
WDC (within a triangle) Guardsman, Genuine Briar, Deresined Processed
WDC (within a triangle), Dunlop, Kerly Briar
WDC (within a triangle) Demuth, Gold Dot

chevalier.tn: Five-petaled flower-shaped logo on the stem.
chevalier.not: A separate brand named "Le Chevalier" also exists.

signature.tn: Logo on the stem consisting of multiple letters; the shank carries the "Signature" stamp.
signature.not: A brand of Larus & Brother Co. Customers could personalize their pipes by having their own signature or initials engraved next to the "L" logo on the stem.

arita-2.tn: No separate logo; the stamp on the underside is limited to the maker's name and numbers.
arita-2.not: Master carver Takeo Arita (b. 1971) has worked in his father Shizuo's workshop since age six. Grading rises in the order X (rustic or smooth), Y (smooth), and Z (superior-quality pipes). In dating, a two-digit number gives the year of production and a three-digit number the serial number.

jeantet.tn: No logo description or stamp record is available.

ponomarchuk.tn: An airplane figure on the underside, with two pairs of digits beside it.
ponomarchuk.not: Alexandre Ponomarchuk (b. 1971) took up pipe making full-time in 2006 after a career as an airline pilot. Dating relies on two two-digit numbers: the first is the pipe's sequence number for the year, the second is the production year (12 = 2012).

savinelli-grand-prix.tn: A bar-shaped logo on the stem; the shank reads "Savinelli Grand Prix".
savinelli-grand-prix.not: Records indicate nearly all pipes named Grand Prix are leather-covered.

rembrandt.tn: A single letter and star-shaped inlays on the stem.
rembrandt.not: A brand of the National Briar Pipe Co, based in Jersey City, New Jersey. The company's other brands are The Biltmore, Forecaster, Honey Brook, and, after 1960, The Doodler.

kaywoodie-early-super-grain.tn: "KAYWOODIE Super Grain" lettering on the left side of the shank, Synchrostem stamp on the underside.
kaywoodie-early-super-grain.not: Since the PAT. APP. FOR stamp was discontinued in 1932, this example is among the first Super Grain pipes produced.

cellini.tn: A fleur-de-lis inlaid logo on the stem.
cellini.not: The brand of a pipe-only shop that opened in Chicago on April 27, 1929; the pipes were mostly imported, with Brebbia as the main supplier. The shop closed on February 28, 1991. The same logo also appears on Vincenzo Lombardi, another of Brebbia's second brands; other brands using the fleur-de-lis include Ajustomatic, Duke of Kent, Fleur de Lis, Harrington Park, Omega, and Thomas.

rows: Under the shank, near the stem

royal-york.not: For a similar knight's-head logo, see Le Chevalier.

viprati.tn: The words "La Pipa" within an oval alongside the signature "L. Viprati"; clover stamps between diamond marks on the underside.
viprati.not: Luigi Viprati was born in 1953 and has been a full-time pipe maker since 1982. Grading rises from one to five clovers; the grade of three clovers is not used, as the number three is considered unlucky in Italy. The top-grade pipes carry the "Fiammata" stamp; rusticated pipes are not graded.

rows: La Pipa (within an oval) L. Viprati

moulin-rouge.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's "Who Made This Pipe", this is a brand of Lane Ltd. (USA). The pipes are of French or English manufacture, and the series are named after famous painters.

rows: Moulin Rouge, Matisse, Made in France, 212

savinelli-gandale.tn: A shield mark on the underside together with "Savinelli" and "Gandale".

walt-disney.tn: A mammal figure stamped on the stem; the body is made of cherry wood instead of briar.
walt-disney.not: Records indicate this cherry-wood pipe was made by the French manufacturer Ropp.

rows: Walt Disney World © Walt Disney Productions

robinson.tn: Logo based on a single letter; the stamp reads "Robinson & Co, Ltd" and "Singapore".
robinson.not: A brand of Robinson & Co. Ltd, the well-known Singapore and Malaysia retail company. The company operates Robinsons, John Little, and Marks and Spencer stores in the two countries.

masters.tn: On the underside, the text "Masters" and "London Made."

rows: Masters, London Made, Made in London, England, 215

royal-briar.tn: Stamp featuring a crown motif without an arch.
royal-briar.not: Records note the crown shape on this example differs slightly from the brand's usual arched-crown stamp.

dr-robert.tn: "Dr Robert" brand-name lettering on the shank.

davidson.tn: No logo; the underside carries the name "Davidson" within an oval, along with the year of manufacture.
davidson.not: Pipes are numbered in order of manufacture. According to 2011 records, annual production is around 90-100 pipes.

cardiff.tn: A stamp made up of a single letter enclosed in a circle; the name "Cardiff" is written on the underside.

shaabi.tn: The left face carries a mouse figure alongside the text "Manuel Shaabi."
shaabi.not: The maker, Manuel Shaabi, was born in Lebanon in 1950. While working as a furniture maker, he decided to learn pipemaking in 1993 and became a professional pipemaker in 1998.

streamliner-2.tn: "Air Cooled" on the shank along with the patent number "U.S. Des. Pat. 127324."
streamliner-2.not: The same logo also appears on the Fortnum's brand.

concorde.tn: Location stamp arranged in a circle on the right face, with "France" at the center.
concorde.not: The circular "Made in St Claude France" stamp follows the same layout as Comoy's "Made in London England" stamp.

rows: Chapuis Comoy, Made in St Claude

steel-s.tn: "Steel's" stamp, the brand name rendered in its own distinctive letterforms.
steel-s.not: The example pipe is a "carburetor" type, fitted with an adjustment valve beneath the bowl; a similar mechanism is seen on the Dunhill Airstream, Kaywoodie Carburetor, Passat, and Yello-Bole pipes. The brand was produced by Civic and La Bruyère; records indicate La Bruyère absorbed Chapuis-Comoy in 1932.

bari.tn: A script logo formed from the letters of the brand name.

rows: Bari, Special, Handcut, Made in Denmark, 847

rondelle.tn: The letters CP inlaid within a transparent disc (rondelle).
rondelle.not: Inlaying a logo within a transparent disc is a technique common to Butz Choquin's production; records suggest this pipe may be one of the examples made by the French factory between 1988 and 2002.

rows: Made by Hand in City of London

morel.tn: The name "Morel" written in a signature style on the shank.
morel.not: On pipes signed by Pierre Morel (son), a plain "e" was used before 1980, and the character ε afterward; Benzon was Morel's Italian distributor up to 1980. The signature-style "Morel" stamp, on the other hand, marks pipes made by Pierre Morel (father) in the 1970s for the Bremen wholesaler Tiedemann.

rows: Morel, Fait main, St Claude, France
P Morel JR, Fait Main, France, Benzon - Italy
Morel [Signature], Hand Made, St Claude, France

p-g-c-hajenius.tn: A single blue dot on the stem and the brand name "P.G.C. Hajenius" on the stamp.
p-g-c-hajenius.not: This is the Amsterdam tobacconist's own brand. The shop is located at Rokin 92-96, with a tobacco museum and library at the rear.

student-prince.tn: A single plain round dot on the stem.

madame.not: The "St Claude France" stamp on the pipe is identical to the stamp seen on pipes marked "Sans tare."

captain-browne.tn: A two-letter stamp; the name "Captain Browne" is written on the shank.

mlc.tn: The letters "MLC" enclosed in an oval frame.
mlc.not: The letters MLC are an abbreviation of the name Mary Linkman & Co. The oval MLC stamp indicates early production at the company's Chicago factory, prior to the Dr Grabow brand. Mary Linkman was the mother of the company's founder, Louis B. Linkman.

rows: MLC [within an oval] Aragon Italian Briar

mc-intosch.not: On some Mc Intosch pipes the stamp "ENGLAND" appears; this indicates the marketing intent rather than the actual country of manufacture.

sasieni-waverley.tn: A text stamp reading "Waverley, Sasieni Made" on the left face.
sasieni-waverley.not: This example pipe has undergone repair; a later-added silver band covers part of the stamp. Not to be confused with the "Waverly" brand.

luigi-pipas.tn: A single plain round dot on the stem.
luigi-pipas.not: The maker of these pipes is Luis Arbotto; the workshop is in Argentina.

maremma.tn: A single-dot stamp; on the underside, the text 'Maremma' and 'Vera Radica.'

jockey.tn: A mammal figure on the stem; a country-of-origin mark set inside a circle on the right face.

perma.tn: Plain round dot motif and "Perma-Dot" lettering.
perma.not: A brand of the Perma Products company.

kabik.tn: No stamp data is on record apart from the brand name "Kabik".

lark.tn: "Lark" and "Dr Grabow" on the left side, "Imported Briar" on the right side.
lark.not: The Lark series was introduced in 1969.

hhb.tn: A logo of a single letter; the shank bears the text "HHB".

hartmann-2.tn: A stamp featuring an eagle figure; the text "Ludwig Hartmann & Eidam Wien" inside a box.
hartmann-2.not: Ludwig Hartmann was founded in Vienna in 1829. Its meerschaum pipes were among the notable products of the period and won a first-class medal at the 1867 Paris World's Fair. "Eidam" in the stamp is an archaic German word meaning son-in-law.

sportsman-3.tn: Logo depicting a mammal; the underside of the shank carries text identifying the type of briar.
sportsman-3.not: A brand of the Tanganyika Meerschaum Corporation, part of Amboseli Pipes. See also Countryman, GBD, Kiko, Kikob, Kilimanjaro, Kudu, Twiga, Merlin.

kaywoodie-500-and-600-series.tn: Word stamp with the name "Kaywoodie" alongside the series number "500" or "600" on the shank.
kaywoodie-500-and-600-series.not: Records indicate this stamp was used between 1959 and 1967. The 500 and 600 series are considered the brand's entry-level line.

honey-swete.tn: A building-shaped emblem together with the text "Honey-Swete".
honey-swete.not: The same logo also appears on the La Ruche brand. Records indicate the same or a very similar logo was used on Savinelli's Melita line.

bromma.tn: An elephant standing on a pipe with the word "DOLLAR" above it.
bromma.not: The brand of Scandinaviska Pipfabriken. Records indicate the Harlekin and Dollar brands came from the same workshop.

rows: [the word "DOLLAR" above the elephant on the pipe]

bristol.not: Records suggest it may be a second-grade brand of Comoy's.

royal-windsor.not: For related brands from the same maker, see Royal Crown, Royal Bruyere, and Oxford.

rows: Sandhewn RGD. Made in London England, 2

avondale.tn: The left face bears the stamp "Parker, Avondale."

sren.tn: The name "Søren" and a "Hand carved" stamp on the underside.
sren.not: The maker of the brand is Søren Refbjerg Rasmussen. Pipes sent to the European market generally carry the "Refbjerg" stamp, while those sent to the US market carry the "Soren" stamp.

bbk.tn: A multi-letter stamp bearing the wording 'Bru-Bu' on the shank.
bbk.not: The name BBK is an abbreviation of Brunner-Buhofer-Kompagnie; the firm operated from 1932 to the late 1970s and was known for short as Bru-Bu. Its workshop in Kleinlützel, canton Solothurn, passed to Nielsen's 'Former' in 1986. Related record: Drexler's Tabakstube.

trapwell.tn: "Trapwell" and a patent number on the left side, "World's Best Briar" on the right side.
trapwell.not: Trapwell pipes stamped "World's Best Briar" are not made from briar but from Kalmia latifolia (mountain laurel) wood of the Ericaceae family; this plant is poisonous. At least three brands are known to have used the same wood: Trapwell, Breezewood, and Custombilt.

jack-o-london.tn: The text "JACK O' LONDON" on the shank together with the name "Hardcastle's".
jack-o-london.not: This pipe was made at Hardcastle's Walthamstow factory before the firm passed to Dunhill in 1967.

rows: Hardcastle's, British Made, JACK O' LONDON, 2

courbet.not: The brass logo is reserved for the higher-grade lines. The stamps on the right face are specific to the tobacconist selling the pipe.

rows: A la Pipe du Nord, 24 Bd Magenta

claude-romain.tn: A two-letter logo together with a clover motif.
claude-romain.not: The brand of the Berrod-Regad group, based in Saint-Claude; production was aimed mainly at the German market.

kaywoodie-white-briar.tn: A series-name stamp appearing on the left face alongside the main brand name.
kaywoodie-white-briar.not: The White Briar line was produced between 1951 and 1989, with bowls finished in a hard white surface. Since the Streamliner shape made in this finish appears in a 1953 calendar, it was already in production that year. The screw thread differs from the one used in the standard Synchro Stem patent.

crugnola.tn: "By Luigi Crugnola" lettering on the underside.
crugnola.not: Luigi Crugnola is the owner of the GIGI brand.

venini.tn: The stamp of the Venini brand; no detailed record data available.

canberra.tn: A single letter in a circle.

richard.tn: No logo on the stem; "TRP", "Pipes", and "AB" on the underside.

lumberman.tn: A letter stamp within a circle; the text 'Jeantet Lumberman' on the shank.

gold-star.tn: A star-shaped logo containing the letters G and S.
gold-star.not: Pipes gathered under the Gold Star name do not come from a single manufacturer. A multi-function pipe tool bearing the R & H stamp under the same name is also recorded.

rows: R & H, Gold Star, London Made, Made in England, 3767

royale.tn: "ROYALE" lettering in a shield, with the letters R and C beside it.
royale.not: Records link the brand to the Marechal Ruchon & Co factory, reflecting an English-French manufacturing relationship.

tabacum.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle; a "Tabacum" stamp on the underside.
tabacum.not: Tabacum is the brand of a tobacconist's shop in Stuttgart. As of 2009 records, the shop's owner was Siegfried Schäuble.

st-james.tn: Logo combining architectural, crown, and heraldic elements with ring motifs filled by a bar; the shank carries the text "St James."
st-james.not: One of Comoy's second-line brands; the other brands sharing the single-bar logo are Carlyle, Charles Cross, The Golden Arrow, Town Hall, and Trident. Brands with a similar logo include Tower, Castleford, and Moorgate. Records indicate St James has the greatest variety of stamps and logos among Comoy's second-line brands.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England, 49
◊ Made in London (within a circle), England, 33 4M ◊

grandmaster.tn: A two-line stamp reading "GRANDMASTER" above and "Made Malta" below.
grandmaster.not: The same logo is also used by the Boschetto brand and is associated with the Big Bill brand.

nana-ivarsson-design.tn: On the underside, the text "An Ivarsson Product" set within a circle.
nana-ivarsson-design.not: Sixten, Lars, and Nana of the Ivarsson family frequently contributed to the design of Stanwell models.

earl-of-essex.tn: Crown-motif logo; "Earl of Essex" lettering on the left side.

savinelli-samanda.tn: The stamp carries the text "Samanda" and the Savinelli crest.
savinelli-samanda.not: The same model code 506 also appears in Savinelli's De Luxe line.

century-old.tn: A logo of several bars (lines) on the stem.
century-old.not: The phrase "Century Old" is usually seen alongside various Lorenzo brand labels (see Jet Pipe, Lloyds, T.V) and, per records, was used for export models. In this example, though, the phrase does not appear with another label.

gucci.tn: A crest-shaped logo on the stem, made up of a green-red-green stripe.
gucci.not: The green-red-green stripe is the signature mark of the Italian luxury brand Gucci. For other luxury-brand pipes, see Hermes, Pierre Cardin, Vuitton.

savinelli-sigla.tn: The stamp carries the words "Savinelli" and "Sigla."

scotsman-s-delight.tn: Brand mark consisting of multiple letters.

casteldoria.tn: A mark featuring an architectural motif.
casteldoria.not: A sub-brand of Tom Spanu's pipes. The name comes from a small village near Spanu's workshop in Laerru (Sardinia); see Clairmont and Castelsardo for the same naming pattern.

english-variables.tn: Single-letter logo; "English Variables" stamp on the left side.

montini.not: The brand name comes from the surname of Alberto Montini, owner of Mastro de Paja.

the-thames.tn: "The Thames, London England" alongside a single-letter motif.

paul-guilland.tn: A text stamp with no separate emblem, consisting of the maker's name and the phrase "Maitre-pipier".
paul-guilland.not: Paul Guilland previously managed Merton. The workshop is in Saint-Claude, France. See also Aurelia.

royal-crown.tn: Stamp in the shape of a crown.

rows: Royal Crown Windsor, Made in England, GIANT

captain-patty.tn: A two-letter stamp; the name "Captain Patty" and the word "Lunel" appear on the shank.
captain-patty.not: Records indicate this is the export brand of Jean Waille (Le Pipier de Lunel), working in Lunel.

rows: Captain Patty, Erika, Made in France, 303

savinelli-virginia.tn: The scripted word "Savinelli" alongside the "Virginia" stamp and the Savinelli shield crest.

zeman.tn: No emblem on the stem; the name "Jan Zeman" on the underside.
zeman.not: The maker of these pipes is Czech-born Jan Zeman.

comoy-s-royal-guard.tn: A two-letter logo stamped on the top face of the stem; on some examples the letters A and U are stamped upside down.
comoy-s-royal-guard.not: Records indicate pipes bearing this stamp were made in Denmark, at the Stanwell workshops in Borup.

rows: [letters A and U stamped upside down — stamping error]

lindbergh.tn: A logo consisting of the word "Lindbergh" in an oval.
lindbergh.not: These pipes have leather-covered bodies. Lindbergh pipes were made in France; the maker or makers are unknown.

rows: Lindbergh (within an oval), Made in France

royal-bruyere.tn: Stamp in the shape of a crown.

l-l-bean.tn: The words "L. L. Bean" within a diamond-shaped frame.
l-l-bean.not: The company was founded in 1912 by Leon Leonwood Bean; it makes and sells outdoor gear. Records indicate the pipes were made by Briarcraft.

rows: L. L. Bean, Freeport ME, Imported Briar

michael-parks.tn: An ornate round inlay on the stem.
michael-parks.not: Grading runs, smallest to largest, from I to VI. The Roman numeral grade is followed by a number giving the year of manufacture; the digit 7 means 2007. A second Roman numeral, serving as a serial number, may also appear on the pipes.

lund.tn: A two-letter stamp; the text 'Lund Outrup, Handarbejde' on the shank.
lund.not: The pipes were made by Sven Aa. Lund, who records indicate has since retired. The workshop is located in the Danish town of Outrup.

yukon.tn: The letters "KBB" set within a clover, the word "Yukon", and a pick-and-shovel motif.

rows: KBB (within a clover), Yukon, Genuine Briar [Pickaxe and shovel]

english-made.tn: Native American chief's head figure on the stem.
english-made.not: This figure is used regularly on the stems of the Blackfriar line; records indicate it is a design specific to the brand.

rows: Ben Wade, Blackfriar, Made in, London England

butz-choquin.tn: A solid ring motif on the stem.

cardin.tn: No logo or stamp details are on record for this brand.

lancaster.tn: An ornamented round inlay; the stamp reads "Lancaster".

spp.tn: Stamp consisting of a star motif.

stending.tn: "Stending" on the shank and a "++" mark.

rows: The Crown, Regp, Made in England, Hardcastel's

tao.tn: A grade letter within a circle beside the brand name.
