tao.not: Grading rises from the letter D to the letter S.

rows: Danish Handmade TAO B (within a circle)

silvano.tn: The stamp carries the text "Silvano" and the word "Set."

genod.tn: Single-letter logo; the left side reads "Genod".
genod.not: The brand was founded in 1970 by Jacques Craen; production is based at the Vincent Genod factory in Saint-Claude. The stem does not always carry a logo. See also Paul Viou.

maillefer.not: Records indicate the brand belongs to the Tabacs Maillefer tobacconist, located at Grand-Chêne 5 in Lausanne.

seafoam.tn: Brand mark consisting of a single letter.

inderwick.tn: A single blue dot in a diamond shape on the stem.
inderwick.not: Inderwick & Co was founded by John Inderwick in the early 19th century. The firm's premises were at 58 Princes Street, near Leicester Square in London.

savinelli-bruna.tn: A shield-shaped crest stamp with a model number beside it.
savinelli-bruna.not: Savinelli's crest form varies by period; this variation is the basis used to date the stamp.

dandylite.tn: Single blue dot on the stem.

airo.tn: A diamond-shaped yellow mark on the stem.
airo.not: The same yellow mark also appears on the Cavalcade brand.

rows: B [within a diamond], AIRO, Genuine Briar

richichi.tn: Round wood inlay on the stem.

middleton.tn: A family of stamps made up of a single letter, an anchor, a crown, and coat-of-arms elements; a single blue dot appears on the stem mark.
middleton.not: John Middleton Co., founded in 1856, earned its main reputation with tobaccos such as Prince Albert. The company moved to King of Prussia, Pennsylvania in 1960 and became a subsidiary of Altria Group in 2007. Records indicate some Middleton pipes came from the same French factory as Royal Ascot examples, which carry the same logo.

scott.tn: Brand mark consisting of a letter topped by a crown.
scott.not: The same logo also appears on the Knute of Denmark and Kingsway brands.

herter-s.tn: A logo consisting of the brand name in script.
herter-s.not: Herter's is the house brand of the outdoor-supply stores of the same name, which sold to hunters, anglers, and forest workers. The brand's pipes were made in a single shape only.

kyringe.tn: "Kyringe, Flame Grain" on the left side, "Bruyère" on the right side.
kyringe.not: During the years of the Second World War the Kyringe company was run by Poul Nielsen; the firm made pipes from briar and beech wood. Nielsen founded the Stanwell brand a few years after the war.

eltang.tn: Stamp featuring a snail figure and an oval containing a pipe depiction.
eltang.not: The current stamp reads "Tom Eltang, Denmark" arranged in a circle on the underside. The letter M enclosed in a circle is stamped only on pipes considered exceptional; records indicate at most two such pipes are made per year. The two digits beside the snail figure give the year of manufacture; the 10 here corresponds to 2010.

xtra.tn: A logo consisting of the letters "GBD" set within an oval, alongside the word "Xtra."
xtra.not: Records indicate pipes carrying this stamp date to the 1930s.

kevin-arthur.tn: The text "Kevin Arthur" arranged in a circle on the underside.
kevin-arthur.not: The pipes are made by Kevin Arthur, born in 1958, a self-taught maker. He began selling his pipes in 2007 and became known after attending the 2009 Chicago Pipe Show.

sasieni-king-s-court.tn: A stamp consisting of a letter enclosed in a circle.

rows: King's Court, London Made, By Sasieni

barbi-design.tn: The left face bears the stamp "brebbia, Barbi design."
barbi-design.not: The pipe was designed for Brebbia by Rainer Barbi.

sabatini.tn: The left face carries the text "Sabatini Oro."

pietenpauw-son.tn: No separate logo; "Pietenpauw" on the left side, "Pietenpaw" and "JP & Son" stamps on the underside.
pietenpauw-son.not: Records indicate the later-dated stamps reflect Pieter making Pietenpauw pipes together with his father.

sachs.tn: Brand name set within a rhombus-shaped stamp.
sachs.not: Georges Sachs ran a tobacconist's business in New York from the 1920s into the 1940s.

simon.tn: Logo depicting a mammal; the stamp carries the text "Simon Classic."

nielsen.tn: No stamp casting or logo data is on record.

novelli.not: This is the private label of the Regali Novelli shop in Rome, which sells pens and pipes. As of 2008 records, the shop's owner was Marco Parascenzo.

comoy-s-blue-riband.tn: The words 'Blue Riband' on the shank.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England, 126

hgh.tn: No separate logo stamp; the text "Høgh" on the left face.
hgh.not: The workshop or maker behind the brand is unknown.

paul-perri.tn: A single dot or three dots on the stem; in the three-dot arrangement, the middle dot is the same size as the others but a different color.
paul-perri.not: The pipes were made by Paul Perri, who retired to Hawaii in 1997. He was Trever Talbert's first mentor.

sasieni-fantail.tn: Single-letter logo; stamps carry the words "Sasieni" and "Fantail".

rows: Sasieni, Fantail, London Made, PAT D-170067
Sasieni, Fantail, London Made, PAT D 170067 (1953)

barnaby.tn: A pipe depiction within a diamond.
barnaby.not: Found on pipes whose stem is also made of briar; other brands with the same feature include Il Ceppo, Kaywoodie Allbriar, LHS, and Salvatella. The brand belongs to Barnaby Briars, a pipe retailer at 28 Powell Street, Brooklyn; the same retailer's other brand is Yorkshire.

soler.tn: No separate logo stamp; "J. P. SOLER" set between lines on the left side.
soler.not: Maker Joan Pere Soler i Molina comes from a Catalan pipe-making family going back to 1890 and has made pipes since 1953. The workshop is in Amer, in the province of Girona.

joe-cortegiano.tn: An ornamented round mark on the stem; the shank bears the stamp "J. Cortegiano, Hand Made".
joe-cortegiano.not: Maker Joseph (Joe) Cortegiano worked in New York; he is deceased. His very large pipes were also sold through retailers such as Wilke and Barclay Rex.

mauro-cateni.tn: A shield (coat-of-arms) motif and, on the left side, the text "Mauro Cateni."
mauro-cateni.not: Records indicate the name does not belong to a real person but was used as a second brand by an unidentified maker. Known series names include Brulio, Classica, Gialla, and Nuova Rossa.

majestic.tn: A crown logo with a letter beside the crown.
majestic.not: Ben Wade also has a sub-brand and model line called Majestic; these should not be confused with Stanwell's Majestic. On some examples the stamps are crossed out with hatching for unknown reasons.

brunton.tn: No logo on the stem; the stamps are on the underside of the shank.
brunton.not: Christopher Brunton began selling his pipes in 2008 while still living in Austria, moving back to the US (Carmichael, California) later that year to take up pipemaking full-time. The stamp consists of the letter "C" and a two-digit number giving the year of manufacture; records indicate a signature was added from around 2010 onward.

smokecraft.tn: A single-letter logo; an oval "Smokecraft" stamp on the shank.

pierluigi.tn: Triangular logo; the stamp reads "Pierluigi" and "Fatta a Mano".
pierluigi.not: The pipes are made by Aldo and Andrea Pierluigi. See also Mastro Beraldi.

rows: Pierluigi, Fatta a Mano, Per i miei Amici, B
Pierluigi, Fatta a mano, Per i miei amici

the-everyman.tn: A brand stamp bearing the name "The Everyman."

omega.tn: A fleur-de-lis motif together with the word "Omega".
omega.not: Pipes bearing this brand are said to come from the same production source as Bayard, Chadhall, Thomas, and Duke of Kent pipes. Other brands with the fleur-de-lis motif include Ajustomatic, Cellini, Fleur de lis, Harrington Park, and Vincenzo Lombardi.

rows: Omega Crown, Algerian Briar, Made in France

savinelli-oscar.tn: A star-motif logo; the top side reads "Oscar Aged Briar".
savinelli-oscar.not: Pipes in the Oscar line may have fills. The same star logo also appears in the Savinelli Antique Shell, Savinelli Garda, and Savinelli Sila entries.

john-surrey.tn: A two- or three-dot mark on the stem; the words "John Surrey Ltd" on the shank.
john-surrey.not: John Surrey, Ltd. was located at 509 Fifth Avenue in New York. Records indicate examples stamped "Super de Luxe" date to around 1945-1950.

rows: John Surrey Ltd. Imported Briar, Super de Luxe

elie.tn: Single-letter logo; "Handmade by Elie, Belgium" lettering in the stamp.

jesper-of-denmark.not: The stamps are in cursive script. The pipes' design is by Jørgen Larsen.

winston.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter set within a circle; the stamp "Winston Custom Deluxe" on the body.

colossals.tn: A multi-letter logo of letters enclosed in circles together with a star motif.
colossals.not: The pipes were made in France and Italy by unidentified manufacturers.

rows: Colossals, Bark Grain, imported Briar, Italy
Colossals, Custom made, Algerian Briar, France

aldo-velani.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem; some examples also show a double dot along with a wooden or ornamented round inlay.
aldo-velani.not: Aldo Velani is a fictitious name for a sub-brand used mainly for export. The brand name is stamped in block letters; the Ultima D 54 model is a Barontini design.

astor.tn: The brand name set within an oval, seen together with a letter and triangle motif within a circle.

rows: Astor (within an oval), Made in London (within a circle), England, 497

forecaster.tn: A stamp using a letter enclosed in a circle, a diamond, and star elements, with a shield depiction on the top side.
forecaster.not: The brand belongs to National Briar Pipe Co, based in Jersey City, New Jersey. The same company's other brands are The Biltmore, Honey Brook, Rembrandt, and, after 1960, The Doodler.

downie.tn: No separate logo; small lowercase "downie" lettering on the lower right side.

kriswill.tn: A star mark on the stem, with the brand name "Kriswill" on the shank.
kriswill.not: Before 1970, stamps on the shank and stem were struck in script lettering; after that date, a star was used on the stem and block letters on the shank. Tiedemann is a German dealer that imported Kriswill pipes. The name of the Bernadotte series refers to Sigvard Bernadotte.

berrod-regad.not: Berrod-Regad, based in Saint-Claude, is a group encompassing brands such as Butz Choquin, Chap, Claude Romain, Bontemps, and Jima. In 1999 annual production reached 230,000 pipes. See also Jacky Berrod.

luxor.tn: The text 'Luxor' within a triangular-cornered cartouche.
luxor.not: The same logo is also seen on the Lord brand. The example bearing the cartouche stamp was made with an 18-karat gold band and a horn stem; records indicate no connection between the workshop that produced this pipe and the other workshop using the same brand name.

carlyle.tn: A single bar-shaped inlaid mark on the stem.
carlyle.not: One of Comoy's second-grade brands. For other brands carrying the same single-bar stem mark, see Charles Cross, St James, The Golden Arrow, Town Hall, and Trident.

berkshire.tn: A two-dot logo on the stem.
berkshire.not: Records indicate it is one of the brands of the Reiss-Premier Co.

royal-captain.not: Wilczak and Colwell list the brand as a second line or series of Savinelli; the "Made in Belgium" stamp on this pipe does not match that information.

k-anastasopoulos.tn: The letters "K.A." enclosed in a rectangle.
k-anastasopoulos.not: Dating is based on a four- or five-digit number: the last two digits give the year of manufacture, and the leading two or three digits give the pipe's sequence number. For example, 8013 denotes the 80th pipe carved in 2013.

jean-dejay.tn: A triangle motif with the text "Jean Dejay".

finsbury.tn: A stamp on the left side reading the brand name "Finsbury".
finsbury.not: According to records based on the study by Wilczak and Colwell, the brand may belong either to Finsbury Products, based in Harrison, New York, or to Oppenheimer Pipes Ltd.

dollar.tn: An elephant figure standing on a pipe.
dollar.not: Dollar is one of Skandinaviska Pipfabriken's brands. Bo Nordh's first pipe was a Dollar. Records indicate the Harlekin and Bromma brands also came from the same workshop.

t-v.tn: The two-letter mark "TV" on the stem, "T.V. Pipe" on the shank.
t-v.not: The "TV" mark on the stem is yellow on some examples and white on others.

hamilton.tn: The letters KBB set inside a clover leaf, with a curved "Hamilton" script, in the stamp.
hamilton.not: For a blue version of the same logo, see Dorset.

rows: KBB (within a clover), Hamilton (curved), Italian Bruyére

l-s.tn: A two-letter "L.S" stamp with a place name beside it.
l-s.not: The initials L.S do not match the names of the two known pipe makers in the village of Cogolin (L. Roux and Courrieu); who the brand belongs to remains uncertain.

wilkinson.tn: A logo consisting of a single blue dot; the stamp "Wilkinson Imported Briar" on the body.
wilkinson.not: According to J. M. Lopes's records, the brand belongs to the Bradberry Pipe Corp. in New York.

waille.tn: A text stamp reading "Waille, Jura" on the left face and "Bruyere, St Claude" on the right face.
waille.not: The workshop was founded in Saint-Claude in 1860 by Horace Waille; his son René continued the business from 1902 to 1932. Horace's grandson André Waille took over from 1932 to 1974, and André's son Michel Waille, who joined the firm in 1968, changed its name to SARL PIPE EWA in 1979.

ermuzi.not: Ermüzi is the house brand of Ernst Mühlensiepen GmbH & Co., a firm dealing in tobacco, cigars, and wine.

perspex-stem.tn: A Barling cross logo and the registration number "REG D 98046" on the stem; "BARLING'S" in an arched stamp on the shank.
perspex-stem.not: The stem is made from Perspex, a semi-transparent acrylic patented in Canada in 1934. This material can be cleaned with alcohol.

rows: BARLING'S (arch-shaped) MAKE, Ye Olde Wood, EXEXEL Fossil, Made in England, T.V.F.

sunrise.tn: A triangular logo; a letter within a circle is also used.
sunrise.not: One example is a churchwarden model made at the Chapuis Comoy workshops in Saint-Claude. Sunrise is an example of the brands whose production was split between Saint-Claude and London before the early 1970s, when Chapuis Comoy and Comoy worked in close partnership.

ichi-kitahara.tn: No separate logo stamp; the underside bears the maker's name, year of production, and country abbreviation.
ichi-kitahara.not: A handmade brand. Ichi Kitahara began pipe making in 2004 under the guidance of H. Tokutomi, then returned to part-time production in 2012 after several years' break.

benner.tn: A round inlaid dot mark on the stem.
benner.not: Pipes bearing the maker's full name -Bent Nielsen- predate those using the 'Benner' pseudonym. On early pipes the grading rises from 1 to 5. Before setting up his own workshop, Bent Nielsen worked in Karl Erik's workshop.

rows: Bent Nielsen, Hand Made in Denmark, 1, Benner

nils-thomsen.not: This Berlin-origin pipe belongs to the "Berliner Kollegiumspfeife" series, which began in 2003.

sasieni-his-royal-highness.tn: The letters HRH and a feather figure taken from the Prince of Wales's crest.
sasieni-his-royal-highness.not: The logo consists of the letters HRH together with the feather figure from the Prince of Wales's coat of arms. Some H.R.H. pipes lack a "Sasieni Made" stamp.

rows: [rugby-ball shaped] 367, His Royal Highness, Sasieni Made

selected.tn: Brand mark in the shape of a rhombus.

rows: Big-Ben Maestro Mondial 418 Made in Holland

cavalcade.tn: A yellow diamond-shaped (rhombus) inlaid mark on the stem containing the letter B.
cavalcade.not: For similar marks see Smokemaster, Sterling Hall, L.L. Bean, and Hallmark.

calvert.tn: A single dot on each face of the stem.
calvert.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's compilation, the brand was distributed by Harry J. Gorfinkel.

polinski.tn: Brand stamp made up of a single letter.
polinski.not: The brand's maker is Tadeusz Polinski; his workshop is in Przemyśl, Poland.

guyot.tn: The name "H. Guyot" and a Paris address in the stamp.
guyot.not: Gilbert Guyot continued to mark the pipes he made with the "H. Guyot" stamp, a reference to his father.

akermann.tn: A pipe-shaped mark on the stem.

bonfiglioli.tn: A stamp formed from a triangular motif.
bonfiglioli.not: The brand of the Italian master Alberto Bonfiglioli.

barclay.tn: A single-letter logo; the underside bears the handwritten-script stamp 'Barclay' within quotation marks.
barclay.not: Records cite three English makers as possible origins of the brand: Bond Engineering, Comoy, and Sasieni. The rustic surface finish, the handwritten-script brand stamp in quotation marks, and the two-line block-letter country-of-origin marking are characteristic of Sasieni's pre-transition period; the brand is accordingly considered a Sasieni sub-brand.

rows: "Barclay" London Made, Made in England, 762 GR

silver-match.tn: Letter logo consisting of two letters.
silver-match.not: These are pipes distributed by the well-known lighter brand of the same name; records indicate this logo was used on pipes sold in France. Other lighter brands that also distributed pipes include Flamidor, Myon, Ronson, and S.T. Dupont.

rows: Logo for pipes sold in France (?)

drexler-s.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle.
drexler-s.not: The private label of a tobacconist in Nuremberg, whose shop address is given as Kaiserstraße 32, 90403 Nürnberg. Records indicate that, based on the "Swiss + Made" stamp, the pipe is linked to the Swiss manufacturer BBK.

arabesque.tn: Logo in the form of a mammal figure.
arabesque.not: Made in Saint-Claude, France, by an unidentified manufacturer. The same logo and the same rustic surface finish also appear on the Wenko brand.

derby-3.tn: "Derby" lettering placed over a horseshoe figure.
derby-3.not: The Derby name is also recorded as a product line of Oldenkott.

peterson-millenium-1988.tn: A Dublin hallmark series on the silver stamp featuring the Hibernia figure, the standard fineness mark, and the date letter 'c.'
peterson-millenium-1988.not: Peterson's Millenium pipe was made to mark the one-thousandth anniversary of the founding of the city of Dublin (988-1988). The hallmarks belong to the Dublin Assay Office.

kaywoodie-the-drinkless-peer.tn: A multi-letter stamp on the left side reading "The Drinkless" and "Peer."

tom-dorion.tn: A letter-shaped logo set within a circle; the stamp reads "Tom Dorion."

golden-danish.tn: A three-line "Golden Danish" stamp struck between lines on the underside.

heeschen.tn: Letter "P." enclosed in an oval, alongside "hand-carved, in denmark" in an arched arrangement.
heeschen.not: Records indicate the workshop produces about 30 pipes a month. Grades rise in the order B, A, and S; some pipes carry no visible grade stamp.

chapuis-comoy.not: The brand of the Chapuis-Comoy factory in France, a product of the Anglo-French pipe connection. Its second-line brands are Honey-Swete, La Ruche, Royal Coachman, and Sunrise.

old-england-2.tn: A single-letter logo enclosed in a crest.

rows: 938XS, Old England, London Made, Made in England (Curved)
Old England, London Made, 60, Made in England (Curved)

special-quality.tn: "Special Quality" on the top surface with "By Hardcastle" below it.

perkins.tn: Letters "H.P.S" inside an oval on the shank; the stamps include a clover motif and the brand name.
perkins.not: The nine-carat gold hallmarks on the ferrule belong to the Birmingham Assay Office and, per records, indicate the year 1920. See also the "Crown of England" entry for the brand.

carey.tn: A stamp made up of a letter enclosed in a circle together with parallel bars; the name "Carey" and the term "Magic Inch" appear on the shank.

porsche-design.tn: A plain stamp formed from the letters "pd", with "Porsche Design" beside it.
porsche-design.not: These stamps date from the earlier period when the pipes were made by Oldenkott.

rodriguez.not: Maker: Tony Rodriguez. He began making pipes in the early 2000s, working under the guidance of Rick Newcombe, Jess Chonowitsch, and Lars Ivarsson. He stopped making pipes around 2007, when he moved with his family from Los Angeles to Portland, Oregon.

millville.tn: On the left side, the name 'Millville' and quality name; on the right side, a text stamp noting London manufacture.
millville.not: The brand's makers were the father-and-son team Dennis and John Marshall, both of whom had previously worked at the Charatan factory.

rows: Made by Hand, In, City of London

manx-meerschaum.tn: A meerschaum pipe; on the band, the text 'Millenium of Tynwald.'
manx-meerschaum.not: Tynwald is the legislature of the Isle of Man and is considered the oldest continuously functioning parliament; its thousandth anniversary was celebrated in 1979. The stamp is linked to the Laxey Pipe Factory, which closed in 2002; the same factory also produced the Manxpipe, Manxman, and Manxland brands. See also Man Pipes.

moretti.tn: A round wooden inlay on the stem; on the shank, a letter and two dots set beneath a crown.
moretti.not: A round wooden inlay is the usual logo on Moretti pipe stems. This particular pipe was made around 1995 for Carlo Lodi, president of the Pipa Club Italia.

thorburn-clark.tn: A two-letter logo; "Thorburn Clark" on the shank.
thorburn-clark.not: The tobacconist business also carved its own pipes. The shop in Manchester is recorded as having closed in the 1970s.

duca-pipe.tn: Letter used together with a crown; "Il Duca" lettering on the shank.
duca-pipe.not: The pipes are made by master carver Massimiliano Rimensi, who works in Occhiobello (Rovigo), Italy. Grades run from lowest to highest: Nobile (rustic), Barone (sandblasted), Cavaliere (smooth), Conte, and Duca. Within each grade, the number of Ds in the stamp (one to three) indicates the pipe's value, with DDD marking the top rank.

l-roux.tn: A two-letter L-R stamp and the brand-name text.
l-roux.not: The brand was founded in Cogolin by Louis Roux; Courrieu also worked in the same village. Roux handed the brand over to Santo d'Amico in 1956; d'Amico stopped carving pipes in the early 1980s but, as of 2009, was still continuing sales.

rows: Sandblasted Briar, L. Roux, Bruyere des Maures, 114

hedegaard.tn: No separate logo; the underside bears "Peter Hedegaard" in an arched arrangement.

kaywoodie-rustica.tn: "Kaywoodie Rustica" on the lower left side.
kaywoodie-rustica.not: Records indicate this stamp was used between 1965 and 1967.

sergio.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; the underside carries the "Sergio" stamp.

statesman.tn: Stamp made of bar motifs arranged side by side.

stanwell.tn: No stamp rubbing is on record.

kiko.tn: A stamp depicting a mammal figure.

abercrombie-fitch.tn: Multi-letter word stamp; the line "Abercrombie & Fitch C°, New York" on the left side.
abercrombie-fitch.not: A private-label brand made for the retailer. Abercrombie & Fitch Co operated around 300 stores in the US as of 2008, with a comparable number outside the country.

masterly.tn: A crown motif and the text "Masterly."
masterly.not: The same crown logo is also seen on the Dun-King brand.

poul-hansen.tn: Logo-free stamp; "Poul Hansen, Copenhagen" on the left side.
poul-hansen.not: Poul Hansen trained under Sixten Ivarsson in the 1960s and 1970s; he first made tools and machinery for Danish pipe makers, then began making his own pipes. He sold the Danish Pipe Shop he founded in Copenhagen to Steffen Nielsen in 1969 and retired in 1998. See also Hansen Briar.

rocky-briar.tn: Letters KBB set inside a clover leaf, with a target-shaped motif.
rocky-briar.not: The brand belongs to the firm Kaufman Brothers & Bondy.

rows: KBB [within a clover] Rocky Briar, REG US PAT No 298978, 1517

mansfield.tn: A single-letter logo; on the left side, the text 'Mansfield' and 'Made in England.'

james-upshall.tn: The text "James Upshall" on the shank with a lettered grade stamp beside it.
james-upshall.not: Maker Barry Jones trained at Charatan from the age of fifteen. He founded the brand with Kenneth Barnes in 1978 at Tilshead in Wiltshire. According to 2006 figures, weekly output is about 30 pipes.

rows: James Upshall Hand Made in England, FH [Red]

leonardo-da-vinci.tn: A logo of three ship's sails and the letters of the brand name.

rows: LEONARDO DA VINCI, HAND MADE, ITALY,

birks.tn: The word 'Birks' written on the shank in two lines.
birks.not: According to Wilczak and Colwell's records, the name likely belongs to an English tobacco shop.

tobacco-pouch.tn: A kangaroo-figure logo on the stem side; the words "Tobacco Pouch" in the stamp.
tobacco-pouch.not: The same logo also appears on the Samirva brand.

kaywoodie-chesterfield.tn: "Chesterfield" on the right face, "Solid Rubber" lettering below the stem; the left face carries no stamp.
kaywoodie-chesterfield.not: The left face carries no stamp. The stamp was used during the period 1924-1971. Chesterfield is a system pipe with a stem design resembling Peterson's P-Lip mechanism.

thomas-james.tn: No logo; the letters "T J" appear on the underside.

rinaldo.tn: Single-letter inlay on the stem; "RINALDO" on the shank.

rows: Hand Made in Italy, Lithos Silver line, YY

tabak-rohr.tn: A chevron (arrowhead-shaped) motif on the stem.

iceberg.tn: No separate logo stamp; the shank bears the text "Brebbia Iceberg" along with a country mark and model number.

bellevue.tn: A two-letter stamp; the shank reads 'Bellevue' and 'Butz-Choquin.'

thomas.tn: A fleur-de-lis motif with a single-letter stamp.
thomas.not: The same fleur-de-lis logo points to a shared origin with the Bayard, Chadhall, Omega, and Duke of Kent pipes. Other brands using the fleur-de-lis motif include Ajustomatic, Cellini, Fleur de lis, Harrington Park, and Vincenzo Lombardi.

imperial.tn: A letter stamp giving the brand name as the word "Imperial".

rows: Imperial Treble, London made, Made in England 426
Imperial Sangrain, Made in England (within a circle)

prior.tn: Letter stamp in the form of the brand name on the stem.
prior.not: A brand of the firm Gros, Grenier, Ostorero & Cie; see also GOC, OSA, Sicana.

romeo.tn: The name "Romeo" written on the underside alongside a symbol.

nrding.tn: A single-letter logo used together with a crown motif.
nrding.not: Most of the meerschaum pipes distributed under the Nørding name were made by Manxman Pipes Ltd on the Isle of Man; these pipes carry no stamp on the shank, with the brand name struck on the band instead. As of 2002 data, annual output was around 50,000 pipes. See also Aalbørg, Son, Eriksen, Kriswill.

rows: Aristokrat, Extra, Handmade by Erik Nørding
Nørding, Made in Denmark (within a circle), 13

shelburne.tn: No logo on the stem; the underside carries the "Shelburne" stamp, a grade mark, and a place-of-manufacture inscription.
shelburne.not: Shelburne is one of the brands made by Karl Erik; other brands from the same maker include Ottendahl, Champ of Denmark, Golden Danish, Half Town, and Knute of Denmark. The stamps may be accompanied by the name of the Larsen & Stigart pipe shop in Copenhagen; the "II S" mark indicates the pipe was prepared for the US market.

jess-chonowitsch.tn: The text ".Chonowitsch. Denmark" inside a circle, with a bird emblem beside it.

fairmorn.tn: "Charles Fairmorn" lettering on the left side, place of manufacture on the right side.
fairmorn.not: A wholesaler's brand; depending on the period, the pipes were made by German, Danish, or Irish craftsmen. As of 2007, production was carried out by Dane Helmer Thomsen.

mpc.not: The abbreviation MPC comes from the name Milano Pipe Club.

rogrus.tn: Logo consisting of an ornamented round dot and two letters.

cole.tn: No logo; the name "Cole" appears on the underside.
cole.not: Master Charles Cole (b. 1965) took up pipemaking as an amateur in 2008. After a period working with Brad Pohlmann and Todd Johnson, he became a full-fledged pipemaker in 2010.

del-grano.tn: Motif made up of several parallel bars.
del-grano.not: The brand was founded by Alberto Del Grano.

adsorba.tn: A motif of target-like concentric rings.

esquire.tn: "Esquire" lettering accompanied by crown and ring motifs.
esquire.not: Records note that pipes sold under the same "Esquire" label may have come from different sources, and may even belong to separate brands.

peterson-irish-free-state.tn: A period stamp bearing "Peterson's, Dublin" on the left face and "Irish Free State" on the right face.
peterson-irish-free-state.not: Peterson's genuine sterling hallmark carries Hibernia and a harp figure as its first two shields. On this pipe, the band's first mark is a shamrock, indicating a non-silver metal, most likely nickel. Such imitation hallmarks cannot be used for dating.

humbry.tn: A logo of a single letter used together with a star motif.
humbry.not: The brand belongs to the Royal Dutch Pipe Factory. See also Amphora, Big Ben, Royal Dutch.

rows: Humbry, Briar, Made in Holland, 5422 R

heidemann.tn: A plain, single-color round dot on the stem.
heidemann.not: A handmade brand. Records indicate Heidemann lived in Wisconsin and produced only a small number of pipes per year.

ottendahl.tn: The brand name "Ottendahl" on the stamp, with a single letter or number next to it.

ken.tn: A cat figure on the underside with the text "Ken" beside it.

red-hat.not: Maker Kjeld Sørensen has made pipes full-time since 2003. Some pipes carry a "Kjeld" stamp beneath the hat logo. Roughly 100 pipes were produced in 2010.

getz-pipe.tn: No logo on the stem; the lower left side reads "getz".
getz-pipe.not: The pipes are made by Georgi Todorov (b. 1971), a full-time pipe maker since 1999.

sea-rock.tn: Round stone inlay on the stem.
sea-rock.not: The stone-inlay logo was originally used on pipes shipped to the US market, and was applied only occasionally in later periods.

rows: Castello, Sea Rock Briar, Made in Cantu (within an oval), Carlo Scotti, SS, 56

the-pearl.tn: A brand stamp bearing the name "The Pearl."

erikson.tn: Single-letter logo; "Erikson, London Made" stamp on the shank.

clifton.tn: A multi-letter logo formed from the letters of the brand name.

dr-maclean.not: One of the brands under Oppenheimer Pipes Ltd.

rows: Dr Maclean Cartridge Pipe, London Made

monaco.tn: A star-motif stamp bearing the name "Monaco" together with "De Luxe" and an Italian production notice.

rows: Monaco, De Luxe, Made in Italy

overland.tn: The brand name "Overland" on the left side, and a country mark enclosed in a circle on the right side.
overland.not: A country stamp enclosed in a circle on the right side of the shank is a distinguishing mark of Comoy production; records therefore attribute the brand to Comoy.

ducate.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the lettering "DUCATÉ".
ducate.not: No information is on record about this Belgian-origin brand.

h-b.tn: No logo; the underside bears brand, series, and place-of-manufacture stamps.
h-b.not: The abbreviation H & B denotes the firm Hirschl & Bendheim; "Irvin S. Cobb" is one of the firm's lines. Per the stamp, the firm was founded in 1871, with production in Washington, Missouri. Records indicate that on one example both the bowl and the shank are made of hickory.

sasieni-royal-prince.tn: Text-only stamp, no shape: "Royal Prince, Sasieni Made" on the top.

janpipes.tn: An ornamented round logo with the text "Janpipes" beside it.
janpipes.not: The brand's maker is Jan Klouček, who learned pipe making in Saint-Claude, France; the brand was founded in 1999. Grades follow cognac naming and are stamped, in rising order, VS, VO, XO, and VSOP.

champ-of-denmark.tn: Lettered "Champ of Denmark" text arranged over two lines.
champ-of-denmark.not: Some pipes bearing this label were distributed by Larsen & Stigart, a well-known tobacconist in Copenhagen; the shop has since closed. Makers such as Søren Eric Andersen worked at the firm's workshop for a period. Karl Erik Ottendahl was not the only maker who contributed to this label.

carlson.tn: A stamp formed from a B set inside a C, accompanied by the word "Sweden".
carlson.not: Records indicate all of the brand's pipes carry only the "BC Sweden" stamp, with no other marking.

sasieni-litewate.tn: A stamp bearing only the text 'Litewate' on the shank.
sasieni-litewate.not: A brand produced solely for the U.S. market.

angelo.not: The second brand of the Rovera family (Angelo and Damiano), who also produced Ardor, Roverart, and Rovera.

cadet.tn: An inverted-V chevron motif on the stem.
cadet.not: Cadet is one of Savinelli's series. In this example the brand marks have been removed: the "S" in the stem logo has been canceled, and the "Savinelli" stamp that should appear on the shank is absent.

kaywoodie-early-thorn.tn: Letters KBB set within a clover on the underside, along with "Thorn" lettering.
kaywoodie-early-thorn.not: On this early Thorn finish, the letters KBB are stamped within a clover on the shank. The Thorn finish was produced between 1928 and the late 1950s, while the KBB clover shank stamp was discontinued in 1933.

rows: KBB (within a clover) Drinkless Kaywoodie, Thorn, 7329

cyclone.tn: Curved "Cyclone" lettering on the left face with "De Luxe" below it.

sasieni-four-dot-bowler.tn: Four dots arranged in a diamond pattern; script "Sasieni" stamp on the underside.
sasieni-four-dot-bowler.not: A Four Dot stamp from the pre-transitional period (1946-1979). After the Second World War, Alfred Sasieni removed the fishtail flourish from the script signature; the signature here shows this new form.

gbd.tn: No logo description or stamp record on file.

lord-windsor.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle on the stem.

rows: Lord Windsor, Made in London, England

mastersen.tn: On the left side, the text "Mastersen" and the word "Freehand."
mastersen.not: Mastersen is one of the brands of Shalom Pipe Co., which was later acquired by Mastercraft. See also Alpha.

vincent.tn: An ornamented round dot on the stem; the brand's stamp uses a French flag motif.
vincent.not: The pipe was made by Pierre Vincent, a now-retired French maker. This pipe was produced for the bicentennial of the French Revolution (1789-1989). For another flag-motif stamp, see Ropp Nationale.

custom-bilt.tn: A dot on each side of the stem; a star beside the "Custom-Bilt" lettering on the shank.
custom-bilt.not: Some Custom-Bilt pipes carry a separate stamp near the stem, on the underside of the shank, in the shape of a square, circle, crescent, or star. For maker Tracy Mincer, see also Tracy Mincer, The Doodler, and Holeysmoke.

anzio.tn: Letter A enclosed in a circle.
anzio.not: The brand of Art-Craft Briar Pipe Co (1944). Records indicate some of the pipes were made for the US military.

rows: A [within a circle], Anzio, Genuine Briar

eriksen.tn: Single-letter logo used together with a crown.

john-bessai.tn: A two-letter mark on the stem.
john-bessai.not: Maker John Bessai (d. 1969) worked in Cleveland as a pipe maker, pipe repairer, and tobacco-shop owner.

peterson-k-briar.tn: "K" Briar text on the shank along with "A Peterson Product".

rows: "A Peterson Product" Made in the Republic of Ireland, 999
"K" Briar, "A Peterson product", Made in the republic of Ireland

altinok.tn: A single-letter logo within a circle, used on meerschaum pipes.
altinok.not: The pipes are made by master carver Sinan A. Altinok in Ankara. No stamp appears on the body.

ps-studio.tn: "PS Studio" between two dashes on the underside.

churchill.not: The stem logo is hat-shaped; other brands with a similar hat logo include Lobbia, London Royal, Man About Town, and Sabatini. According to Wilczak and Colwell's study, the brand may be one of Comoy's second-line brands.

lorenzetti.tn: The letter L in a triangle on the stem; on later models, a script letter L in a double oval.
lorenzetti.not: The brand was founded in 1934 by Otello Lorenzetti. As of 2009 the company is headed by Alessandro Lorenzetti. The workshop is in Recanati (Macerata), Italy.

rows: Lorenzetti, L [within a double oval], Bruyere Extra
Lord [crown] Byron, Bruyere Extra, by Lorenzetti, 115

corsellini.tn: Single dot on the stem and a grade letter enclosed within a circle.
corsellini.not: Grading letters run from lowest to highest: C, B, and A; the letter is given within a circle. See also the Brebbia Silver Star entry.

old-pal.tn: A logo made up of an eagle emblem with the words "Old Pal" arched above it.

rows: ◊ Old Pal (Curved) [Eagle emblem] Made in France ◊
Old Pal (curved above the eagle) Standard

peterson-meerschaum-1892.tn: On the silver band, the text 'Kapp Bro' along with the Hibernia, harp, and 'W' stamps.
peterson-meerschaum-1892.not: This meerschaum pipe was made in 1892, two years after the Kapp brothers and Charles Peterson patented their system; dating relies on the Dublin Assay Office's date-letter chart. The silver band shows both the Peterson name and the parent company Kapp Brothers (the "KAPP BRO" stamp). The P-Lip stem carries a "HAND CUT" stamp, and the box is of the "Kidney" type.

kingsway.tn: A single-letter stamp; the word "Kingsway" appears on the shank.

ashton.tn: A stamp consisting of a solid ring motif.
ashton.not: Surface names include Pebble Grain (dark sandblast), Brindle (brown sandblast), Old Church (light brown sandblast), Pebble Shell (rusticated and sandblasted), Claret (always smooth with a silver band), and Sovereign (smooth, natural). Size codes range from X to XXX; LX denotes very large, ELX huge, Magnum the largest size, and SG an exceptionally grained Sovereign. The number on the stamp gives the number of years elapsed since 1980; for example, 23 corresponds to the year 2003.

rows: Aston, Sovereign, LX, SG (within an oval)

geiger-pipes.tn: Generally no logo on the stem; the left side reads "Geiger" along with a solid symbol enclosed in a circle.
geiger-pipes.not: The pipes are made jointly by Love Geiger (b. 1979) and Sara Geiger. Some examples are stamped with a two-digit number giving the year of production (06 = 2006). The meaning of the circled symbol beneath "Sweden" is unknown.

sasieni-claret.tn: Single blue dot on the stem.
sasieni-claret.not: The stamp belongs to Sasieni's transitional period, 1979-1986.

oppenheimer.not: This is a brand within Oppenheimer Holding and Cadogan Investments Ltd.

corinthian.not: The house brand of Grant's Pipe Shop in San Francisco. The shop previously operated under the name Sutliff; it was bought by Ed Grant in 1953, who retired in 1988 and died in 2003. California's oldest tobacconist passed to Ted Ware and Joe Barron in 2004.

rows: Grant's Pipe Shop, San Francisco Calif

eminent.not: Originally a Danish brand, Eminent later passed to Oldenkott.

luxe.tn: On the left side of the shank, the text 'Luxe Jeantet.'
luxe.not: The 'Jeantet' stamp is struck in a curved line.

special.tn: A stamp with two letters and a diamond motif; "Special" beneath the curved "Comoy's" wording on the left side.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England

knute.tn: The words "Knute Extra, Superior Briar, Italy" on the shank.

lido.tn: A letter logo enclosed in a circle.

rows: Brebbia Lido, Root Briar, Italy [Dwarf figure] 9004

phoenix-american-pipe.tn: On corncob pipes, "Phoenix AM. Pipe Wks" and "Boonville. MO" stamped on the underside; the brand's emblem is a bird motif.
phoenix-american-pipe.not: The factory was located at the corner of 2nd and Vine streets in Boonville, Missouri. Production ended in the mid-1950s.

creative.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries a brand stamp and a date.

mathiss.tn: A triangle motif and the text "Mathiss."

leif.tn: There is no logo; the word "Leif" appears on the underside.
leif.not: A brand of Danish origin; the manufacturer is unknown.

de-la-concha.tn: Animal-figure emblem and "De La Concha" lettering.
de-la-concha.not: The brand's retail location is on 6th Avenue in New York, between 56th and 57th Streets.

rows: De La Concha, London Made, Made in England, 62

sharrow.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; the shank carries the "Sharrow England" stamp.

senator.tn: Brand mark consisting of two letters.
senator.not: Records based on the work of Wilczak and Colwell suggest this label's maker may be Singleton & Cole.

h-t-l.tn: A pipe-shaped logo on the stem.
h-t-l.not: For a similar logo, see Almanac.

harwood-s.tn: A bird-figure logo; the underside bears the text "Harwood's" along with a patent number.
harwood-s.not: The brand belongs to Harwood Brothers Ltd., a pipe manufacturer based in Liverpool. Records include the firm's letterhead dated 1956.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England, 56071

dr-bernard.tn: A letter enclosed in a circle, along with a crown motif.
dr-bernard.not: These two pipes sharing the same name come from different manufacturers. Records link the French example bearing the crown logo to the André Bourgeois workshop in Saint-Claude (see Pipe de Roi).

raffaello.tn: Single-letter emblem and a ring-shaped decoration on the stem; "Raffaello" on the shank.
raffaello.not: The meaning of the letters "AP" is unknown.

manhattan.tn: A two-dot stamp; on the left side, the text 'Manhattan supreme.'
manhattan.not: Records suggest this pipe may be a product of The Manhattan Briar Pipe Co. Sources also mention other British-made 'Manhattan' brands.

colossal.tn: A logo made up of a single letter enclosed in a circle together with an animal figure.

savinelli-sherwood.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter; the left face carries the "Sherwood" stamp and a shape number within a shield mark.
savinelli-sherwood.not: Shape number 623 was also used in Savinelli's Gold and Molinella lines.

three-star.tn: A logo consisting of a star motif.

sasieni-early-one-dot.tn: Single blue dot on the top of the stem, fishtail-style script Sasieni signature on the shank.
sasieni-early-one-dot.not: An example from the pre-transitional period (1919-1924). A single dot appears on the top of the stem.

rows: Sasieni (fishtail-shaped cursive) London Made, PAT. N° 150221/20

savinelli-estella.tn: "Estella" lettering and model number on the shank.

smokewell.tn: A logo made up of a letter within a circle.

schiffsmakler-jurgensen.tn: Brand mark in the shape of a triangle.
schiffsmakler-jurgensen.not: A private label of the Jürgensen ship-broking firm, founded in Flensburg, Germany. The pipe was made in France and distributed as a corporate gift. The firm is noted for having inspired the painter Otto Heinrich Engel (1866-1949).

skagerrak.not: The same anchor logo was also used on the Commodore line.

sun-logo.not: This pipe carries no series-name stamp. The same sun logo is also used on Nicofry-line pipes; a similar logo appears on the Savinelli Molinella.

baroque.tn: A logo consisting of a single letter 'B' on the stem.
baroque.not: The brand appears to come from the same workshop as 'Barok' (Made in England); both pipes share the same shape and the same 'B' logo on the stem.

machiavelli.tn: A single-letter logo used together with a chevron (inverted V) motif.

gardesana.tn: A shield/crest figure on the stem.
gardesana.not: The brand belongs to Gardesana Pipe SNC di Fiorenzo Rovera e C., located in Mairano (Brescia), Italy.

roverart.tn: A single letter in a circle alongside the brand name.
roverart.not: The brand has seven distinct surface finishes: Armony (light walnut), Sinfony (dark mahogany), Ricciolo (carved with curls), Ritmica (rustic with red highlights), Tuba (carved with a bamboo shank), Sax (screw-bowl black rustic), and Cornetta. Annual output is recorded at roughly 500-800 pipes.

comoy-s-golden-arrow.tn: A stamp with the brand name alongside an arrow-shaped motif.
comoy-s-golden-arrow.not: It has not been firmly established that the brand is a Comoy's second line; Comoy's usually marked its second lines with the script prefix "The" (as in The Guildhall, The Everyman, The St James). See also The Golden Arrow.

rows: Made in London [within a circle], England

mac-lintock.tn: A letter logo combining several letters.

remington.tn: No logo on the stem; "Remington" and a "USA 10" mark on the underside.

savinelli-linea-artisan.tn: A stamp featuring the Savinelli coat of arms beside the text 'Linea Artisan' and 'Savinelli Product.'
savinelli-linea-artisan.not: This stamp identifies Savinelli's handmade series.

crable.tn: No separate logo; the underside carries the maker's signature and a date stamp.
crable.not: Joseph Crable carved his first pipe in 1999 and began selling in 2000. In 2006 he stopped making pipes to return to his original profession as a firefighter.

old-england.tn: A logo consisting of a single-colored round dot.

bee-hive-co.tn: The wording 'Bee Hive C°' used with a building-like emblem.
bee-hive-co.not: Records suggest this pipe may originate from a different source than the separately recorded 'Bee Hive' brand.

riff.tn: Star-shaped inlay on the stem; "RIFF" and three stars on the shank.

borgart.tn: A crowned lion figure; on ordinary examples only the initials "LB" and a notice of hand-carving appear.
borgart.not: The brand of the Danish master Leo Borgart (1944-2009). Pipes the maker considered exceptional were marked with the crowned lion stamp.

eug-ropp.not: This stamp carries the signature of Eugène Ropp, a second-generation craftsman of the Ropp family, and is among the brand's early stamps.

aldo-morelli.tn: A multi-letter mark on the stem.
aldo-morelli.not: The pipes were made for Denicotea GmbH in Italy, at either the Barontini or Molina workshops.

partner.tn: A single-letter stamp; "Partner" appears on the right side of the shank.
partner.not: One of F. W. Cole's brands.

nic-out.tn: A rooster standing atop two circles.

sir-percy.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.

chheda.tn: No logo stamp on the stem; large-lettered "Chheda" text and production codes on the shank.
chheda.not: Early-period (2003-2007) pipes have a 14- or 18-carat gold sphere inlay on top of the stem. The letters "BS" and "PC" mark the period Bill Shaloski and Premal Chheda worked together, during which the gold-sphere application was discontinued.

french-made.tn: "Ben Wade" and "Sienna" on the left side, "Made in France" on the right.

twenty-one.tn: "Twenty One" on the left side, a patent number on the right side.
twenty-one.not: One of the Oppenheimer Pipes Ltd. brands. Regarding the number stamp on the stem, see also Tree.

apitz.tn: No logo on the stem; the silver band bears the initials "M. A."
apitz.not: The Michael Apitz brand is marketed by Dan Pipe (Lauenburg, Germany) and is better known for its tobaccos. The pipes are made in Denmark or Germany; nearly all are fitted for a 9 mm filter.

kaywoodie-lady.tn: "Kaywoodie" on the left side, a single-letter "F" stamp on the right side.
kaywoodie-lady.not: Stem color and body finish vary from example to example; records show three distinct variants. Loosening of the decorative stones set into the body is a known flaw of this model. See also White Briar.

lloyds-2.tn: On the left side, 'LLOYDS'; on the right side, the text 'Made in England.'
lloyds-2.not: The brand information relies on Wilczak and Colwell's study.

kaywoodie-filter-plus.tn: A stamp on the underside reading "Kaywoodie", for a model with a gold-colored metal shank.
kaywoodie-filter-plus.not: A model produced with a gold-colored metal shank. Its period is 1955-1959.

paul-viou.tn: A stamp consisting of the brand name on the stem.
paul-viou.not: Pipes under this brand were made by Jacques Craen, and production was continued after 2006 by Sébastien Beaud. The brand was sold by Jacques Craen. See also Genod.

amadeus.tn: A logo depicting an architectural structure; the stamps read 'Amadeus' and 'Akropolis.'
amadeus.not: The brand was founded in 1975 by eight craftsmen coming together.

drucquer-sons.tn: Mammal figure and the brand name lettering.
drucquer-sons.not: Records indicate the shop was located on University Avenue in Berkeley in the late 1980s; by 2009 the address is listed as Albany, California.

rocheleau.tn: Logo in the form of a round wood dot.
rocheleau.not: Maker: John Rocheleau. He gave up pipe making to turn to painting.

darby.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter.

natural-virgin.tn: A single black dot on a white stem.
natural-virgin.not: The black dot is used only on white stems.

starfire.tn: Stamp on the left face consisting of the words "Starfire" and "Dr. Grabow."

cao.tn: An ornamented round inlay on the stem; on meerschaum examples, the maker's signature on the left face.
cao.not: The meerschaum examples were made by master İsmet Bekler, working in Eskişehir. Records indicate that as of 2010, CAO held exclusive US rights to Bekler's pipes.

the-pickwick.tn: The letters "KBB" set within a clover, with "The Pickwick" beside it.
the-pickwick.not: The pipe's unusually long shank is made of two pieces joined by a screw. The stamps aligning exactly across the two pieces show this is not a later repair of a broken shank. For the same design, see Savinelli Long John.

rows: KBB (within a clover), The Pickwick, Algerian Bruyere

marmet.tn: A star-motif logo; the text 'Marmet' on the shank.

supra.tn: "Oldenkott Supra" on the left side; "Bruyere Supra" with two stars between diamond marks on the right side.

sebilo.tn: The letter "S" between two lines with three dots on the right side of the bowl.
sebilo.not: The number of dots on Sébilo pipes, ranging from one to four, indicates the hardness grade of the bog oak used. As the number of dots increases, so does the grain density and heat resistance.

turbo.tn: "Turbo" in large letters on the shank, with the "Oldenkott" brand on the underside.
turbo.not: Turbo is one of Oldenkott's product lines.

holtman.tn: No separate logo; the text "Holtman U.S.A." on the underside.

bruxo.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle on the stem.

rad-davis.tn: "Rad Davis", "Hand Made", "USA", and year stamps between dashes on the underside.
rad-davis.not: Maker Robert "Rad" Davis began making and selling freehand pipes in 2003. Some pipes lack a year stamp; alternate stamps show only "Rad", the country name, and the year.

ultima-thule.tn: The letters "BBB" within a diamond, alongside the words "Ultima Thule."

rows: BBB [within a diamond] Own Make, Ultima Thule

gatlin-burlier.tn: A logo showing the head and shoulders of a man wearing a hat.

holeysmoke.tn: No separate logo; the text "Holeysmoke" on the underside.
holeysmoke.not: See also Custom-Bilt and Tracy Mincer.

karsten-tarp.tn: A stem mark of a single dot and an arrow motif.

rows: KARSTEN TARP (curved) Denmark (within a circle) Hand Made, A

royal-coachman.tn: Stamp in the shape of a coat of arms.
royal-coachman.not: The logo on this example is worn from polishing.

sasieni-four-dot-danzey.tn: "Four Dot" series stamp on the left side, "Danzey" shape name on the right side.
sasieni-four-dot-danzey.not: A Four Dot stamp from the pre-transitional period (1946-1979). "Natural" is the name given to the plain (unsandblasted) finish; the XS stamp denotes pipes in the top price class.

gold-crown.not: On the recorded example the crown logo on the stem is worn, so no comparative identification of the brand could be made.

k-w-co.tn: The words "Brito" and "KW & Co" on the left side.
k-w-co.not: The year letter "O" in the Birmingham assay marks on the silver band corresponds to 1913; the mark belongs to the Birmingham Assay Office.

ivarsson-2.tn: The text ". An Ivarsson . Product" set inside a circle on the underside, with the handwritten initials N I.
ivarsson-2.not: Nana Ivarsson is Lars Ivarsson's second daughter and Sixten Ivarsson's granddaughter; according to 2010 records she produces about 70 pipes a year. The pipes carry the same round stamp as her father's, with the cursive initials "NI" added. The last two digits of the number give the year of production (07 = 2007), while the first two digits give the production order within that year; on early stamps the date is set inside a circle.

totem-star.tn: A mark of one, two, or three dots on the stem; the stamp reads "Totem Star" with a year and serial number.
totem-star.not: The pipes were made by Gunnar Weber-Prada, who worked in Los Angeles, California, around 2009.

logo-r.tn: The letter R within a circle.

john-mackenzie.tn: A diamond-shaped mark on the stem; a brand-name stamp on the underside.

lamy.tn: The brand name itself is used in place of a logo: the words "J LAMY".
lamy.not: The brand bears the name of pipe maker Jean Lamy, whose workshop was in Saint-Claude.

ebenharts.tn: Mark of two, three, or four dots on the stem.
ebenharts.not: The pipes are made by craftsman Ebenhart Botha.

natural-world.tn: An ornate round inlay on the stem.
natural-world.not: The maker of these pipes was Frank Augsberger (1959-1995). He carved pipes between 1978 and 1987, first in Chicago and later in Lombard, Illinois.

rows: Natural World, Hand Made (on the logo)

coat-of-arms.tn: A single letter enclosed in a circle on the stem.
coat-of-arms.not: See also the Coat of Arms record, also listed as a Sasieni sub-brand.

tesch.tn: A stamp containing a single letter along with the brand name.

roermond.not: Records attribute it to the Royal Dutch Pipe Factory. Other brands linked to the same maker: Amphora, Royal Dutch, Humbry, Big Ben.

koziolek.tn: The letters "M K" on the right side, with the word "handmade" below.
koziolek.not: Maker Manfred Koziolek is a retired telecommunications technician. He is one of the few craftsmen who regularly carves pipes from ebony wood; most of his output is fitted for 9mm filters.

the-lumberman.not: The same three-bar logo also appears on the Everyman, Guildhall, and The Mansion House stamps.

rows: Made in London (within a circle) England

ed-s.tn: Letter mark enclosed in a circle on the stem; "Ed's" lettering on the left side of the shank.
ed-s.not: The private label of the Tinderbox pipe shop in Santa Monica, California.

corsaire.tn: Logo consisting of a single letter.

gentleman.tn: Single-letter logo; the left side reads "Parker Gentleman".
gentleman.not: Pipes bearing this name were made by Chacom and Butz Choquin (France) as well as P.M.T. Amadeus (Greece).

epoca.tn: Single-letter logo on the stem; the shank stamp bears a castle emblem containing a two-digit number.
epoca.not: Dating is based on the number stamped inside the castle emblem: the number 46 denotes 1993. Stamps in the Epoca line show the phrases "C.S. Castello" and "Made in Cantu, Italy" together with the Carlo Scotti signature.

rows: (cursive) Carlo Scotti, Made in Cantu, Italy
Carlo Scotti (within an oval), Made in Cantu, Italy

henry-tibb-s.tn: A text stamp struck on the underside of corncob pipes.
henry-tibb-s.not: The China-based brand takes its name from Henry Tibbe (d. 1896), founder of the Missouri Meerschaum Co.

luciano.not: The brand was founded in 2007 by Luca di Piazza (Neatpipes). The designs are by Luca di Piazza, with production generally carried out at the Radice workshop. In 2009 a joint Pease/DiPiazza series began to be designed with American Greg Pease.

captain-comfy.tn: A two-letter stamp; the name "Captain Comfy" and the word "Special" appear on the shank.
captain-comfy.not: The brand of the firm Simon Vuillard & Strauss, working in Saint-Claude, France. The same maker's brands also include Kola, Vuillard, and Windsor. Records mention the Emile Vuillard & Cie factory in a 1910 manufacturers' list.

the-carlyle.tn: A single blue dot on the stem.
the-carlyle.not: The name Carlyle is also recorded as a separate brand.

frabenver.tn: Logo made up of a letter, star, and ring elements enclosed in a circle.
frabenver.not: The name Frabenver is an abbreviation referring to the Benzon brothers of Verona: FRAtelli BENzon VERona. See also Benzon.

arita.tn: A stamp on the underside pairing an ant emblem with the carver's name.
arita.not: Master carver Shizuo Arita (b. 1935) withdrew from commercial production in 1998 but continued making pipes; as of 2009 annual output was about 100 pipes. Grading rises in the order S (sandblasted), T, S, N, A, and AA; AA pipes carry two ant stamps, other grades one. The first two digits of the number give the year of production.

professor.tn: "Professor" on the left side, "London England" on the right side.

parker-of-london.tn: A brand stamp framed in a diamond (rhombus) shape.

parker.tn: The brand name "Parker" on the stamp.

buckingham-palace.not: Records indicate this brand belongs to John Redman Ltd.

monarch.tn: A ring-shaped logo; on the shank, the word "Monarch" between two diamond marks.
monarch.not: The patent application (1935) referenced on the stamp belongs to a pipe with a system where the metal fitting is set inside the shank and the stem is attached by screw. The brand was founded by Fred Warnke in Hartford, Connecticut in the late 1930s, and the company moved to Tulsa, Oklahoma in the 1950s.

butera.tn: A single gold-colored dot on the stem.
butera.not: This pipe was carved in the mid-1980s. In this early period, the maker applied a raised signature to the stem.

leghorn.tn: A text logo formed from the letters of the brand name.
leghorn.not: Leghorn is the traditional English name for the Italian city of Livorno.

skoda.tn: A two-dot logo; an oval "Skoda Pipes" stamp on the underside.
skoda.not: Maker Joe Skoda began making pipes in the spring of 1997. In the four-digit stamp number, the first two digits give the year of production and the rest the production sequence. Higher-grade pipes carry a stamp combining an Alpha or Omega symbol with a Latin letter.

oldenkott.tn: A logo combining crown, chevron, and solid-ring motifs.
oldenkott.not: The Oldenkott factory closed in 1992. For brands from the same circle, see also the Derby and Maxim entries.

haymarket.tn: A logo of a single letter set inside a circle; the text "Haymarket, London Made" on the left face.
haymarket.not: The brand name comes from 62 Haymarket in London, where Emil Loewe established his shop and workshop in 1856. Loewe pipes were made at this address until at least the 1960s.

bruken.tn: The word "Bruken" enclosed in an oval.
bruken.not: A brand based in Aldaya, Valencia, known for its leather-covered pipes. Annual output is recorded at roughly 20,000 pipes. See also ENA, Bamboo Briar.

kaywoodie-leather-wrapped.tn: A leather-wrapped body; the word "Kaywoodie" on the left side of the stem.
kaywoodie-leather-wrapped.not: The stitching pattern of the leather covering differs from that seen on other brands' leather-covered pipes.

rebel.tn: Logo made up of a single letter; shank stamped "Medico, Rebel, Imported Briar".

aaron-beck.tn: A round wood inlay in the stem; "A. Beck, Straight Grain" on the shank.
aaron-beck.not: Maker Aaron Beck (d. 1984) worked more on repairs than on making new pipes. He is known for the unusual inlays he set into his stems.

kaywoodie-campus.tn: The words Kaywoodie and Campus on the shank.
kaywoodie-campus.not: Campus is also found with a white briar surface. Records associate these models with the Drinkless stinger and Synchro Stem patents.

frickert.tn: A Viking helmet on the right side along with "Handcut By Holger" and "Danske Pibe"; no stamp on the stem.
frickert.not: Maker Holger Frickert runs Dan Pipe Cigar & Company in Lauenburg, Germany, together with Heiko Behrens. He began making his own pipes in 1984. See also Holmer Knudsen, Bentley.

l-aiglon.tn: A bird-figure stamp; the words "L'Aiglon, France" on the top face.
l-aiglon.not: Seen on pipes with leather-covered bodies.

linkman-s-2.tn: The text 'Linkman's' on the shank together with bar, star, filled-ring, target, and clover motifs.
linkman-s-2.not: The FIFTY GRAND model was introduced in 1937; its model number always begins with 15.

wengholt.tn: A single-letter logo together with a crown.

rows: Hand Made In Denmark, G. M5
Wengholt, Unique Hand Made In Denmark, 3 [within a circle]

golden-jubilee.tn: A bar-motif logo on the stem; the left side reads "Hardcastle's GOLDEN JUBILEE Super Grain".

billerbeck.not: The maker is Klaus-Dieter Billerbeck, who began making freehand pipes in 1989 after retiring as a police inspector. The number stamped on the shank increases with each new pipe; pipe no. 944 corresponds to October 1998, and no. 999 to November 1999.

savinelli-s-l-e.tn: The text "Savinelli S.L.E." stamped alongside the Savinelli crest.

argyle.tn: A stamp on the shank giving the brand name along with wording identifying the maker.
argyle.not: The same logo is used on the Tally Ho brand.

rows: Argyle London Made, Made by Hardcastle's

connoisseur.tn: Letter-form logo enclosed within a circle.
connoisseur.not: Records indicate it is one of the Hall & Fitzgerald brands. The same name was also used by Lorenzo and Kaywoodie for pipe lines.

muller.tn: On the left side, a windmill depiction placed between "Steffen" and "Müller."
muller.not: Maker Steffen Müller's brand is also known as "The Pipemill," which is where the windmill in the stamp comes from. Müller first exhibited at the Chicago Pipe Show in 2011.

lobbia.tn: A stylized face wearing a hat.
lobbia.not: Grading is indicated by the number of hats struck on the shank. For other logos featuring a hat, see Churchill, London Royal, Man About Town, and Sabatini.

brigham-five-dots.tn: A mark consisting of five dots.

aktas.tn: A meerschaum pipe; the mark consists of the letters of the brand name, with no stamp on the shank.
aktas.not: Kemal Aktaş, founder of Aktaş Meerschaum, died in 2005. As of 2011 the brand is owned by Abdurrezzak Aktaş; the firm is registered in the village of Beyazaltın, Eskişehir.

early-markings.tn: Jeantet stamp written with an ornate letter J.
early-markings.not: In the brand's early stamps, the name was written with an ornate letter J.

rows: Jeantet (ornate J) Bruyere, Preference N°6.P73-1 G.P.

tonni-nielsen.tn: No separate logo mark; the words "Tonni Nielsen" and a grade stamp on the underside.
tonni-nielsen.not: The phrase "In Kentucky" began to be stamped after the maker's arrival in the US, and records indicate it was dropped some years later on an unknown date. Grading rises from 1 to 10, with Drakkar (the Viking grade) at the top. Records indicate annual production of roughly 150 pipes as of about 2010.

rows: On the edge of the bowl

premier.tn: A single red dot on the stem; letters "KBB" set inside a clover leaf on the shank stamp.
premier.not: A brand of Reiss-Premier Corp., which made pipes with Redmanol stems. Its sub-brands are Berkshire, Chester, Fremont, and Pinehurst; see also Devonshire.

wenko.tn: A logo in the form of a mammal figure.
wenko.not: Another brand carrying the same logo and the same rustic surface finish is Arabesque.

old-sea-rock.tn: The words "Castello" and "Old Sea Rock" on the stamp, with the name "Carlo Scotti" enclosed in an oval.

rows: Made In Cantu, Italy, Carlo Scotti (within an oval)

pipex.tn: One or two dots on the stem; the shank reads "Pipex".
pipex.not: The brand's maker is George Stefanou.

kaywoodie-matched-grain.tn: On the left side, the text "Matched Grain" and "Kaywoodie."
kaywoodie-matched-grain.not: Records indicate that "Matched Grain" pipes were also offered in five-piece boxed sets and seven-day sets.

captain-kidd.tn: A two-letter stamp; the words "Captain Kidd" and "London Made" appear on the left face.
captain-kidd.not: Records indicate the brand belonged to A. Frankau & Co, the same firm that also owned the BBB brand.

abbeyhorn.tn: A stamp on the left side reading "Made for Abberhorn Of Kendal".

funambolo.tn: A human figure on the stem.
funambolo.not: The maker, Federico Giorio, does this as a hobby.

bentley-2.tn: A single-letter logo set within a circle.
bentley-2.not: In 2008 annual production stood at around 1,500 pipes. See also Former.

rows: BENTLEY Former's Design, Made in Denmark

apollo.tn: Single-letter logo; "Medico Apollo" on the shank.

bertram.tn: No logo; the left face reads 'Bertram, Washington. D.C.'

savinelli-royal-oak.tn: Logo made up of bars arranged side by side.
savinelli-royal-oak.not: The same bar logo is also used on the Bent Bob's and Kings Cross stamps.

briar-lee.tn: A single dot on the stem.

danish-made-2.tn: Lettered stamp reading "Majestic, Design Series" on the left face and "Ben Wade" on the right face.
danish-made-2.not: Majestic is also recorded as a sub-brand of Ben Wade.

rows: Ben Wade, Hand made in Denmark

penthouse.tn: "Penthouse" on the left side, "London. England" and a shape number on the right side.

thinbite.tn: A single letter within a circle.
thinbite.not: One of the brands within Whitehall Products (USA).

passatore.tn: A decorated round inlay on the stem.

b-s.tn: The letters "B.S" beneath a crowned crest.
b-s.not: Records describe two minotaur-like figures flanking the crowned crest, with an inverted V-shaped band on the shield. No further information on the brand has been established.

week-end.tn: A logo in the form of a solid ring.

broadcaster.tn: A ring motif on the stem.
broadcaster.not: The brand of the Penn Tobacco Company. The pipes were made for Penn by Henry Leonard & Thomas. See also Bruce Peters, Vox Pop, Royalton.

mason-house.tn: The text "Mason House" on the shank; the letters TB within a shield on the silver band.

rows: Mason House, Comfort, 110, Made in London, England

paf.tn: The brand name "PAF" on the left side.

yorkshire.tn: A single dot and a letter-in-circle motif on the stem; the word "Yorkshire" on the body.
yorkshire.not: This is a brand of Sears, Roebuck & Co. Records indicate the pipes were made by Gasparini or by French pipe makers.

rows: Yorshire, Filter de Luxe, Imported Briar, Italy

lord-roger.tn: A single-letter logo on the stem.

fitzgibbon.tn: Single-letter logo; the left side reads "Fitzgibbon, Limerick".

chretin.tn: Two-letter stamp on the stem within a diamond-shaped frame.
chretin.not: The maker of these pipes is Jean Chretin; the stamps mention the name Saint-Claude. Records indicate Enrique's workshop was located within Chretin's factory.

darnell.tn: Single round yellowish dot and a letter-form logo enclosed within a circle.

myon.tn: A letter stamp on the stem for the brand name; "Myon - Broadway" text on the shank.
myon.not: The pipes were made for the lighter brand of the same name. Other lighter brands that also distributed pipes include Flamidor, Ronson, S.T. Dupont, and Silver Match.

bonacquisti.tn: A stamp with the name in block letters and a round stone-shaped mark in the middle.
bonacquisti.not: The name is struck in block letters on the stamp. As of 2010 records, annual output was under a hundred pipes.

rows: Bonacquisti, Sabbia, 11, made by hand, XL (within an oval)

britannia.tn: The word "Britannia" rendered with six three-pronged tridents.
britannia.not: See David Jones Sydney for the same three-pronged trident logo. The brand also has a series called Barrister, not to be confused with the French Barrister brand.

rows: Britannia (underlined with a trident), Made in England
